Rev Judith Akers has sent a joint letter from local churches, including the two on the route, saying the closures will stop worshippers reaching Sunday morning services. Cllr Yvonne Price wants to reply that the date is fixed and the closures are lawful. Which action is MOST LIKELY to reduce the churches' resistance to the event?
o: Ask Cllr Yvonne Price to explain the event's economic and charity benefits in an interview with the local paper.
Send each church a copy of the road closure order and the communication management approach for reference.
Record the joint letter in the risk register and review it again when the safety plan is submitted for approval.
Meet Rev Judith Akers and the church leaders to understand their needs and design crossing points and timings with them.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: Pockets of resistance show where engagement should focus: find out why stakeholders resist rather than sidelining them, and co-create solutions with key influencers so they are adopted (see manual 3.2.2 and 3.4). Rev Akers organized the joint letter, so she is a key influencer for the churches.

n.0: Promoting benefits in the media does not address the churches' specific concern and may harden their position.
n.1: Sending documents informs the churches but does not engage them or address why they object.
n.2: The objection is already happening, so it is an issue to engage with now, not a matter to review later.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Kezia Oduya's stakeholder analysis lists the cabinet, Paceline, the building society, the police, the ambulance service, the traders' association and residents on the route. Zara Quinn points out that the route crosses the main access road to Carrowford Royal Infirmary and passes two churches holding morning services. Is Kezia's stakeholder analysis appropriate, and why?
o: Yes, because the police and ambulance service sit on the safety advisory group, which will consider hospital access.
Yes, because the traders' association and residents already speak for everyone living or working near the route.
No, because the hospital's patients, staff and visitors and the churches' congregations are affected and are missing.
No, because the stakeholder analysis should be written by the communication team once the project is authorized.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: A stakeholder is anyone who can affect, is affected by, or perceives themselves to be affected by the project, and engagement starts by identifying all stakeholders and key influencers, including those with no formal role (see manual 3.2.2). People using the hospital and the church congregations are affected by the closures but have been missed.

n.0: The safety advisory group considers emergency access, but it does not represent patients, visitors or hospital staff, whose concerns differ.
n.1: Residents and traders have their own interests; they do not represent hospital users or church congregations.
n.3: The communication management approach, including stakeholder analysis, is agreed during initiation, before the project is authorized.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the build-up stage. Zara Quinn is recruiting about 1,200 volunteers, most of whom have never helped at a race. To save time, Kezia Oduya proposes emailing each fortnightly highlight report to every volunteer as their main source of information about their roles and race-day arrangements. Is this an appropriate application of the communication management approach, and why?
o: Yes, because sending the same report to everyone keeps the whole project ecosystem equally well informed.
Yes, because a highlight report is issued at regular intervals, which suits a large group of volunteers.
No, because highlight reports are confidential to the project board and should not leave the board.
No, because volunteers need role information through channels and at times that suit them as an audience.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: The communication management approach sets the means and frequency of communication for each stakeholder group, with purpose, channels and messages suited to that audience (see manual 3.4). A board-level stage status report does not tell new volunteers what they need to do; they need targeted role briefings, for example through the volunteering programme.

n.0: Different groups need different messages; one board report does not inform volunteers about their roles.
n.1: Regular timing does not make the content right; highlight reports summarize stage status for the board.
n.2: Highlight reports can go to other stakeholders where useful; the problem is that this one does not meet volunteers' needs.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Kezia Oduya is drafting the communication management approach and writes this entry: 'Residents on the route: affected for five hours on race day; active on social media; individually low influence but able to create media pressure through residents' groups.' Under which heading of the communication management approach should this entry be recorded?
o: Stakeholder analysis
Communications schedule and procedures
Supporting tools and techniques
Resources
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: Stakeholder analysis identifies who is affected by the project's outcome or delivery and who can influence its success or failure (communication management approach contents, manual 3.4). The entry describes how residents are affected and how much influence they have.

n.1: The schedule and procedures set out what will be communicated to each group, how often and through which channels; the entry gives none of this.
n.2: Supporting tools and techniques are things such as communication platforms or analytics tools, not an assessment of a stakeholder group.
n.3: Resources are the people and budget for communication activities, not a description of a stakeholder group.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is at the end of the foundations stage. The cloud provider has raised its prices, and Mairi Campbell's updated forecast cuts the yearly running cost saving from £1.4 million to £1.1 million, which is still within the benefits tolerance. Before the board decides whether to authorize the wave migration stage, Fraser McIntyre asks Mairi to re-test the options, including keeping some applications at the Falkirk site, against the updated costs, risks and benefits. How well does this apply the 'ensure continued business justification' principle, and why?
o: It applies it well, because the senior user is accountable for the business case and has to approve the revised saving.
It applies it well, because the justification is revalidated against the latest forecasts before the board commits to the next stage.
It applies it poorly, because a fall in forecast benefits should be escalated to the business layer in an exception report.
It applies it poorly, because the society's board approved the cloud strategy, so the options should stay closed during the project.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: The principle requires the justification to remain valid and to be revalidated throughout the project, using the latest costs, risks and benefits; the board checks it at each stage boundary before committing to the next stage (see manual 2.1 and 5.3.1, the 'check' step). Re-testing the options when forecasts change is exactly this.

n.0: The executive, Fraser McIntyre, is accountable for the business case; the senior user specifies the benefits and demonstrates that forecast benefits are on track (see manual 6.2.4.2).
n.2: The reduced saving is within the benefits tolerance, so there is no exception; changes to benefits forecasts are handled when the business case is updated at the stage boundary.
n.3: Approval of a strategy does not fix the project's justification; it must be revalidated throughout, and a cheaper or better option may emerge as costs change.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is in the foundations stage. During the pilot wave, Arjun Menon's team finds that three applications failed their first switch-over because server addresses had been written into their code. Mairi Campbell records this in the lessons log, holds a short session in which the Pune engineers explain the problem to the Edinburgh team and to Hugh Bannerman's operations staff, and adds an address check to the migration checklist for wave 1. How well does this apply the 'learn from experience' principle, and why?
o: It applies it well, because the lesson is recorded, shared across the teams and acted on while the project is still running.
It applies it well, because a lessons report has to be issued to the project board after each migration wave is complete.
It applies it poorly, because lessons should be gathered at the end of the project so that they can be passed on in a lessons report.
It applies it poorly, because a failed switch-over should be raised as an issue rather than recorded and shared as a lesson.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: Learning from experience means seeking, recording and acting on lessons throughout the project, not only at the start and end, and sharing them in ways that suit different people (see manual 2.2). Recording the lesson, sharing it across the three locations and changing the checklist before wave 1 does this well.

n.1: A lessons report can be produced when useful, but there is no requirement for one after every wave; the reason does not explain why this is good practice.
n.2: Lessons are sought, recorded and acted on throughout the project; waiting until closure would lose the benefit for the later waves.
n.3: Handling the failures as issues and learning from them are not alternatives; recording and sharing the lesson is a good application of the principle.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is in the foundations stage. Mairi Campbell finds that the Stratoshift engineers in Pune are taking requests directly from Steven Clarke, from Hugh Bannerman's operations staff and from Mairi herself, and their priorities are clashing. She agrees with Lena Fischer that Arjun Menon will be team manager for all migration work, records this in the role descriptions, and sets up a weekly joint call so that the Pune engineers get to know the operations staff they hand applications to. Which principle is being applied, and why?
o: Define roles, responsibilities and relationships, because she clarifies who directs the work and builds links between the teams.
Manage by exception, because Arjun Menon can now make decisions within the tolerances set for his work packages.
Focus on products, because the joint call will help the operations staff to accept the migrated applications at handover.
Tailor to suit the project, because the team manager role is being adapted for a supplier based in another country.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: The principle calls for agreed roles and responsibilities so that people know what is expected of them, and for the project management team to build relationships with and between internal and external stakeholders (see manual 2.3). Naming one team manager and creating a regular link between Pune and the operations staff applies both parts.

n.1: Nothing is said about tolerances or escalation; the problem being solved is unclear direction and weak relationships.
n.2: The call is set up so that the teams get to know each other, not to define or co-create products; the main action is clarifying who directs the work.
n.3: The team manager role is used as PRINCE2 describes it; nothing about the method is being adapted to the project.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. To reduce the number of board decision points, Fraser McIntyre proposes merging the wave migration stage and the core banking stage into one stage of 11 months. Moving core banking is the riskiest part of the project, and when it can start depends on the results of the earlier migration waves. How well does this apply the 'manage by stages' principle, and why?
o: It applies it well, because longer stages reduce the burden that the project places on the members of the board.
It applies it well, because the board can still control the project through the tolerances set for the longer stage.
It applies it poorly, because each stage of a PRINCE2 project should be of a similar length to the others.
It applies it poorly, because the board would lose a decision point to review viability before the riskiest work begins.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: Stages give the board review and decision points at which to assess viability; shorter stages give more control and stage length should reflect risk and complexity (see manual 2.4). Removing the boundary before the core banking move takes away the decision point at the most critical moment, so the principle is applied poorly.

n.0: It is true that longer stages reduce the burden on senior managers, but this does not justify losing control at the project's riskiest point.
n.1: Tolerances support manage by exception; they do not replace the stage boundary at which the board decides whether to commit to the core banking move.
n.2: Stages can be of different lengths; their number and length depend on risk, complexity and decision points, not on matching each other.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Mindful of the board's very low appetite for outages, Fraser McIntyre proposes that the project board meets each month to approve the switch-over date of every application due to move in the following month, instead of setting tolerances for the stage and leaving the dates to Mairi Campbell. How well does this apply the 'manage by exception' principle, and why?
o: It applies it well, because a very low risk appetite means the board should take the day-to-day decisions on migrations.
It applies it well, because monthly meetings give the board regular, time-driven control over progress in the stage.
It applies it poorly, because the board should delegate within tolerances and be told when they are forecast to be exceeded.
It applies it poorly, because switch-over dates for individual applications should be approved by the business layer.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: Manage by exception sets limits of delegated authority through tolerances; the board delegates day-to-day decisions to the project manager and is alerted when a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded, which saves senior time without removing control (see manual 2.5). The low appetite should be reflected in tight risk tolerances, not in the board approving every date.

n.0: Risk appetite shapes the tolerances the board sets; it does not mean the board should take over day-to-day management from the project manager.
n.1: Time-driven reporting such as highlight reports is useful, but approving each date is day-to-day management, not control by exception.
n.3: The business layer sets project tolerances and decides on project-level exceptions; it does not approve individual switch-over dates.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Aileen Docherty asks Arjun Menon's engineers to build parts of her proposed data platform while they are migrating the finance applications, saying it will be cheaper to do it now. The data platform is not one of the products in the approved plans and it has no product description. How well does this apply the 'focus on products' principle, and why?
o: It applies it well, because doing related work during a migration reduces the total cost of change to the society.
It applies it well, because the chief information officer can approve changes to the scope of the work packages.
It applies it poorly, because the team would be doing work that is not needed to deliver the project's agreed products.
It applies it poorly, because the data platform should have been added to the project product description in initiation.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: Focus on products means the project does no more work than is needed to deliver its agreed products, which are defined by product descriptions; this controls scope creep (see manual 2.6). Building an unplanned, undefined product is work outside the agreed scope, so the principle is applied poorly.

n.0: Possible savings do not make unplanned work acceptable; the project should deliver its agreed products and nothing more.
n.1: Being chief information officer gives Aileen Docherty no authority over the project's agreed scope; changes to baselined products go through issue and change control.
n.3: The data platform has not been approved as part of the project, so there is no reason it should have been in the project product description; any addition should go through change control.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell proposes highlight reports every two weeks during the foundations, wave migration and core banking stages, and monthly during decommissioning, using the society's standard change portfolio template. One report each month will also serve as the written update the audit committee wants. The project board agrees, and the arrangement is recorded in the PID. How well does this apply the 'tailor to suit the project' principle, and why?
o: It applies it well, because frequent highlight reports can take the place of end stage reports at stage boundaries.
It applies it well, because report frequency and format are matched to each stage's risk and to the society's governance.
It applies it poorly, because the format of highlight reports is set by PRINCE2 and should not be adapted.
It applies it poorly, because reports to the audit committee should be exception reports sent by the executive.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: Tailoring makes project controls fit the project's scale, risk and environment, for example the frequency and formality of reports, and aligns the method with the business's own processes; tailoring decisions are documented and agreed in the PID (see manual 2.7). Reporting more often in the riskier stages and reusing the society's template is proportionate tailoring.

n.0: End stage reports support the board's decision at each stage boundary; highlight reports do not replace them, however often they are produced.
n.2: Management products may be adapted in format, merged or renamed; using the society's template is a normal tailoring choice.
n.3: Exception reports are for forecast breaches of tolerance and go to the project board; a regular update to the audit committee is a communication arrangement.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is in the foundations stage. The Pune engineers and Hugh Bannerman's operations staff have never met, and handovers of the pilot applications are causing friction and blame. Mairi Campbell arranges for Arjun Menon and two of his engineers to spend the first two weeks of the pilot wave in Falkirk, working alongside the operations staff, and sets up a short daily call in the hours when both countries are at work. Is this an appropriate approach to leading the team, and why?
o: Yes, because working side by side removes the need for checkpoint reports from the Pune team during the pilot.
Yes, because a team split across sites needs deliberate contact to build trust and social cohesion between its parts.
No, because team building is a matter for each supplier's own line managers rather than for the project manager.
No, because the Stratoshift engineers should be managed through the framework contract rather than by the project.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: Virtual, remote and hybrid teams do not share information naturally, so the project should deliberately build social cohesion and trust across silos, for example through synchronized co-location days for key people and regular purposeful contact (see manual 3.3.3). Bringing key engineers to Falkirk and setting a shared daily call does this.

n.0: Checkpoint reports are still needed to report work package progress; co-location improves relationships but does not replace reporting.
n.2: Building an effective team is part of leading the project team; the project manager should act when friction between parts of the team harms the work.
n.3: The contract sets the commercial terms, but the engineers are still part of the project team and need to work well with the society's staff.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Few of Brennan Mutual's IT staff have cloud skills, yet the society will run the new environment after the project closes. To save time, Mairi Campbell proposes that Stratoshift engineers write all the cloud operating procedures and run the migrated applications until closure, with cloud training for the operations staff arranged by the IT department after the project ends. Is this an appropriate approach to building the team's capability, and why?
o: Yes, because in a thin client delivery model the supplier carries out most of the work on the project.
Yes, because training staff for business as usual falls outside the scope of a PRINCE2 project.
No, because the capability gap should be closed during the project, for example by upskilling the operations staff.
No, because the senior supplier should write the operating procedures personally as a member of the board.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: Leading successful teams includes understanding competencies and capabilities, identifying gaps and closing them, for example by upskilling or shifting responsibilities (see manual 3.3.2). The operations staff will run the new environment, so their skills gap should be addressed while the project is running, not left until it has closed.

n.0: A thin client model describes who does the work, but it does not remove the need for the society's own staff to be able to run the products after handover.
n.1: Preparing people to use and support the project's products is part of transition and of leading the team; enabling activities such as training belong in the project.
n.3: The senior supplier commits supplier resources and is accountable for the quality of supplier products; writing procedures is team work, and it would not close the society's skills gap.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is in the foundations stage. Ross Leckie, who is respected by the operations staff, has told colleagues that the promise of retraining will not be kept, and two engineers have asked about redundancy terms. Hugh Bannerman suggests leaving Ross out of the project's briefings and design workshops so that his doubts do not spread any further. Is this an appropriate way to lead the change, and why?
o: Yes, because Ross Leckie holds no formal role in the project management team for Project Skyline.
Yes, because resistance from staff should be handled by the society's HR team rather than by the project.
No, because Ross Leckie should be appointed as a senior user so that he represents the operations staff.
No, because Ross Leckie is a key influencer whose concerns should be explored and who should be involved.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: Leading change means identifying stakeholders and key influencers, including people with no formal role, and treating pockets of resistance as a sign of where to engage: find out why people resist and involve them, for example through co-creation (see manual 3.2.2 and 3.4). Excluding the informal leader would deepen mistrust.

n.0: Projects must involve key people who are affected or critical to success even when they hold no formal role.
n.1: HR support may help, but the project is responsible for engaging the people affected by its change.
n.2: Engaging Ross does not require a board role; the senior user represents the users and must have the authority to commit them, which Ross does not have.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell drafts the change management approach. It describes how the IT operations function should look once both data centres have closed, and states that retraining for the operations staff will begin after decommissioning is complete. How well does this apply the guidance on leading successful change, and why?
o: It applies it well, because change management controls changes to the products in the project's baseline.
It applies it well, because the target state is the part of the approach that the board approves in the PID.
It applies it poorly, because retraining should be recorded as a risk in the risk register instead of in an approach.
It applies it poorly, because it should plan the move through interim states, with enabling activities before, during and after.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: The change management approach sets out the target organizational state and how the business will move from the current state through any interim states, with enabling activities such as training before, during and after transition (see manual 3.2.1). As the data centre roles shrink wave by wave, retraining that starts after decommissioning comes too late.

n.0: In PRINCE2 7 change management is the organizational transition from current to target state; controlling changes to baselines belongs to the issues practice.
n.1: The whole approach is approved as part of the PID; describing only the end state leaves out how people will get there.
n.2: Concerns about retraining may give rise to risks, but planning the retraining itself is an enabling activity in the change management approach.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is in the foundations stage. Mairi Campbell's stakeholder analysis lists the project board, the IT department and Stratoshift. Joanne Pettigrew points out that the first switch-over weekends will affect branch staff, the contact centre and members who use online banking, and none of them have been told. What should Mairi do to apply the communication approach?
o: Add branch, contact centre and online banking users to the stakeholder analysis and plan messages for each before switch-overs.
Ask the audit committee to approve each message about the switch-over weekends before it is sent to staff and members.
Report the switch-over dates in the next highlight report so that the board members can brief their own teams.
Wait until the end of the foundations stage and add the affected groups when the approaches are reviewed.
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: The communication management approach should identify everyone affected by the project or its delivery, and set out the purpose, timing, channels and messages for each group, so that communication is planned and two-way across the project ecosystem (see manual 3.4). Branch staff, the contact centre and members are affected by switch-overs and need planned communication before they happen.

n.1: The audit committee receives a monthly update; it has no role in approving operational messages to staff and members.
n.2: Highlight reports keep the board informed of stage status; they are not the way to communicate with affected staff and members.
n.3: The switch-over weekends are imminent; a gap in the stakeholder analysis should be fixed now rather than left to a later review.

Practitioner: Principles & People.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell is writing the communication management approach. She records that a shared collaboration platform, with a channel for each migration wave and recorded daily stand-ups, will be used between Pune, Edinburgh and Falkirk. Under which heading of the communication management approach should this be recorded?
o: Stakeholder analysis
Communications schedule and procedures
Supporting tools and techniques
Resources
Practitioner: Principles & People.w: The supporting tools and techniques heading records the platforms and tools used to communicate, such as collaboration platforms and analytics or automation tools (see manual 3.4). A shared collaboration platform is a tool.

n.0: Stakeholder analysis identifies who is affected by or can influence the project, not the tools used to reach them.
n.1: The schedule and procedures set out the purpose, frequency, channels and messages for each stakeholder group, not the platform itself.
n.3: Resources are the people and budget for communication activities; a collaboration platform is a tool, not a resource.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Hannah Okoro is preparing the full business case for Permits Online. Which heading of the business case should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 1 of 3: The project will run for 44 weeks from the start of initiation, and its benefits will be realized over the two years after launch.
o: Reasons
Expected benefits
Time
Costs
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The time heading records the period over which the project runs and the period over which its benefits are expected to be realized (business case composition, manual chapter 5).

n.0: Reasons explain why the project is needed and how it supports business objectives, not how long the project and its benefits will take.
n.1: Expected benefits states the measurable improvements themselves; when they will be realized is recorded under time.
n.3: Costs covers project costs and ongoing running costs with their funding, not durations.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Hannah Okoro is preparing the full business case for Permits Online. Which heading of the business case should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: Support for the current permit database ends on 31 October next year, and the corporate plan commits the council to services that are digital by preference.
o: Reasons
Expected benefits
Time
Costs
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The reasons heading explains why the project is needed and how it enables the organization's business objectives, here the end of support and the corporate plan's digital commitment (business case composition, manual chapter 5).

n.1: These are the drivers for the project, not measurable improvements that it will produce.
n.2: No duration or period of benefits realization is given; these explain why the project is needed.
n.3: No cost or funding information is given.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Hannah Okoro is preparing the full business case for Permits Online. Which heading of the business case should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: Kestrel Lane will charge £48,000 a year to host and support the live service, funded from the parking services budget.
o: Reasons
Expected benefits
Time
Costs
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The costs heading includes ongoing operations and maintenance costs as well as project costs, together with how they will be funded (business case composition, manual chapter 5).

n.0: A running charge is not a reason for undertaking the project.
n.1: A charge is a cost of the investment, not an improvement it delivers.
n.2: The yearly charge is a cost of running the product; the time heading records the duration of the project and of benefits realization.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). The project management team for Permits Online is being appointed. Using the additional information about the people, which individual would be most appropriate for each role? Statement 1 of 3: Executive.
o: Graham Pell
Ruth Abernethy
Siobhan Kerr
Priya Lal
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Graham Pell is the budget holder for parking services and is named in the mandate as accountable for Permits Online. The executive is the single point of accountability for the project, secures its funding and owns the business case (manual 6.2.4 and appendix B).

n.1: Ruth Abernethy runs the service that will use the products, which suits the senior user role; she does not hold the budget or the accountability named in the mandate.
n.2: Siobhan Kerr leads the supplier and represents its interests, which suits the senior supplier role; the executive represents the council's business interest.
n.3: Priya Lal has no role in parking services and no budget; her independent review role suits assurance.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). The project management team for Permits Online is being appointed. Using the additional information about the people, which individual would be most appropriate for each role? Statement 2 of 3: Senior supplier.
o: Graham Pell
Ruth Abernethy
Siobhan Kerr
Priya Lal
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Siobhan Kerr is Kestrel Lane's delivery director, accountable for the agency's staff, its contract and the technical quality of what it builds. The senior supplier represents those delivering the products, commits supplier resources and is accountable for the quality of the supplier's products (manual 6.2.4).

n.0: Graham Pell is best placed as executive, holding the budget and named as accountable; he does not lead the organization delivering the products.
n.1: Ruth Abernethy runs the service that will use the products, so she represents users rather than suppliers.
n.3: Priya Lal reviews digital projects for the council; she does not lead the supplier or commit its staff.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). The project management team for Permits Online is being appointed. Using the additional information about the people, which individual would be most appropriate for each role? Statement 3 of 3: Project assurance, carried out by someone the board appoints to review the project on its behalf.
o: Graham Pell
Ruth Abernethy
Siobhan Kerr
Priya Lal
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Project assurance must be independent of the project manager and is carried out for the board. Priya Lal already reviews digital projects against the council's service standard and has no role in parking services, so she can give the board an independent view (manual 6.2.4).

n.0: Graham Pell is best suited to be the executive, a board member, rather than someone the board appoints to assure the project for it.
n.1: Ruth Abernethy runs the service that the project changes and is best suited to be the senior user, a board member.
n.2: Siobhan Kerr is accountable for Kestrel Lane's delivery and suits the senior supplier role; she cannot give an independent view of her own agency's work.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Which role should carry out each of these planning actions on Permits Online? Statement 1 of 3: Set the tolerances for the project as a whole and document them in the project mandate.
o: Executive
Business layer
Team manager
Project manager
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The business layer provides the planning standards and sets project tolerances, documenting them in the project mandate (plans roles, manual table 7.1). For Permits Online this is the chief executive's office.

n.0: The executive defines tolerances for each stage; project-level tolerances come from the business layer.
n.2: Team managers work within work package tolerances; they do not set project tolerances.
n.3: The project manager works within project tolerances set from above and sets work package tolerances.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Which role should carry out each of these planning actions on Permits Online? Statement 2 of 3: Define the tolerances for the private beta stage and approve the private beta stage plan.
o: Executive
Business layer
Team manager
Project manager
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The executive defines the tolerances for each stage and approves stage plans (plans roles, manual table 7.1).

n.1: The business layer sets project tolerances, not stage tolerances, and does not approve stage plans.
n.2: Team managers prepare schedules and team plans for their work packages; they do not set stage tolerances.
n.3: The project manager prepares the stage plan but neither approves it nor sets its tolerances.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Which role should carry out each of these planning actions on Permits Online? Statement 3 of 3: Prepare the schedule for the work package that builds the automatic eligibility checks.
o: Executive
Business layer
Team manager
Project manager
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Team managers prepare the schedules for each work package they take on, and team plans where needed (plans roles, manual table 7.1).

n.0: The executive approves stage plans and sets stage tolerances; work package schedules are below that level.
n.1: The business layer provides planning standards; it does not schedule work packages.
n.3: The project manager prepares the work package description; the schedule for the work package is prepared by the team manager.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). Hannah Okoro is updating the quality register entry for the accessibility check on the online application form. Which heading of the quality register should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 1 of 3: Each screen tested by a panel of residents who use screen readers, followed by an automated WCAG 2.2 AA scan.
o: Quality method
Planned and actual dates
Responsibilities
Result
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The quality method heading records how the product is checked, for example testing or inspection (quality register composition, manual chapter 8).

n.1: No dates are given; this describes how the check is carried out.
n.2: No reviewer or approver is named; this describes the method of checking.
n.3: No outcome is recorded; this is the method, not whether the form passed.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). Hannah Okoro is updating the quality register entry for the accessibility check on the online application form. Which heading of the quality register should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: A tester from Tom Achebe's team carried out the check, and Ruth Abernethy approved the form.
o: Quality method
Planned and actual dates
Responsibilities
Result
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The responsibilities heading records who carried out, reviewed and approved the quality activity (quality register composition, manual chapter 8).

n.0: This names people and their part in the check, not the method used.
n.1: No planned or actual dates are given.
n.3: No pass or fail outcome is given; this records who was involved.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). Hannah Okoro is updating the quality register entry for the accessibility check on the online application form. Which heading of the quality register should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: Failed on two screens that could not be completed using a keyboard; the form will be fixed and checked again.
o: Quality method
Planned and actual dates
Responsibilities
Result
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The result heading records the outcome of the quality activity, typically pass or fail, and what will happen after a failure, such as a repeat check (quality register composition, manual 8.2.2).

n.0: This is the outcome of the check, not the method used to carry it out.
n.1: A repeat check is mentioned, but no planned or actual dates are given; the entry records the outcome.
n.2: No reviewer or approver is named; the entry records the outcome and the follow-up.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Permits Online is in the 'starting up a project' process. In the outline business case Hannah Okoro analyses one option, the full online service. She does not assess carrying on as now or replacing only the permit database, saying the mandate has already chosen the online service. Is this an appropriate application of the business case practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the outline business case in starting up is high level and is refined into the full business case in initiation.
Yes, because the mandate from the chief executive's office has already named the online service as the solution.
No, because a project that the council has to undertake should choose the do-minimum option to keep costs down.
No, because carrying on as now should be assessed as the baseline for measuring the benefits of the other options.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The business case technique compares business options, starting with doing nothing differently, which is the baseline for quantifying the others, then doing the minimum and doing more than the minimum; the difference between them is what the investment buys (see manual 5.3.1). Without that baseline the board cannot judge whether the online service is the best value.

n.0: The outline business case is high level, but it still needs enough options analysis to show that the project is worth initiating.
n.1: A mandate triggers starting up; it does not remove the need to justify the chosen option, even for an unavoidable project (manual 2.1).
n.2: Justification means choosing the option of best overall value, which may or may not be the do-minimum option.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Permits Online is nearing the end of the private beta stage. Online take-up in the Old Town ward is 35%, against the 70% assumed in the business case, so forecast savings are lower. Hannah Okoro updates the business case with actual costs, the take-up data and revised benefit forecasts, and the board reviews whether the project is still worth continuing before deciding on the public beta. Is this an effective way to apply the business case practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the senior user is accountable for the business case and should present the revised forecasts.
Yes, because the business case is maintained at each stage end so the board can check it is still justified.
No, because benefits are confirmed after closure, so the board should not act on forecasts from a beta.
No, because project assurance, not the project manager, should update the benefit forecasts in the business case.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: At the end of each stage the project manager maintains the business case with actual progress and the latest forecasts, and the board checks whether the project is still desirable, viable and achievable before authorizing the next stage (see manual 5.3.1). Falling take-up is exactly the evidence that check needs.

n.0: The executive, not the senior user, is accountable for the business case; the senior user specifies the benefits and shows they are on track.
n.2: Benefits are mostly confirmed after closure, but forecasts must be checked at each stage boundary so the board can decide whether to continue.
n.3: Project assurance monitors the business case for the board; the project manager prepares and maintains it on the executive's behalf.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Permits Online is in the 'initiating a project' process. Before designing the project team structure, Hannah Okoro maps how the council makes decisions that will affect the project: cabinet approval for permit fee changes, consultation with the trade union and HR on job changes, and the ICT change board for integration work. Is this an appropriate application of the organizing practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the business layer must approve the project team structure before the initiation stage can start.
Yes, because the council's existing structures and approvals are understood before the project ecosystem is designed.
No, because mapping the council's governance is a task for the business layer rather than the project manager.
No, because the project ecosystem should be designed first and the council's structures then fitted around it.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The organizational design and development technique begins by understanding the organizational ecosystem: its existing structures, governance, the decisions that need business approval and its people management policies. Designing the project ecosystem follows (see manual 6.3.1).

n.0: The project management team is appointed in starting up, by the executive with the business layer accountable; that does not explain why mapping governance is useful here.
n.2: The business layer provides the mandate and appoints the executive; understanding the ecosystem in order to design the project's organization is part of the project's own organizing work.
n.3: The technique works the other way round: the existing ecosystem is understood first so that the project ecosystem fits it.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Permits Online is in the 'initiating a project' process. The PMO's second officer will provide project support, maintaining the registers and planning tools. To save staff time, Graham Pell proposes that the same officer also carries out business assurance for him, as she already knows the project's documents well. Is this an effective way to apply the organizing practice, and why?
o: Yes, because board members may delegate their assurance work to someone in the business.
Yes, because the PMO already holds the council's project templates and its portfolio list.
No, because project assurance should be carried out by a firm from outside the council.
No, because project support and project assurance must be kept as separate roles.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Project assurance is the board's responsibility and must be independent of the project manager; it cannot be given to project support, and the two roles must be kept separate (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B). The officer would be assuring work she maintains for the project manager.

n.0: Delegating assurance is allowed, but not to the person providing project support.
n.1: Familiarity with the templates does not make the support officer independent of the project manager.
n.2: Assurance can be carried out by board members, by people from the business or by external parties; an outside firm is not required.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Permits Online is in the 'initiating a project' process. Before estimating anything, Hannah Okoro and Tom Achebe list the products needed: the online application, eligibility checks, council tax integration, migrated permit records, the telephone assisted route and staff guidance. They then draw how each depends on the others, showing that the integration depends on Alan Briggs's ICT team. Is this an appropriate application of the plans practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the products are identified and their dependencies mapped before estimates and a schedule are prepared.
Yes, because the product flow diagram can be used in place of a schedule for a supplier working in sprints.
No, because a supplier using Scrum plans its work in sprints and should not be asked to define products first.
No, because the product breakdown is prepared by the team manager in the 'managing product delivery' process.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Product-based planning starts by defining and analysing the products (project product description, product breakdown structure, product descriptions and product flow diagram), then organizes work packages, prepares estimates and schedules them (see manual 7.3.1). The flow diagram also exposes the dependency on the ICT team.

n.1: The product flow diagram shows sequence and dependencies; a schedule is still prepared to show timing and durations.
n.2: Iterative delivery uses a product backlog, but products are still defined; planning is product-based whatever the delivery approach.
n.3: Product-based planning for the project plan is led by the project manager in initiation; team managers plan their own work packages.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Permits Online must be live, with all permits migrated, before 31 October, when support for the old database ends. The leadership team will accept some risk to speed but very little to data and accessibility. Hannah Okoro recommends, and the chief executive's office agrees, no time tolerance on the go-live date and a scope tolerance that lets online applications for business permits follow after launch. Is this an effective way to apply the plans practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the project manager is responsible for setting the tolerances for the project as a whole.
Yes, because knowing which constraints take precedence shows where tolerance can be given and where it cannot.
No, because tolerances should be set for every aspect of performance using the same percentage range.
No, because scope tolerance is set in work package descriptions and not at the level of the project plan.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Using tolerances to manage constraints depends on understanding which constraints take precedence (see manual 7.2.4). With a date that cannot move, flexibility is placed in scope instead. Project tolerances are set by the business layer, here on Hannah's recommendation.

n.0: Project tolerances are set by the business layer, here the chief executive's office; the project manager recommends but does not set them.
n.2: Tolerances are set per aspect to reflect the project's constraints and priorities; there is no rule of a common range.
n.3: Tolerances exist at each level of plan, so scope tolerance can be set for the project plan as well as for stages and work packages.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Permits Online is in the 'starting up a project' process. While Hannah Okoro drafts the project product description, Ruth Abernethy asks for 'permit calls to the contact centre halved within a year of launch' to be an acceptance criterion. Hannah records it as an expected benefit instead, and lists meeting WCAG 2.2 AA, passing the independent accessibility audit and passing the IT health check as acceptance criteria. Is this appropriate, and why?
o: Yes, because acceptance criteria are set by the project manager, who decides what the users will accept.
Yes, because acceptance criteria must be met before the product is accepted, and halving calls is a later benefit.
No, because the senior user specifies the benefits and so decides what the acceptance criteria will be.
No, because every acceptance criterion should be linked to a benefit that can be measured after launch.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Acceptance criteria are a prioritized list of measurable criteria that the project product must meet before the users will accept it, recorded in the project product description (see manual 8.1.1). Halving calls is a benefit realized after launch; it belongs in the business case and the benefits management approach.

n.0: The project manager documents acceptance criteria but agrees them with the users; it is the users, not the project manager, who accept the product.
n.2: The senior user provides quality expectations and acceptance criteria, but a benefit realized a year after launch cannot be a condition of accepting the product.
n.3: Acceptance criteria must be met at acceptance; a benefit measured after launch cannot be tested at that point.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Permits Online is in the discovery and alpha stage. Kestrel Lane runs accessibility and usability tests in every sprint and keeps the results in its own tool, which council staff cannot see. Hannah Okoro has no record of which products have passed their quality checks. At the end of the stage the board asks for evidence that quality control has been carried out. Is this an effective way to apply the quality practice, and why?
o: Yes, because quality control is carried out by the team, and the supplier's records are its own concern.
Yes, because Kestrel Lane uses Scrum, and agile teams can tailor out quality records for the project.
No, because a quality register should show the quality activities planned and done, so progress can be reviewed.
No, because test results should be recorded in the risk register so that failures can be managed as risks.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Quality control results are recorded in the quality register, which summarizes all quality activities planned or performed and is used by the project manager and project assurance to review progress (see manual 8.2.2). The supplier's tool could serve as that record if the project could see it, but here no usable record exists.

n.0: The team performs the quality checks, but the results must be visible to the project so that the project manager, board and assurance can rely on them.
n.1: Tailoring can change the form of the record, but not remove the need for evidence that quality control has been done.
n.3: Failed tests are recorded in the quality register and, where needed, raised as issues; the risk register holds uncertain future events.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Which management product, or heading of the business case, should each piece of information be recorded in? Statement 1 of 3: Sunita Rao's team will count apprentice enrolments each September for three years after opening and report the figures at planned benefits reviews.
o: Business case: expected benefits
Benefits management approach
Business case: costs
Sustainability management approach
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The benefits management approach defines the benefits management actions and benefits reviews, including how and when benefits are measured and who is responsible, so that realization can be confirmed after the project (manual 5.5 and 5.3.1).

n.0: The expected benefits heading states the measurable benefits themselves; the measurement actions, timing and reviews belong in the benefits management approach.
n.2: No cost is described; this is how and when a benefit will be measured and reviewed.
n.3: Apprentice numbers are a benefit measure, not a sustainability performance target.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Which management product, or heading of the business case, should each piece of information be recorded in? Statement 2 of 3: The heat pumps and solar panels will add £38,000 a year to the centre's running and maintenance costs, met from the estates budget.
o: Business case: expected benefits
Benefits management approach
Business case: costs
Sustainability management approach
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The costs heading of the business case covers project costs and the ongoing operations and maintenance costs of the products, with their funding arrangements (business case composition, manual chapter 5).

n.0: This is a cost of owning the products, not an improvement they bring.
n.1: A running cost is not a benefits management action or review.
n.3: The sustainability management approach sets the actions, reviews and controls for sustainability targets; the running cost of the equipment and its funding belong under costs.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Which management product, or heading of the business case, should each piece of information be recorded in? Statement 3 of 3: Construction waste diverted from landfill will be checked monthly from the contractor's waste records, with a tolerance of two percentage points below the 90% target.
o: Business case: expected benefits
Benefits management approach
Business case: costs
Sustainability management approach
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Sustainability performance targets and tolerances are documented in the sustainability management approach, which defines the actions, reviews and controls needed to achieve them (manual 5.2.2).

n.0: Diverting waste is a sustainability target for the work, not an expected benefit of the centre.
n.1: Waste diversion is a sustainability target, not one of the project's benefits; its tolerance and checks belong in the sustainability management approach.
n.2: No cost is described; this is a target, a tolerance and a control.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). Greystack Build Ltd has won the design-and-build contract, and the project board for Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre is being confirmed. Using the additional information about the people, which individual would be most appropriate for each role? Statement 1 of 3: Executive.
o: Paul Kettering
Mark Ostrowski
Owen Pryce
Sunita Rao
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Mark Ostrowski controls the college budget and reserves that part-fund the project and has led a major capital project. The executive is the single point of accountability, owns the business case and secures funding (manual 6.2.4 and appendix B).

n.0: Paul Kettering is a governor and chairs the finance and resources committee, which belongs to the business layer that sets project tolerances; he is not part of the college's management with the budget to commit.
n.2: Owen Pryce represents the contractor, which suits the senior supplier role; the executive represents the college's business interest.
n.3: Sunita Rao is responsible for the apprenticeship programmes that will use the centre, which suits the senior user role.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). Greystack Build Ltd has won the design-and-build contract, and the project board for Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre is being confirmed. Using the additional information about the people, which individual would be most appropriate for each role? Statement 2 of 3: Senior user.
o: Paul Kettering
Mark Ostrowski
Owen Pryce
Sunita Rao
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Sunita Rao is responsible for the apprenticeship programmes that will run in the centre and for recruiting its instructors. The senior user represents those who will use the products, specifies the benefits and is responsible for showing that forecast benefits are on track and for their realization after closure (manual 6.2.4.2 and appendix B).

n.0: Paul Kettering is a governor in the business layer and will not use the centre's products.
n.1: Mark Ostrowski holds the budget and accountability for value, which suits the executive role.
n.2: Owen Pryce represents the organization delivering the building, not the people who will use it.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). Greystack Build Ltd has won the design-and-build contract, and the project board for Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre is being confirmed. Using the additional information about the people, which individual would be most appropriate for each role? Statement 3 of 3: Senior supplier.
o: Paul Kettering
Mark Ostrowski
Owen Pryce
Sunita Rao
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Owen Pryce is contracts director at Greystack Build, which will design and build the centre. The senior supplier represents those delivering the products, commits supplier resources and is accountable for the quality of supplier products (manual 6.2.4 and appendix B).

n.0: Paul Kettering is a governor and a retired construction director; he does not represent or commit any supplier's resources.
n.1: Mark Ostrowski represents the college's business interest as executive.
n.3: Sunita Rao represents the users of the centre.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Leah Whitfield is writing the work package description for the asbestos removal in stage 3, to be carried out by a licensed subcontractor. Under which heading of the work package description should each piece of information be recorded? Statement 1 of 3: Site vehicles must not cross the student pedestrian route, and no removal work may take place while students are arriving or leaving.
o: Techniques and procedures
Constraints
References
Targets and tolerances
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Constraints in a work package description cover restrictions on how the work is done, such as permitted hours, safety and security requirements (plans practice, work package description composition, manual chapter 7).

n.0: These are restrictions on when and where work may happen, not the methods to be used for removal.
n.2: References list the documents the work package draws on, such as higher-level plans; these are restrictions.
n.3: No target or permitted deviation for time, cost or scope is stated.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Leah Whitfield is writing the work package description for the asbestos removal in stage 3, to be carried out by a licensed subcontractor. Under which heading of the work package description should each piece of information be recorded? Statement 2 of 3: Complete the removal in five weeks at a cost of £140,000, plus or minus three days and £7,000.
o: Techniques and procedures
Constraints
References
Targets and tolerances
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: A work package description sets the targets and the time, cost and scope tolerances within which the team manager works; benefits and quality tolerances are not set at this level (manual 11.2.1).

n.0: Duration, cost and permitted deviation are targets and tolerances, not techniques.
n.1: These are targets with permitted deviations rather than restrictions on how the work is done.
n.2: Figures for time and cost with a permitted deviation are tolerances, not references to other documents.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Leah Whitfield is writing the work package description for the asbestos removal in stage 3, to be carried out by a licensed subcontractor. Under which heading of the work package description should each piece of information be recorded? Statement 3 of 3: The stage 3 plan, the asbestos survey report and the product description for the cleared warehouse.
o: Techniques and procedures
Constraints
References
Targets and tolerances
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: References identify the documents the work package relies on, such as the stage plan it comes from and related product descriptions (plans practice, work package description composition, manual chapter 7).

n.0: These are documents to refer to, not the methods the subcontractor will use.
n.1: No restriction on the work is described; these are source documents.
n.3: No time, cost or scope targets are given.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). Leah Whitfield, Bethany Cole and Craig Dunmore are writing the product description for the welding bays. Under which heading of the product description should each piece of information be recorded? Statement 1 of 3: Twenty-four bays, each with a screened booth, a fume extraction hood, a gas supply point and a welding power source.
o: Quality specifications
Quality responsibilities
Composition
Derivation
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Composition lists the parts the product is made up of (product description composition, manual chapter 8).

n.0: No measurable level the product must meet is stated; this lists its parts.
n.1: No producer, reviewer or approver is named.
n.3: Derivation says what the product is developed from; this lists what it contains.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). Leah Whitfield, Bethany Cole and Craig Dunmore are writing the product description for the welding bays. Under which heading of the product description should each piece of information be recorded? Statement 2 of 3: Each extraction hood must achieve a capture velocity of at least 0.5 metres per second at the welding position.
o: Quality specifications
Quality responsibilities
Composition
Derivation
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Quality specifications set the measurable levels the finished product must meet, which quality control checks against (manual 8.2 and product description composition).

n.1: No person responsible for producing, reviewing or approving the bays is named.
n.2: This is a measurable performance level, not a list of the product's parts.
n.3: This is not a source the product is derived from; it is a measure it must meet.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). Leah Whitfield, Bethany Cole and Craig Dunmore are writing the product description for the welding bays. Under which heading of the product description should each piece of information be recorded? Statement 3 of 3: The architect's approved layout drawings and the fume extraction design produced in stage 2.
o: Quality specifications
Quality responsibilities
Composition
Derivation
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Derivation identifies the source products from which the product is developed, here the approved drawings and extraction design (product description composition, manual chapter 8).

n.0: Drawings and a design are sources for the product, not measures of its quality.
n.1: No responsibilities for quality are described.
n.2: These are inputs the bays are built from, not parts of the bays.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the detailed design and procurement stage. Tender prices put the project close to its budget, and Mark Ostrowski suggests replacing the heat pumps with gas boilers to save £280,000, saying this must improve the business case. Leah Whitfield instead updates the business case to show both the saving and the effect on the combined authority's grant compliance scoring and on the college's climate targets, so the board can compare the options. Is this an appropriate application of the business case practice, and why?
o: Yes, because justification is about overall value, and outcomes must stay aligned with business objectives, including ESG goals.
Yes, because the sustainability management approach fixes the heat pumps as a requirement that the board cannot change.
No, because sustainability targets are recorded in the sustainability management approach, not in the business case.
No, because the executive chooses between business options, so the project manager should not analyse alternatives.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Business justification is about value, not cost alone: outcomes and benefits must align with business objectives, which can include ESG goals, and the sustainability management approach supports the business case (see manual 5.2.2 and 5.2.3). A saving that put grant compliance and the climate targets at risk could reduce overall value, so both effects must be shown.

n.1: The sustainability management approach sets targets and controls, but the board can still decide on options; the reason the analysis is right is that value, not cost alone, decides justification.
n.2: The targets sit in the sustainability management approach, which supports the business case; the effect of dropping them on grant scoring and objectives is part of the justification.
n.3: The project manager prepares and maintains the business case on the executive's behalf, including assessing options for the board.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'initiating a project' process. The draft benefits management approach says that Sunita Rao, as senior user, will specify the apprenticeship benefits, show the board at each stage end that the forecast is on track, and remain responsible for the continued realization of the benefits after opening. Benefits reviews are planned at the end of the first and second academic years after opening. Is this an effective way to apply the business case practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the project board will carry out the reviews itself, as it is accountable for the benefits.
Yes, because the senior user specifies the benefits and is responsible for their realization, including after closure.
No, because the executive owns the business case and so should demonstrate that the forecast benefits are on track.
No, because benefits reviews should take place before the board authorizes closure, while the team is in place.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The senior user specifies the benefits, demonstrates that forecast benefits are on track and is responsible for their continued realization after the project closes (see manual 6.2.4.2). The benefits management approach plans the reviews that will confirm them, which the business carries out after closure (see manual 5.5 and 5.3.1).

n.0: Post-project benefits reviews are carried out by the business; the project board does not continue after closure.
n.2: The executive is accountable for the business case, but demonstrating that forecast benefits are on track is a senior user responsibility.
n.3: Most benefits arise after the project; reviews are planned during the project and carried out by the business after closure.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Leah Whitfield works three days a week. Mark Ostrowski proposes that Craig Dunmore act as project manager on her two non-working days, with each of them authorizing work packages and taking decisions on their own days. Is this an appropriate application of the organizing practice, and why?
o: Yes, because PRINCE2 roles can be shared between people when the workload is too great for one person.
Yes, because Craig Dunmore holds a health and safety qualification and knows the college site well.
No, because Craig Dunmore represents the users and so cannot hold any project role other than senior user.
No, because the project manager role should not be shared, so that day-to-day management keeps a single focus.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The project manager role should not be shared, so that day-to-day management has a single point of focus; depending on scale and capacity the project manager may take on team manager and project support roles, but two people should not each act as project manager (see manual 6.2.4).

n.0: Some roles, such as senior user, can be shared, but the project manager role should not be.
n.1: Craig's knowledge may make him useful to the project, but it does not justify splitting the project manager role.
n.2: One person can hold more than one role within the rules, for example user assurance or team manager; the problem is sharing the project manager role.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mark Ostrowski, as executive, asks the college's head of internal audit to provide business assurance by reviewing cost reports and forecasts independently of Leah Whitfield. Sunita Rao, as senior user, asks Craig Dunmore to provide user assurance that the building can be run and maintained. Mark and Sunita remain answerable for assurance in their areas. Is this an effective way to apply the organizing practice, and why?
o: Yes, because assurance can go to suitable people independent of the project manager, while accountability stays with the board.
Yes, because delegating assurance moves accountability for each area from the board members to the people appointed.
No, because project assurance has to be carried out by the board members themselves and cannot be delegated.
No, because assurance should come from project support, so that the registers can be checked at the same time.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Board members are accountable for assurance of their own areas, business, user and supplier, but may delegate it to people in the business or outside it, who must be independent of the project manager; delegating does not move the accountability (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B).

n.1: Board members remain accountable for assurance of their areas even when they delegate the work.
n.2: Assurance can be delegated to people from the business or to external parties.
n.3: Project support must be kept separate from project assurance; it cannot assure the project.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'initiating a project' process. In the product flow diagram, Leah Whitfield shows the nacelle training rig as an external product from the Danish manufacturer. Working back from the opening date, its 30-week lead time and installation in stage 4 mean the order must be placed during stage 2, before the building contract is signed. She schedules the order accordingly. Is this an appropriate application of the plans practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the product flow diagram shows the sequence and dependencies of products, including those from outside.
Yes, because the rig is a must-have product for the wind operators and so is scheduled ahead of every other product.
No, because products supplied from outside the project are outside its control and are left out of its plans.
No, because committing to the rig before stage 4 is authorized conflicts with the manage by stages principle.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Product-based planning includes a product flow diagram showing the sequence of development and the dependencies between products, including external products; the schedule is then built from it, which reveals when long-lead items must be ordered (see manual 7.3.1).

n.1: The rig's importance does not set its place in the schedule; its dependencies and lead time do.
n.2: External products are shown in the product flow diagram because the project depends on them.
n.3: The order is placed within stage 2 under a plan the board has authorized; scheduling for lead times is part of planning.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'initiating a project' process. The governors have set a zero time tolerance on the September opening and a cost tolerance of 3% above budget. In the project plan, Leah Whitfield ranks the products, marks the visitor viewing gallery and the external landscaping as lower priority, and proposes a scope tolerance, for the governors to confirm, that allows them to be dropped if time or cost come under pressure. Is this an effective way to apply the plans practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the project manager sets the project tolerances in the project plan for the board to approve.
Yes, because with time fixed and cost capped, a scope tolerance on lower-priority products gives room to manage.
No, because scope tolerance is set for work packages, not for the project plan or the stage plans.
No, because tolerances should be set equally across all seven aspects so that none takes precedence.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Tolerances are used to manage constraints, and understanding which constraints take precedence is crucial when setting them (see manual 7.2.4). With no time tolerance and a tight cost limit, a scope tolerance based on prioritized products is what allows the plan to flex.

n.0: Project tolerances are set by the business layer, here the governors; the project manager proposes and plans within them.
n.2: Scope tolerance is set for project and stage plans as well as work packages.
n.3: Knowing which constraints take precedence is crucial to setting tolerances; they are not set equally.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the mechanical and electrical fit-out stage. The combined authority wants confidence that the project's checks on the fume extraction and the electrical installation are adequate. Mark Ostrowski asks the college's quality and compliance unit, which sits outside the project management team, to review whether the planned inspections and tests are appropriate and to report its findings to the board. Is this an appropriate application of the quality practice, and why?
o: Yes, because quality assurance is done independently of the project management team, checking that quality controls are suitable.
Yes, because the quality and compliance unit is part of project assurance, which the project manager is responsible for.
No, because quality assurance should be done by the senior supplier, who is accountable for the quality of supplier products.
No, because checking the tests is part of quality control, which team managers carry out within their work packages.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Quality assurance is a planned, systematic activity, performed independently of the project management team, often by a business function, that gives confidence the project's quality control measures are appropriate (see manual 8.2.3). It differs from project assurance, which is the board's responsibility.

n.1: Project assurance is the board's responsibility, not the project manager's, and a unit outside the project management team is providing quality assurance.
n.2: The senior supplier is accountable for supplier products, but quality assurance is independent of the project management team.
n.3: Quality control checks the products themselves; reviewing whether the controls are appropriate is quality assurance.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the commissioning and handover stage. The contractor's commissioning engineer tests the fume extraction, finds four bays below the specified capture velocity, adjusts the fans and retests them the next day. Only the passing retest results are entered in the quality register, so it shows every bay passing first time. Is this an effective way to apply the quality practice, and why?
o: Yes, because a failed check may be repeated where a pass is expected, and the final result is what counts.
Yes, because the quality register is a record for the team, and the board relies on the end stage report instead.
No, because the register should record each quality activity and its result, including failures and the response.
No, because the failed bays are off-specifications that must be accepted as concessions by the project board.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The quality register records all quality activities planned and performed, with dates, responsibilities and results, including failures and the response to them; a failed check may be repeated, but the record must be complete so that progress and quality can be reviewed (see manual 8.2.2 and 8.3.1.2).

n.0: Repeating a failed check is allowed, but the register should still record the failure and the response to it.
n.1: The quality register is used by the project manager and project assurance to review progress, and its records feed the end stage report.
n.3: After adjustment the bays meet their specification, so there is no off-specification needing a concession.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). The SPA project is in the 'initiating a project' process, and Ellie Chandran is preparing the full business case and the management approaches. Which product should each piece of information be recorded in?
