Statement 1 of 3: The project will cost £650,000, mostly to backfill clinical time and pay for training, funded from the commissioner's transformation money; the running cost of the triage hub rota will be met from the community services budget.
o: Project brief
Sustainability management approach
Business case
Benefits management approach
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Project costs, ongoing running costs and how they are funded are recorded under the costs heading of the business case, which is completed as the full business case during initiation (see manual 5.5, business case composition).

n.0: The project brief, with its outline business case, was the basis for authorizing initiation and is superseded by the project initiation documentation; full costs belong in the business case now being prepared.
n.1: The sustainability management approach sets out actions, reviews and controls for sustainability targets, not the project's costs and funding.
n.3: The benefits management approach covers how benefits will be measured and reviewed, not what the project costs.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). The SPA project is in the 'initiating a project' process, and Ellie Chandran is preparing the full business case and the management approaches. Which product should each piece of information be recorded in? Statement 2 of 3: The target is three days from referral to first contact; a result of up to four days is acceptable, and anything above that must be escalated to the trust's executive team.
o: Project brief
Sustainability management approach
Business case
Benefits management approach
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Benefits tolerance, the permitted deviation from a benefit target before escalation, is documented in the benefits management approach (see manual 5.2.2).

n.0: The project brief set out the outline position for initiation; benefits tolerance is documented in the benefits management approach.
n.1: Referral waiting time is a service benefit rather than a sustainability performance target, so its tolerance is not recorded in the sustainability management approach.
n.2: The business case states the expected benefits, but the tolerance on a benefit target is documented in the benefits management approach.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). The SPA project is in the 'initiating a project' process, and Ellie Chandran is preparing the full business case and the management approaches. Which product should each piece of information be recorded in? Statement 3 of 3: Moira Healy's team will count lost and duplicated referrals each month after each locality goes live, and a benefits review will be held 12 months after the final roll-out.
o: Project brief
Sustainability management approach
Business case
Benefits management approach
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The benefits management approach defines the benefits management actions and the benefits reviews, including who measures what and when, so that realization can be confirmed, including after the project closes (see manual 5.5).

n.0: The project brief is superseded at initiation and does not plan benefits measurement after closure.
n.1: Lost referrals are a service benefit; the sustainability management approach covers sustainability targets and their controls.
n.2: The business case says which benefits are expected; the actions and reviews that measure them belong in the benefits management approach.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). The SPA project is in the 'starting up a project' process and the project management team is being appointed. Using the additional information about the people, which individual would be most appropriate for each role? Statement 1 of 3: Executive.
o: Karen Lindqvist
Moira Healy
Dr Samuel Adeyemi
Neil Ashworth
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Karen Lindqvist holds the budget for community services, sits on the trust's executive team and reports to the commissioner on contract performance, so she can secure funding and be accountable for the business case (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B).

n.1: Moira Healy will lead the triage hub and represents the nurses who will use the SPA, which suits the senior user role.
n.2: Dr Samuel Adeyemi's part is to approve changes to the clinical triage criteria; he does not hold the community services budget that the executive needs to secure funding.
n.3: Neil Ashworth is independent of operational services and holds no budget for them, which suits assurance rather than the accountable executive role.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). The SPA project is in the 'starting up a project' process and the project management team is being appointed. Using the additional information about the people, which individual would be most appropriate for each role? Statement 2 of 3: Senior user.
o: Karen Lindqvist
Moira Healy
Dr Samuel Adeyemi
Neil Ashworth
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Moira Healy is head of nursing for Eastfield and will lead the triage hub during the pilot, so she can specify user requirements and benefits and commit user resources (see manual 6.2.4).

n.0: Karen Lindqvist is the budget holder, which suits the executive role; she does not lead the teams that will use the SPA.
n.2: Dr Adeyemi approves the clinical triage criteria, which is a quality approval role; Moira Healy leads the hub whose staff will use the SPA.
n.3: Neil Ashworth is independent of operational services and will not use the SPA.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). The SPA project is in the 'starting up a project' process and the project management team is being appointed. Using the additional information about the people, which individual would be most appropriate for each role? Statement 3 of 3: Business assurance, carried out on Karen Lindqvist's behalf by someone independent of the project manager and of the services being changed.
o: Karen Lindqvist
Moira Healy
Dr Samuel Adeyemi
Neil Ashworth
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Project assurance must be independent of the project manager. Neil Ashworth heads internal audit and assurance, reports to the audit committee and is independent of operational services (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B).

n.0: Karen Lindqvist is the executive; the statement asks for someone to carry out business assurance on her behalf.
n.1: Moira Healy leads the hub that the project changes, so she is not independent of the services being changed.
n.2: Dr Adeyemi must approve the triage criteria that the project produces, so he is not independent of the products and services being assured.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Which role should carry out each of these planning actions on the SPA project? Statement 1 of 3: Provide the trust's planning standards, which the project plan and stage plans must follow.
o: Business layer
Senior user
Project assurance
Project manager
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Providing the planning standards required by the business is an area of focus of the business layer in the plans practice (see manual table 7.1).

n.1: The senior user makes sure plans reflect the user perspective and provides user resources; planning standards come from the business.
n.2: Project assurance reviews progress against tolerances and advises; it does not provide the business's standards.
n.3: The project manager prepares plans in line with the standards; the business layer provides them.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Which role should carry out each of these planning actions on the SPA project? Statement 2 of 3: Make sure the Eastfield pilot stage plan stays consistent with how district nurses and therapists will work in the triage hub.
o: Business layer
Senior user
Project assurance
Project manager
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Ensuring that project and stage plans remain consistent with the user perspective is the senior user's area of focus in the plans practice (see manual table 7.1).

n.0: The business layer provides standards and sets project tolerances; it does not check a stage plan against users' ways of working.
n.2: Project assurance reviews progress against tolerances; keeping plans consistent with the user perspective is the senior user's focus.
n.3: The project manager prepares the stage plan, but making sure it stays consistent with the user perspective is the senior user's focus.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Which role should carry out each of these planning actions on the SPA project? Statement 3 of 3: Decide how the project's work will be divided into stages and delivery steps when drafting the project plan.
o: Business layer
Senior user
Project assurance
Project manager
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Deciding how stages and delivery steps are applied, and preparing the project plan, are areas of focus of the project manager in the plans practice (see manual table 7.1); the board then approves the plan.

n.0: The business layer provides planning standards and sets project tolerances; how the work is divided into stages is decided by the project manager.
n.1: The senior user keeps plans consistent with the user perspective; dividing the work into stages is a project manager decision.
n.2: Project assurance reviews progress against tolerances for the board; it does not decide the project's stages.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). In the design and pilot preparation stage, Ellie Chandran is writing the product description for the triage criteria. Which heading of the product description should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 1 of 3: Gives the triage hub one agreed basis for deciding how soon each referral needs a first contact.
o: Purpose
Composition
Derivation
Quality specifications
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Purpose explains what the product is for and why it is needed (product description composition, manual chapter 8).

n.1: Composition lists the parts the product is made up of, not what it is for.
n.2: Derivation records what the product is based on or developed from.
n.3: Quality specifications set the measures the product must meet and how they are checked; this statement explains why the product exists.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). In the design and pilot preparation stage, Ellie Chandran is writing the product description for the triage criteria. Which heading of the product description should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: Based on the three localities' current acceptance rules, the findings of the serious incident review and national guidance on pressure ulcer care.
o: Purpose
Composition
Derivation
Quality specifications
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Derivation records the sources from which the product is developed (product description composition, manual chapter 8).

n.0: These are the sources of the criteria, not what the criteria are for.
n.1: These are inputs to the criteria, not the sections that make them up.
n.3: No quality measure or check is described; these are the sources the criteria draw on.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). In the design and pilot preparation stage, Ellie Chandran is writing the product description for the triage criteria. Which heading of the product description should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: A flowchart for each referral category and a list of red-flag symptoms that need a first contact on the same day.
o: Purpose
Composition
Derivation
Quality specifications
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Composition lists the parts that make up the product (product description composition, manual chapter 8).

n.0: The statement lists the contents of the criteria rather than explaining what they are for.
n.2: The statement describes what the product contains, not what it is derived from.
n.3: These are parts of the criteria themselves; quality specifications would state how the criteria will be checked, such as clinical sign-off.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The SPA project is in the 'starting up a project' process. In the outline business case, Ellie Chandran compares three options: keep the 14 referral routes and accept the loss of part of the contract value; set up one phone number that forwards calls to the three localities; or the full single point of access with a triage hub. She uses the first option as the baseline against which the other two are measured. Is this an appropriate application of the business case practice, and why?
o: Yes, because even a required project should show that its chosen option gives best value against doing nothing differently.
Yes, because the outline business case gives detailed costs of every option so the board can authorize the project.
No, because the commissioner has made the SPA a contract condition, so the full SPA is the one option to cost.
No, because keeping the current 14 routes is not a valid option to analyse once the commissioner has made the SPA compulsory.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Developing the business case includes options analysis: 'do nothing differently' always comes first and is the baseline for measuring the others, followed by 'do the minimum' and 'do more than the minimum' (see manual 5.2.3 and 5.3.1). Compulsory projects still need to justify the option chosen.

n.1: The outline business case in starting up is high-level and supports the decision to authorize initiation; the project is authorized later on the full business case.
n.2: A contract condition may make some change unavoidable, but the chosen solution must still be justified against the alternatives.
n.3: Keeping things as they are ('do nothing differently') is analysed first even for a required project, because it is the baseline against which the other options are measured.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The SPA project is in the 'initiating a project' process. In the draft benefits management approach, Ellie Chandran names herself as responsible for measuring the fall in unnecessary home visits for 12 months after the final roll-out. No one in the nursing service is named, and Moira Healy, the senior user, has not been asked about the measures. Is this an effective way to apply the business case practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the project manager prepares the benefits management approach on behalf of the executive of the project.
Yes, because the project manager is best placed to compare the home visit data with the figures in the business case.
No, because the senior user is responsible for showing that benefits are on track and for their realization after closure.
No, because benefits should be measured before closure, while the project team is still in place to do the work.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The senior user specifies the benefits and is responsible for demonstrating that forecast benefits are on track and for their continued realization after the project closes, when the project manager's role has ended (see manual 6.2.4.2). Leaving Moira and the nursing service out of the measures weakens the business's ownership of the benefits.

n.0: The project manager may draft the approach for the executive, but that does not make her the right person to measure benefits after the project has closed.
n.1: The project team disbands at closure; measurement over the following 12 months must be owned by the business through the senior user.
n.3: Most benefits are realized after the project closes, so measurement has to continue after closure; the flaw is that nobody in the nursing service owns it.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The SPA project is approaching the end of the Eastfield pilot stage. For the roll-out stage, Ellie Chandran plans how Moorside and Holtby nurses will join the triage rota, which Eastfield pilot staff will hand over and return to their teams, and when Medivault's configurers will leave. She updates the role descriptions and arranges an induction for new hub staff. Is this an appropriate application of the organizing practice, and why?
o: Yes, because 17% staff turnover means the project management team must be redesigned at every stage boundary.
Yes, because the people needed change during a project, so moving people on and off it should be managed.
No, because the project management team structure is fixed at authorization and changes through an exception plan.
No, because moving staff between rotas is a line management matter for the business and lies outside the project.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The organizational design and development technique includes managing ongoing changes to the project ecosystem: the capabilities needed change over the lifecycle, so people are moved on and off the project and new members are inducted (see manual 6.3.1). Role descriptions and the team structure are adapted at stage boundaries.

n.0: Turnover is a reason to plan succession, but the technique does not require a full redesign at every boundary; these changes follow the move from pilot to roll-out.
n.2: The team structure and role descriptions are reviewed and adapted at stage boundaries; they do not need an exception plan to change.
n.3: Line managers release their staff, but planning who joins and leaves the project team, and inducting them, is part of the project's organizing work.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The SPA project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Moira Healy is the senior user. To save her time, she proposes that one of the hub nurses who is writing the triage criteria also carries out user assurance on her behalf, as the nurse knows the criteria in detail. Ellie Chandran agrees. Is this an effective way to apply the organizing practice, and why?
o: Yes, because board members may delegate their assurance work to people from within the business.
Yes, because delegating assurance passes Moira's accountability for user assurance to the nurse.
No, because user assurance should be carried out by an organization from outside the trust.
No, because assurance should not be given to a team member who produces the products being assured.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Project assurance is the board's responsibility and must be independent of the project manager; it cannot be assigned to team members, the project manager or project support (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B). A nurse writing the triage criteria would be assuring her own work.

n.0: Delegating assurance within the business is allowed, but not to someone doing the work being assured.
n.1: Board members stay accountable for assurance of their area even when they delegate the work.
n.2: Assurance can be carried out by board members, by people from the business or by external parties; an outside organization is not required.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The SPA project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Before estimating, Ellie Chandran and Josie Barker draw a product breakdown structure for the SPA, then a product flow diagram showing that the hub rotas cannot be finalized until the triage criteria are signed off. The diagram also shows the commissioner's approval of the new referral pathway, which the project needs but does not produce. Is this an appropriate application of the plans practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the flow diagram shows the sequence and dependencies of products, including external ones.
Yes, because the product breakdown structure lists the activities each team will carry out in the stage.
No, because products from outside the project are beyond its control and should be left out of its plans.
No, because the schedule should be drawn up first so the 18-month deadline decides which products are included.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Product-based planning defines and analyses the products first: the project product description, product breakdown structure, product descriptions and a product flow diagram showing sequence and dependencies, including external products. Work packages, estimates and the schedule follow (see manual 7.3.1).

n.1: A product breakdown structure is a hierarchy of products, not activities; the work is derived from the products later.
n.2: External products and dependencies should be shown so the plan reflects what the project relies on.
n.3: Scheduling comes after the products are defined and estimated; the deadline is a constraint, but the products drive the plan.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The SPA project is in the 'initiating a project' process. The draft project plan has four stages: initiation, design and pilot preparation, the Eastfield pilot, and evaluation and roll-out. To reduce the number of board meetings, Karen Lindqvist, the executive, asks Ellie Chandran to merge the design stage and the pilot into one 28-week stage. The trust has a low appetite for clinical safety risk. Is this an effective way to apply the plans practice, and why?
o: Yes, because longer stages reduce the burden on senior managers, and the trust's directors have limited time for the project.
Yes, because the medical director can sign off the triage criteria during the merged stage without involving the board.
No, because the start of the pilot is a key decision point, and the board should check readiness before patients are triaged.
No, because the stages of a project should be equal in length so that progress can be compared from one stage to the next.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The number and length of stages depend on decision points, risk and complexity, and shorter stages give more control (see manual 2.4 and 7.2.3). Starting to triage real patients is a major, safety-critical commitment, so a stage boundary before the pilot lets the board decide whether the criteria, rotas and system are ready.

n.0: Longer stages do reduce the board's burden, but that trade-off does not suit a safety-critical step in a trust with a low appetite for clinical safety risk.
n.1: Clinical sign-off of the criteria is still required, but it does not replace the board's decision to commit to a live pilot.
n.3: Stage lengths vary with risk, complexity and decision points; equal length is not a requirement.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The SPA project is in the 'initiating a project' process. In the quality management approach, Ellie Chandran states that the trust's quality team, which is independent of the project, will audit whether the project's quality checks on the triage criteria and the system configuration are suitable and are being carried out. Is this an appropriate application of the quality practice, and why?
o: Yes, because this is project assurance, which the board carries out independently of the project.
Yes, because quality assurance gives independent confidence that the project's controls are suitable.
No, because the senior user should check the quality controls, as she will accept the products.
No, because quality checks should be assured by the teams that produce and test the products.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Quality assurance is performed independently of the project management team, typically by a business function such as a quality team, and checks that the project's quality control measures are appropriate (see manual 8.2.3).

n.0: Project assurance is the board's responsibility and is part of the project, though independent of the project manager; an audit by a business function independent of the project is quality assurance.
n.2: The senior user accepts the project product; independent review of the project's quality controls is quality assurance.
n.3: Producing and testing products is quality control; assurance of those controls comes from outside the project management team.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The SPA project is in the 'starting up a project' process. While drafting the project product description, Ellie Chandran records Moira Healy's statement 'referral to first contact within three days' as the first of the SPA's acceptance criteria. Moira, the senior user, agrees with the wording. Is this an effective way to apply the quality practice, and why?
o: Yes, because acceptance criteria should be measurable, and the three-day target can be measured.
Yes, because the senior user is responsible for providing quality expectations and acceptance criteria.
No, because it is a benefit that depends on use after handover, not a test the SPA can be accepted against.
No, because acceptance criteria are set by the project board when it authorizes the project, not in starting up.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Acceptance criteria are prioritized, measurable criteria that the project product must meet before the users accept it, recorded in the project product description (manual chapter 8). An outcome or benefit, such as a shorter wait from referral to first contact, is not a quality expectation or acceptance criterion; it belongs in the business case.

n.0: Being measurable is necessary but not enough: the criterion must be something the delivered product can meet at acceptance, not a benefit that emerges from use.
n.1: The senior user does provide expectations and criteria, but that does not turn a benefit into an acceptance criterion.
n.3: Acceptance criteria are captured in the project product description during starting up.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Nadia Osei is preparing the full business case for Fernhollow Kitchen. Which heading of the business case should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 1 of 3: Branded sales are forecast to reach £6 million a year by year three, at a gross margin of 28%.
o: Reasons
Expected benefits
Expected dis-benefits
Costs
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Expected benefits sets out the measurable improvements the project is expected to bring, assessed against the current situation (business case composition, see manual 5.5). Forecast branded sales and margin are those improvements.

n.0: Reasons explain why the project is needed and how it supports business objectives; this statement gives the measurable result expected.
n.2: Dis-benefits are measurable declines that stakeholders see as negative; higher branded sales and margin are improvements.
n.3: Costs covers project and running costs and their funding, not the income the range will generate.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Nadia Osei is preparing the full business case for Fernhollow Kitchen. Which heading of the business case should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: The new tray-sealing line will cost £640,000 to buy and install, and servicing it will cost £35,000 a year from the operations budget.
o: Reasons
Expected benefits
Expected dis-benefits
Costs
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Costs covers the project's costs and the ongoing operations and maintenance costs, together with how they will be funded (business case composition, see manual 5.5).

n.0: The purchase and servicing costs are not why the project is being undertaken.
n.1: These are costs of the investment, not improvements that it delivers.
n.2: A dis-benefit is a negative outcome of the change, such as lost sales elsewhere; buying and servicing equipment is a cost of the investment.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Nadia Osei is preparing the full business case for Fernhollow Kitchen. Which heading of the business case should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: Own-label sales have been flat for three years with falling margins, and the board's strategy is to build a brand of its own.
o: Reasons
Expected benefits
Expected dis-benefits
Costs
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Reasons explains why the project is needed and how it enables the organization's business objectives, here flat own-label sales and the strategy of building a brand (business case composition, see manual 5.5).

n.1: These are the drivers for the project, not measurable improvements that it will produce.
n.2: Falling own-label margins describe the situation before the project, which is why it is needed; dis-benefits are negative results caused by the project's outcomes.
n.3: No cost or funding information is given.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). The project management team for Fernhollow Kitchen is being appointed. Imogen Fairley, who issued the mandate, will stay in the business layer, and Charlotte Vane has agreed to be one of the senior users. Using the additional information about the people, which individual would be most appropriate for each role? Statement 1 of 3: Executive.
o: Luke Barraclough
Rob Hennessy
Felix Haddad
Dariusz Nowicki
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The executive is the single point of accountability for the project, secures its funding and owns the business case (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B). Rob Hennessy, the finance director, controls funding and is already focused on cash flow and value, so he suits the role.

n.0: Luke Barraclough is independent of production and responsible for food safety, which suits an assurance role rather than ownership of the business case.
n.2: Felix Haddad works for the design agency and would represent a supplier interest, not Fernhollow's business interest.
n.3: Dariusz Nowicki will run the new line and the factory that uses it, which makes him a user representative rather than the owner of the investment.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). The project management team for Fernhollow Kitchen is being appointed. Imogen Fairley, who issued the mandate, will stay in the business layer, and Charlotte Vane has agreed to be one of the senior users. Using the additional information about the people, which individual would be most appropriate for each role? Statement 2 of 3: Senior user, alongside Charlotte Vane.
o: Luke Barraclough
Rob Hennessy
Felix Haddad
Dariusz Nowicki
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The senior user represents those who will use or operate the products and is accountable for specifying the benefits and making sure the products deliver them (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B). Dariusz Nowicki runs the factory and will own the new line after launch, so he represents the operational users.

n.0: Luke's independence from production makes him valuable for assurance; he is not the person who will operate the products.
n.1: Rob is better placed as executive, holding the business interest and funding, not as a user representative.
n.2: Felix represents the agency that designs the packs, which is a supplier interest.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). The project management team for Fernhollow Kitchen is being appointed. Imogen Fairley, who issued the mandate, will stay in the business layer, and Charlotte Vane has agreed to be one of the senior users. Using the additional information about the people, which individual would be most appropriate for each role? Statement 3 of 3: Project assurance on food safety and quality.
o: Luke Barraclough
Rob Hennessy
Felix Haddad
Dariusz Nowicki
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Project assurance must be independent of the project manager and cannot be given to the project manager, team members or project support (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B). Luke Barraclough is responsible for food safety and supermarket audits and is independent of production, so he can assure the board on these matters.

n.1: Rob is better suited to executive; board members are accountable for assurance in their area but usually delegate the work to someone with the right expertise.
n.2: Felix is part of a supplier delivering products, so he could not independently assure the quality of that work.
n.3: Dariusz runs production, so he is not independent of the work that food safety assurance would check.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Fernhollow Kitchen is preparing and approving its plans. Which role should carry out each planning action? Statement 1 of 3: Provide the company's standards for planning capital projects, which every plan in the project must follow.
o: Business layer
Executive
Project manager
Team manager
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: In the plans practice the business layer provides the planning standards that the business requires (plans roles, see manual table 7.1).

n.1: The executive defines stage tolerances and approves stage plans; company-wide planning standards come from the business layer.
n.2: The project manager applies the planning standards when preparing plans but does not set them for the business.
n.3: Team managers plan their own work packages within the standards they are given.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Fernhollow Kitchen is preparing and approving its plans. Which role should carry out each planning action? Statement 2 of 3: Prepare the schedule for the packaging design work package that Mint and Tallow will deliver.
o: Business layer
Executive
Project manager
Team manager
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Team managers prepare the schedules for each work package they take on, and may prepare team plans (plans roles, see manual table 7.1).

n.0: The business layer sets planning standards and project tolerances, not schedules for individual work packages.
n.1: The executive approves stage plans and sets stage tolerances; it does not schedule work packages.
n.2: The project manager prepares the stage plan and work package descriptions; the schedule for the work within a package is prepared by its team manager.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Fernhollow Kitchen is preparing and approving its plans. Which role should carry out each planning action? Statement 3 of 3: Define the tolerances for the trials stage and approve the trials stage plan.
o: Business layer
Executive
Project manager
Team manager
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The executive defines the tolerances for each stage and approves stage plans (plans roles, see manual table 7.1).

n.0: The business layer sets project-level tolerances; stage tolerances are set on the board by the executive.
n.2: The project manager prepares the stage plan and works within its tolerances; approving it and setting its tolerances is for the executive.
n.3: Team managers work within work package tolerances set by the project manager.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). Nadia Osei is drafting the quality management approach for Fernhollow Kitchen. Which heading of the quality management approach should each statement be recorded under? Statement 1 of 3: Fernhollow's existing food safety management system and Mint and Tallow's own design quality procedures apply to the project.
o: Standards
Supporting tools and techniques
References
Responsibilities
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: References lists associated documents and products, such as the business's or the supplier's quality management systems, that the approach relies on (quality management approach composition, see manual 8.5).

n.0: Standards sets out the standards that apply to quality management itself, such as legal requirements and the format of quality records; existing management systems are referenced documents.
n.1: Supporting tools and techniques covers the systems and techniques used for quality planning and control, such as testing or inspection.
n.3: Responsibilities names who does what in quality planning, control and acceptance; no roles are given here.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). Nadia Osei is drafting the quality management approach for Fernhollow Kitchen. Which heading of the quality management approach should each statement be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: Luke Barraclough will approve the allergen controls for each recipe, and Charlotte Vane will accept the finished range on behalf of the users.
o: Standards
Supporting tools and techniques
References
Responsibilities
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Responsibilities defines who is responsible for quality planning and control activities, including assurance and acceptance authorities (quality management approach composition, see manual 8.5).

n.0: No standard is stated; the entry assigns approval and acceptance to named people.
n.1: No tool or technique is described; the entry says who approves and who accepts.
n.2: No external document is cited; the entry sets out quality responsibilities.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). Nadia Osei is drafting the quality management approach for Fernhollow Kitchen. Which heading of the quality management approach should each statement be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: Every label must comply with food labelling and allergen law, and all quality records must follow the company's standard register format.
o: Standards
Supporting tools and techniques
References
Responsibilities
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Standards covers any standards that apply to quality management, including legal requirements for published material and the composition and format of the quality register and other quality records (quality management approach composition, see manual 8.5).

n.1: Labelling law and record formats are standards to comply with, not tools or techniques for carrying out quality control.
n.2: References points to associated documents such as quality management systems; these are standards the project must meet.
n.3: No person or role is named; the entry sets out standards.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'initiating a project' process. Nadia Osei's draft full business case assesses a single option: launching all six recipes, with two made by Greendale. Rob Hennessy asks her to compare three options instead: doing nothing differently, launching the four recipes that can be made in-house, and launching all six. Each option is to show its costs, benefits and risks. Is this an appropriate application of the business case practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the executive is accountable for the business case and so can decide what it contains.
Yes, because comparing options, with doing nothing as the baseline, shows the value each investment would buy.
No, because paying the £180,000 listing fee has committed the board to launching at least four recipes.
No, because options are assessed in starting up, so the full business case should cover the chosen option.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Developing the business case includes analysing options: do nothing differently (assessed first, as the baseline), do the minimum and do more than the minimum. The difference between them is the benefit the investment buys (see manual 5.3.1). Four in-house recipes is Harbridge's accepted minimum, so it is a realistic option alongside six.

n.0: Rob is accountable for the business case, but that does not explain why comparing options is good practice.
n.2: Paying the fee does not commit the board to continue: the fee is lost under every option, and doing nothing differently stays the baseline against which the other options are quantified.
n.3: The outline business case is developed in starting up, but it is refined into the full business case in initiation, when options can be assessed with better cost and risk information.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'managing a stage boundary' process at the end of the development stage. The tray-sealing line has cost £70,000 more than planned, and Greendale has confirmed its 150,000-meal minimum, which is now above the sales forecast for its two recipes. Nadia Osei updates the project plan and the trials stage plan but leaves the business case as it was approved in initiation, because the launch week cannot move. How well does this apply the business case practice, and why?
o: It applies it well, because the business case was approved by the board when it authorized the project.
It applies it well, because the fixed launch week means the business case cannot change the plan.
It applies it poorly, because the business case should be updated with actuals and forecasts for the board to check.
It applies it poorly, because the business case should be confirmed by a benefits review at each stage end.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The business case is maintained at the end of each stage: the project manager updates it with progress data and the latest forecasts, and the board checks it is still desirable, viable and achievable before authorizing the next stage (see manual 5.3.1). Higher line costs and a co-manufacturing minimum above forecast sales directly affect the justification.

n.0: Approval at authorization creates a baseline, but the business case must then be maintained and checked throughout, not frozen.
n.1: A fixed date constrains the plan but does not make the costs, benefits and risks irrelevant to the decision to continue.
n.3: Benefits are confirmed mainly after closure; at stage ends the business case is updated and checked, not confirmed.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage. Before Gerrit Vos's installation engineers arrive for the factory shutdown, Nadia Osei arranges a site induction, a food hygiene certificate and allergen awareness training for each of them, and pairs each engineer with a Fernhollow maintenance fitter for the first week. Which step of the organizational design and development technique is being applied?
o: Understand the organizational ecosystem
Design the project ecosystem
Develop the project ecosystem
Transition the project into the organizational ecosystem
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Developing the project ecosystem is the ongoing development of people and relationships as needs and membership change, including onboarding such as site visits, induction and certification (see manual 6.3.1).

n.0: Understanding the organizational ecosystem examines existing structures, governance and policies before the project ecosystem is designed.
n.1: Designing the project ecosystem decides how work and people will be organized; the onboarding of new members follows once that design is in place.
n.3: Transition hands products, people and learning back to the business at closure; the engineers are joining the project, not leaving it.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'initiating a project' process. To keep costs down, Rob Hennessy, the executive, proposes that Amy, the project coordinator who maintains the project log and prepares board papers for Nadia Osei, should also carry out business assurance and report directly to him. How well does this apply the organizing practice, and why?
o: It applies it well, because the board decides how project assurance is done and may appoint anyone from the business.
It applies it well, because Amy would report to Rob, which keeps business assurance independent of the project manager.
It applies it poorly, because project support and project assurance should be kept separate.
It applies it poorly, because project assurance has to be carried out by an organization outside Fernhollow.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Project assurance cannot be given to the project manager, team members or project support, and project support must be kept separate from assurance (see manual 6.2.4 and appendix B). Amy maintains the project log for Nadia, so she would be assuring her own work.

n.0: The board does decide how assurance is done, but it cannot give it to someone who already holds the project support role.
n.1: A reporting line to the executive does not make Amy independent: she prepares the material that assurance would check.
n.3: Assurance can be done by board members, by people appointed from the business or by external parties; an outside organization is not required.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'initiating a project' process. Working with Megan Cho and Dariusz Nowicki, Nadia Osei draws a product flow diagram. It shows that the carbon label cannot be finalized until the recipes are fixed, and that the Harbridge's audit result, an external product, depends on the line being commissioned. Is this an appropriate application of the plans practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the product flow diagram replaces the need for a product breakdown structure on a hybrid project.
Yes, because it shows the sequence and dependencies of the products, including external ones, before scheduling.
No, because external products such as the audit result are outside the project's control and are not planned.
No, because dependencies should be shown in the work breakdown structure, not in a product flow diagram.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: In product-based planning the product flow diagram shows the sequence in which products are developed and the dependencies between them, including intermediate and external products (see manual 7.3.1). Identifying these early lets the schedule reflect them, here the link between commissioning the line and passing the audit.

n.0: The product breakdown structure is still created; the product flow diagram builds on it rather than replacing it.
n.2: External products are outside the project's control, which is exactly why they are shown as dependencies in the plan.
n.3: The work breakdown structure is a hierarchy of work linking products to work packages; product sequence and dependencies are shown in the product flow diagram.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'initiating a project' process. Nadia Osei's draft project plan contains a day-by-day schedule for all five stages, including every factory trial run nine months from now. Charlotte Vane praises the detail and asks for it to be baselined so that progress can be tracked against it. Is this an appropriate application of the plans practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the fixed launch week means all of the work should be scheduled in detail from the start.
Yes, because a detailed baseline gives the board the clearest basis for managing by exception.
No, because the project plan should be prepared by the team managers who will carry out the work.
No, because the near future can be planned in detail, and later stages are detailed in their own stage plans.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The planning horizon limits how far ahead detailed planning is reliable. PRINCE2 uses a high-level project plan and a detailed plan for the current stage, with each later stage plan prepared near the end of the stage before it (see manual 7.2.1 and 7.2.2). A day-by-day schedule for trials nine months away is likely to be wrong and costly to maintain.

n.0: A fixed end date makes planning important but does not extend the planning horizon; detail is added stage by stage.
n.1: Tolerances need a realistic plan; a detailed but unreliable schedule creates false deviations rather than better control.
n.2: The project manager prepares the project plan; team managers prepare team plans and work package schedules.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the trials stage. Fernhollow's group food safety auditor, who reports to Imogen Fairley and has no role in the project, reviews whether the shelf-life tests, allergen swabbing and metal detection checks planned for the trials are adequate for a supermarket launch. Which part of the quality practice is being applied?
o: Quality assurance
Quality control
Project assurance
Quality planning
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Quality assurance gives confidence that products will meet their quality specifications when tested. It is carried out independently of the project management team, typically by a business function, and checks that the project's quality control measures are appropriate (see manual 8.2.3).

n.1: Quality control is carrying out the checks on the products themselves; the auditor is reviewing whether the planned checks are adequate.
n.2: Project assurance is the project board's responsibility and sits within the project; the auditor has no project role and works for the business.
n.3: Quality planning defines the quality specifications and methods; the auditor is reviewing the planned checks independently, not planning them.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'starting up a project' process. While the project product description is being prepared, Charlotte Vane asks for 'Fernhollow Kitchen recognized by 30% of Harbridge's shoppers within a year of launch' to be listed as an acceptance criterion for the range. Is this an appropriate application of the quality practice, and why?
o: Yes, because acceptance criteria should be measurable, and a 30% recognition target can be measured.
Yes, because the senior user provides the acceptance criteria for the project product.
No, because brand recognition is an outcome of using the products, not something the range must meet to be accepted.
No, because acceptance criteria are set out in each product description rather than in the project product description.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Acceptance criteria are a prioritized list of measurable attributes that the project product must meet before the users accept it (see manual 8.1.1). Shoppers recognizing the brand is a result of the change after launch, an outcome, and cannot be checked when the range is handed over.

n.0: Being measurable is necessary but not enough: the criterion must describe the product, not the result of using it.
n.1: Acceptance criteria do come from the users, through the senior user role, but this entry is an outcome, and who proposes it does not make it a valid criterion.
n.3: Acceptance criteria belong in the project product description; quality specifications belong in product descriptions.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Kezia Oduya is preparing the business case practice products for the Carrowford Half Marathon. Which product should each piece of information be recorded in? Statement 1 of 3: No single-use plastic bottles on the course, 70% of event waste recycled, free bus travel for runners, and a carbon footprint report published within two months of the event.
o: Business case
Benefits management approach
Sustainability management approach
Communication management approach
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The sustainability management approach defines the actions, reviews and controls that will ensure the project's sustainability performance targets are met, with reference to the organization's environmental goals (see manual 5.2.2 and 5.5).

n.0: The business case sets out the reasons, benefits, costs and time for the investment; the council's sustainability targets and their controls belong in the sustainability management approach.
n.1: The benefits management approach covers how benefits will be measured and reviewed, not sustainability performance targets.
n.3: The communication management approach covers communication with stakeholders; publishing a carbon report is one of the sustainability targets, not a communication procedure.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Kezia Oduya is preparing the business case practice products for the Carrowford Half Marathon. Which product should each piece of information be recorded in? Statement 2 of 3: Local spending may fall up to 10% below the £2.5 million target before the shortfall must be escalated; it will be measured by an independent economic impact study six weeks after race day.
o: Business case
Benefits management approach
Sustainability management approach
Communication management approach
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The benefits management approach defines how benefits will be measured and reviewed and records the benefits tolerance, the permitted deviation in benefit targets before escalation (see manual 5.2.2 and 5.5).

n.0: The business case states the expected benefits themselves; the tolerance and the way they will be measured and reviewed belong in the benefits management approach.
n.2: Local spending is an economic benefit target, not one of the event's sustainability performance targets.
n.3: The statement sets a benefits tolerance and a measurement method, not how stakeholders will be informed.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Kezia Oduya is preparing the business case practice products for the Carrowford Half Marathon. Which product should each piece of information be recorded in? Statement 3 of 3: The event will cost £900,000, partly offset by £45 entry fees and £150,000 of sponsorship, with the council's net contribution capped at £300,000.
o: Business case
Benefits management approach
Sustainability management approach
Communication management approach
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The business case records the costs of the project and how they are funded, weighed against the expected benefits and risks (business case costs heading, manual 5.5).

n.1: The benefits management approach covers measuring and reviewing benefits, not the project's costs and funding.
n.2: No sustainability target or control is given; these are costs and funding arrangements.
n.3: Costs and funding are not communication arrangements.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). The project management team for the Carrowford Half Marathon is being appointed. Using the additional information (people), which individual is most appropriate for each role? Statement 1 of 3: Executive, accountable for the business case and for securing the project's funding.
o: Cllr Yvonne Price
Andrew Mallory
Bernadette Lowe
Greg Halloran
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The executive is the single point of accountability, owns the business case and secures funding (see manual 6.2.4). Andrew Mallory received the mandate from the cabinet and holds the events budget.

n.0: Cllr Price is the event's political champion and part of the cabinet that commissioned it; she does not hold the budget or the mandate.
n.2: Bernadette Lowe is an internal auditor, independent of the project, which suits an assurance role rather than accountability for it.
n.3: Greg Halloran runs the contracted supplier; he represents the supplier interest, not the council's business interest.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). The project management team for the Carrowford Half Marathon is being appointed. Using the additional information (people), which individual is most appropriate for each role? Statement 2 of 3: Senior supplier, able to commit the supplier's people and accountable for the quality of what it delivers.
o: Cllr Yvonne Price
Andrew Mallory
Bernadette Lowe
Greg Halloran
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The senior supplier represents the suppliers, commits their people and resources, and is accountable for the quality of supplier products (see manual 6.2.4). Greg Halloran commits Paceline's staff and is accountable for its race-day operations.

n.0: Cllr Price champions the event for the council; she has no authority over Paceline's resources.
n.1: Andrew Mallory represents the council's business interest; he cannot commit Paceline's staff.
n.2: Bernadette Lowe audits for the council and has no authority over the supplier.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (organizing). The project management team for the Carrowford Half Marathon is being appointed. Using the additional information (people), which individual is most appropriate for each role? Statement 3 of 3: Business assurance, checking on the executive's behalf and independently of Kezia Oduya that the project is being run properly.
o: Cllr Yvonne Price
Andrew Mallory
Bernadette Lowe
Greg Halloran
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Project assurance is independent of the project manager and can be provided by people appointed from the business (see manual 6.2.4). Bernadette Lowe is a senior auditor who has audited two council events and whose team has said it will review the project.

n.0: Cllr Price is the event's public champion and wants to start the race, so she is not well placed to give independent assurance.
n.1: Andrew Mallory is the executive; this role acts on his behalf, so it needs someone else.
n.3: Greg Halloran represents the supplier, so he cannot give the council independent business assurance.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Kezia Oduya is drafting the work package description for Paceline's course set-up work on the Carrowford Half Marathon. Which heading of the work package description should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 1 of 3: Crews may work on the roads between 10pm and 5am only under police escort, and every marshal must have completed the council's safety briefing.
o: Techniques and procedures
Constraints
References
Targets and tolerances
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Constraints are restrictions or limits on the work, such as authorized working hours, safety and security measures (work package description contents, manual 7.5).

n.0: Techniques and procedures describe how the work is to be done; permitted hours and safety conditions are limits on the work.
n.2: References point to applicable higher-level plans; these are restrictions on how the work may be carried out.
n.3: Targets and tolerances set permitted deviations in scope, cost and time; these are limits on hours and safety, not tolerances.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Kezia Oduya is drafting the work package description for Paceline's course set-up work on the Carrowford Half Marathon. Which heading of the work package description should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: The dates and the certified route set out in the build-up stage plan and the project plan.
o: Techniques and procedures
Constraints
References
Targets and tolerances
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: References list the applicable references from higher-level plans that the team manager needs (work package description contents, manual 7.5).

n.0: The statement points to higher-level plans rather than describing how the work is to be done.
n.1: No restriction such as hours or safety measures is given; it identifies the plans the work must follow.
n.3: No permitted deviation in scope, cost or time is given.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (plans). Kezia Oduya is drafting the work package description for Paceline's course set-up work on the Carrowford Half Marathon. Which heading of the work package description should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: The work may finish up to two days late or cost up to £3,000 more before Lisa Ventnor must raise it with Kezia.
o: Techniques and procedures
Constraints
References
Targets and tolerances
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Targets and tolerances set the permissible deviations for scope, cost and time for the work package, beyond which the team manager raises the matter with the project manager (work package description contents, manual 7.5 and 11.2.1).

n.0: The statement sets limits of delegated authority, not working methods.
n.1: Constraints are restrictions on how the work is done, such as hours or safety; time and cost deviations are tolerances.
n.2: No higher-level plan is referred to; these are the work package's own tolerances.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). Kezia Oduya is drafting the quality management approach for the Carrowford Half Marathon. Which heading should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 1 of 3: Paceline's own quality management system for race operations, which the project will refer to for its timing and course checks.
o: References
Responsibilities
Supporting tools and techniques
Standards
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The references heading points to associated documents or products, such as the business's or a supplier's quality management system (quality management approach contents, manual 8.5).

n.1: No person or role is given a quality duty; the statement points to the supplier's existing system.
n.2: Supporting tools and techniques are methods such as testing or inspection; the statement identifies a document to be referred to.
n.3: Standards are the standards that apply to quality management on the project; a supplier's own system is recorded as a reference.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). Kezia Oduya is drafting the quality management approach for the Carrowford Half Marathon. Which heading should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: Bernadette Lowe will provide business assurance on quality, and Lisa Ventnor will approve the race-day marshal guide before it is printed.
o: References
Responsibilities
Supporting tools and techniques
Standards
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The responsibilities heading defines who does what in quality planning and control, including project assurance responsibilities and who approves products (quality management approach contents, manual 8.5).

n.0: No associated document or quality system is referred to; the statement assigns quality duties to people.
n.2: No testing, inspection or other technique is described; the statement names who assures and who approves.
n.3: No standard is set; the statement assigns roles.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (quality). Kezia Oduya is drafting the quality management approach for the Carrowford Half Marathon. Which heading should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: Everything published for the event, from the entry website to the race-day guide, must comply with data protection legislation.
o: References
Responsibilities
Supporting tools and techniques
Standards
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The standards heading records standards that apply to quality management across the project, such as legal compliance required of all published material (quality management approach contents, manual 8.5).

n.0: The statement sets a requirement that applies to every published item, not a pointer to an associated quality system.
n.1: No person or role is assigned a quality duty.
n.2: No testing, inspection or other technique is described; this is a standard all published items must meet.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'initiating a project' process. In the full business case Kezia Oduya compares three options: holding no event, which shows what would happen without the investment; a 10k race with no festival; and the full half marathon with the riverside festival. She quantifies the costs, risks and local spending of the last two against the first. Is this an appropriate application of the business case practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the 'do nothing differently' option is the baseline against which the value of the others is measured.
Yes, because the cabinet's mandate names the half marathon, so the comparison will confirm that choice is right.
No, because holding no event is not a real option once the date has been agreed with the national athletics body.
No, because benefits cannot be quantified until the event has run and the economic impact study is complete.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Business options always start with 'do nothing differently', which is the baseline for quantifying the other options; the difference between the options is the benefit the investment buys (see manual 5.3.1). Comparing the 10k and the full event against no event shows which option gives the best value.

n.1: The comparison is meant to show which option gives the best value, not to confirm a choice already made.
n.2: Even when a project is expected, the 'do nothing differently' option is kept as the baseline for measuring the others.
n.3: Benefits are forecast in the business case to support decisions; they are confirmed later through benefits reviews.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the build-up stage. Harriet Bloom tells Kezia Oduya that the building society will cut its sponsorship from £150,000 to £100,000 because entries are behind target. Kezia logs the news but decides that the business case can wait for her end stage update in eight weeks' time, when the board will review it. Is this an effective way to apply the business case practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the business case is maintained at the end of each stage with the latest costs and forecasts.
Yes, because sponsorship income is a commercial matter for Andrew Mallory as executive, not for Kezia.
No, because Kezia should assess the effect of issues on the business case as they arise, as this threatens the cap.
No, because the sponsor's change should be confirmed through a benefits review before it is accepted.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The project manager checks the business case when assessing issues and risks for their impact on the justification, not only at stage ends (see manual 5.3.1). Losing £50,000 of income could push the council's net contribution past the £300,000 cap, so the board may need to act before the stage ends.

n.0: It is true that the business case is maintained at stage ends, but this does not remove the need to assess a major issue when it arises.
n.1: The executive owns the business case, but the project manager assesses issues for their impact on it on the executive's behalf.
n.3: Benefits reviews confirm whether benefits have been realized, mostly after closure; they are not used to assess a change in funding.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in its final stage. Kezia Oduya plans how the race know-how, the volunteer database, Paceline's contract contacts and the events officers who gained experience on the project will pass to the council's events team, which will run the race each year as normal business. Which step of the organizational design and development technique is she applying?
o: Develop the project ecosystem, as the events officers' new skills are recorded for later events.
Manage ongoing changes to the project ecosystem, as people move off the project when it ends.
Understand the organizational ecosystem, as the events team's current structure must be known.
Transition the project into the organizational ecosystem, as people, products and learning return.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The final step of the technique transitions the project into the organizational ecosystem: products, people and learning are handed back to the business at closure (see manual 6.3.1). Here the event is being handed to the events team to repeat as normal business.

n.0: Developing the project ecosystem is ongoing onboarding, skills and culture work while the project runs, not the handover at the end.
n.1: Managing ongoing changes covers moving people on and off as needs change during the lifecycle; handing the event to the business is the transition step.
n.2: Understanding the organizational ecosystem happens first, before the project ecosystem is designed.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'initiating a project' process. To save money, Andrew Mallory proposes that Martin Cole, the council's corporate risk and insurance manager, provide business assurance for the project and also act as project support, keeping the risk register, the issue register and the project log up to date for Kezia Oduya. Is this an effective way to apply the organizing practice, and why?
o: Yes, because Martin Cole is independent of Kezia Oduya, which project assurance requires.
Yes, because roles can be combined to suit the project, and the council saves the cost of a support officer.
No, because project assurance should be carried out by a board member rather than delegated to others.
No, because project support should be kept separate from project assurance so that assurance stays objective.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Project support is the project manager's responsibility and must be kept separate from project assurance, which is the board's; support staff cannot carry out assurance (see manual 6.2.4). Maintaining Kezia's registers would put Martin Cole inside the work he is meant to assure.

n.0: Independence from the project manager is needed, but combining assurance with support breaks the rule that the two roles are kept apart.
n.1: Roles can be combined, but not these two; the saving does not make the combination acceptable.
n.2: Board members are accountable for assurance but may delegate the work to people from the business or outside it.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'initiating a project' process. After writing the product breakdown structure, Kezia Oduya and Lisa Ventnor draw a product flow diagram. It shows that the course certificate must exist before entries open, and that the safety advisory group's approval and the police road closure order, which the project does not produce, are needed before race-day set-up. Is this an appropriate application of the plans practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the diagram lets the team estimate each product's cost before the product descriptions are written.
Yes, because a product flow diagram shows the sequence and dependencies of products, including external ones.
No, because products that the project does not create, such as the approval, should be left off the diagram.
No, because product flow diagrams are drawn by team managers for team plans, not for the project plan.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: In product-based planning the product flow diagram defines the sequence in which products are developed and the dependencies between them, including intermediate and external products (see manual 7.3.1). The approval and road closure order are external products the event depends on.

n.0: Estimates come after the products are defined and analysed; the diagram's purpose is sequence and dependencies, not costing.
n.2: External products are shown on the diagram because the project depends on them.
n.3: Product-based planning is used for project, stage and team plans; the project plan needs it during initiation.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Before the board sets stage tolerances, Kezia Oduya runs a short workshop with its members. They agree that race day cannot move, that public safety standards cannot be lowered and that the council's £300,000 cap is firm, so any flexibility must come from the scope of the riverside festival. Is this an effective way to apply the plans practice, and why?
o: Yes, because knowing which constraints take precedence is needed to choose approaches and set suitable tolerances.
Yes, because the project manager sets the stage tolerances and needs the board's views before doing so.
No, because stage tolerances are set by the business layer, so the board's views on constraints are not needed.
No, because scope tolerance belongs in work package descriptions rather than in stage plans.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Understanding which constraints take precedence is a crucial part of planning, used to select approaches and set tolerances (see manual 7.2.4). The board then allocates stage tolerances to the project manager, here leaving flexibility in festival scope.

n.1: The project board sets stage tolerances; the project manager sets work package tolerances.
n.2: The business layer sets project tolerances; the board sets stage tolerances within them.
n.3: Scope tolerance is set for plans at each level, including stage plans, as well as in work package descriptions.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'starting up a project' process. Kezia Oduya is drafting the project product description with Andrew Mallory and Greg Halloran. Under the user's quality expectations she writes: 'The event will bring about £2.5 million into local businesses over the weekend.' Is this an appropriate application of the quality practice, and why?
o: Yes, because quality expectations should show how the event supports the council's Active Carrowford strategy.
Yes, because user's quality expectations are high-level statements that do not need to be measurable.
No, because local spending is a benefit expected from the event, not the quality expected of what is delivered.
No, because quality expectations belong in the quality management approach, not the project product description.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The user's quality expectations describe the quality expected of the project product, captured in the project product description; an outcome or benefit such as more local spending is not a quality expectation (see manual 8.1.1 and 5.1). Expectations here would cover, for example, a safe, certified and well-marshalled course.

n.0: Alignment with strategy is shown in the business case; quality expectations describe the quality of the product itself.
n.1: It is true that expectations are high-level and may not be measurable, but this does not make a benefit into a quality expectation.
n.3: The user's quality expectations are recorded in the project product description; the quality management approach describes how quality will be achieved.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the build-up stage. Because Paceline's medical response at an earlier race was criticized, Andrew Mallory wants confidence in the medical plan. Lisa Ventnor's team checks the plan against its product description, and Kezia Oduya asks the council's health and safety unit, which is independent of the project, to review whether those checks are adequate. Is this an effective way to apply the quality practice, and why?
o: Yes, because quality control by the producers is backed by quality assurance from a function outside the project.
Yes, because project assurance must be independent of the project manager, which the health and safety unit is.
No, because the senior supplier is accountable for the quality of Paceline's products, so the council should not review them.
No, because quality assurance should be carried out by project support, who maintain the quality register.
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: Quality control checks products against their specifications, while quality assurance, carried out independently of the project management team by a business function, gives confidence that the quality controls are appropriate (see manual 8.2.2 and 8.2.3).

n.1: Project assurance is the board's responsibility and is independent of the project manager only; a unit outside the project is providing quality assurance.
n.2: The senior supplier is accountable for supplier product quality, but the business can still seek independent assurance that quality controls are adequate.
n.3: Project support administers quality records; it is part of the project management team, so it cannot provide independent quality assurance.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Mairi Campbell is preparing the full business case for Project Skyline. Which heading of the business case should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 1 of 3: The landlord of the Leeds data centre will not extend the lease, and the society's board has adopted a strategy of moving to public cloud hosting.
o: Reasons
Expected benefits
Time
Costs
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The reasons heading explains why the project is needed and how it supports the organization's business objectives: here the end of the Leeds lease and the approved cloud strategy (business case composition, manual chapter 5).

n.1: These are the drivers for the project, not measurable improvements it will produce.
n.2: No project duration or benefits period is described; the lease ending is a reason for the project.
n.3: No cost or funding information is given.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Mairi Campbell is preparing the full business case for Project Skyline. Which heading of the business case should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: The project will run for about 19 months from the start of initiation, and the running cost savings will be realized from year three onwards.
o: Reasons
Expected benefits
Time
Costs
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The time heading records the period over which the project runs and the period over which its benefits are expected to be realized (business case composition, manual chapter 5).

n.0: These are timings, not the reasons why the project is needed.
n.1: Expected benefits states the measurable improvements themselves; when the project runs and when benefits arrive is recorded under time.
n.3: No cost or funding information is given; this is about duration and timing.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Matching set (business case). Mairi Campbell is preparing the full business case for Project Skyline. Which heading of the business case should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: Once all applications are live, the cloud subscription and the vendor's hosted core banking service will cost about £2.1 million a year, paid from the IT operations budget.
o: Reasons
Expected benefits
Time
Costs
Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.w: The costs heading covers the project's costs and the ongoing operating and maintenance costs of its products, together with how they will be funded (business case composition, manual chapter 5).

n.0: A running cost is not a reason for undertaking the project.
n.1: The charge is a cost of the investment, not an improvement it delivers, even though it is lower than today's running costs.
n.2: The yearly charge is a running cost; the time heading records how long the project runs and over what period benefits are realized.

Practitioner: Business Case to Quality.q: Project Skyline is in the 'starting up a project' process. Mairi Campbell prepares the outline business case with three options: do nothing differently, which would leave the Leeds systems with nowhere to run when the lease ends; move the Leeds systems to Falkirk and replace the old hardware; and move both sites to the cloud, as the strategy proposes. Each option is compared with the first. Is this an appropriate application of the business case technique, and why?
o: Yes, because the outline business case has to recommend the cheapest of the options that meets the lease deadline.
Yes, because doing nothing differently is the baseline against which the benefits of the other options are measured.
