It supports, rather than replaces, the project manager's reporting.

n.0: Data can inform forecasts, but tolerances are set by the management levels, not by systems.
n.2: The project manager still owns the highlight report, but drawing on automated data makes it more timely and accurate.
n.3: Routes switched over, staff trained and shifts filled measure progress on the stage's work, not benefits.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (risk). Nadia Osei is adding a risk about the new tray-sealing line to the risk register. Which heading of the risk register should each statement be recorded under? Statement 1 of 3: Because the line has a 14-week lead time, a late purchase order could delay commissioning, leaving too little time for factory trials before launch.
o: Risk owner
Risk description
Risk action owner
Proximity
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The risk description sets out the cause, the uncertain event and its effect on objectives (risk register composition, see manual 9.5). Here the cause is the lead time, the event is a late order delaying commissioning, and the effect is squeezed trials.

n.0: The risk owner is the person responsible for managing the risk; no person is named here.
n.2: The risk action owner carries out agreed actions for the risk owner; no person is named here.
n.3: Proximity records how soon the risk might occur; this statement describes its cause, event and effect.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (risk). Nadia Osei is adding a risk about the new tray-sealing line to the risk register. Which heading of the risk register should each statement be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: The risk could occur within the next six weeks, when the purchase order for the line must be signed.
o: Risk owner
Risk description
Risk action owner
Proximity
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Proximity records how close in time the risk might occur (risk register composition, see manual 9.5).

n.0: No person is assigned; the statement is about timing.
n.1: The statement gives when the risk might occur, not its cause, event and effect.
n.2: No person or action is assigned; the statement is about timing.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (risk). Nadia Osei is adding a risk about the new tray-sealing line to the risk register. Which heading of the risk register should each statement be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: Dariusz Nowicki will be responsible for managing the risk and deciding how to respond to it.
o: Risk owner
Risk description
Risk action owner
Proximity
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The risk owner is the person responsible for managing the risk and deciding its response (risk register composition, see manual 9.5).

n.1: The statement names who manages the risk, not the risk's cause, event and effect.
n.2: A risk action owner carries out specific agreed actions on behalf of the risk owner; Dariusz is managing the risk as a whole and deciding the response.
n.3: No timing is given.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (issues). Amy provides project support for Fernhollow Kitchen, and Felix Haddad is the team manager for packaging design. Senior user
Project support
Team manager

n.2: Project support administers the issue procedure; it does not decide on escalated issues.
n.3: Team managers implement corrective actions in their work packages; they do not decide on escalated issues.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (issues). Amy provides project support for Fernhollow Kitchen, and Felix Haddad is the team manager for packaging design. Which role should carry out each action? Statement 2 of 3: Write new product descriptions and a new work package after the board approves an extra 'high protein' claim on two of the packs.
o: Project manager
Senior user
Project support
Team manager

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (issues). Amy provides project support for Fernhollow Kitchen, and Felix Haddad is the team manager for packaging design. Which role should carry out each action? Statement 3 of 3: Enter a new request for change from Charlotte Vane in the issue register and update its status as it is assessed.
o: Project manager
Senior user
Project support
Team manager
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Project support administers the issue and change control procedures by maintaining the issue register (issues roles, see manual table 10.2).

n.0: The project manager runs the issue procedure and keeps the register when there is no project support; here Amy provides support.
n.1: The senior user decides on escalated issues; keeping the register is administration.
n.3: Team managers implement corrective actions in their work packages; they do not keep the issue register.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (progress). Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage. Which report or log should each item be recorded in? Statement 1 of 3: Ordering pack proofs in batches of six cut two weeks from the design cycle, and Nadia Osei wants later stages and future projects to use the idea.
o: Highlight report
Lessons log
Daily log
Exception report

n.2: The daily log holds informal issues, actions and notes; a lesson to be reused is recorded in the lessons log.
n.3: Nothing is forecast to exceed tolerance.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (progress). Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage. Which report or log should each item be recorded in? Statement 2 of 3: The stage is now forecast to finish four weeks late, beyond its two-week time tolerance, and Nadia Osei sets out options and a recommendation for the board.
o: Highlight report
Lessons log
Daily log
Exception report
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: An exception report is produced by the project manager when a stage plan is forecast to exceed its tolerances, and it gives options and a recommendation (see manual 11.5).

n.0: A highlight report gives routine stage status; a forecast breach of stage tolerance needs an exception report.
n.1: This is not a lesson; it is a forecast breach of tolerance that must be escalated.
n.2: A forecast breach of stage tolerance needs formal escalation to the board, not an informal note.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (progress). Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage. Which report or log should each item be recorded in? Statement 3 of 3: Nadia Osei's fortnightly summary for the board of the stage's progress, including the results of the latest consumer panel.
o: Highlight report
Lessons log
Daily log
Exception report
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: A highlight report summarizes stage status for the project board at the intervals the board has set (see manual 11.5).

n.1: The lessons log records lessons, not routine status reports to the board.
n.2: The daily log is the project manager's informal record, not a report to the board.
n.3: Nothing is forecast to exceed tolerance; this is routine time-driven reporting.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the concept and recipe stage. Sesame has never been handled on the Fernhollow site, and a cross-contact incident there could lead to a recall that puts the own-label contracts at risk. Greendale Ready Meals already handles sesame under audited controls. The board agrees to Nadia Osei's proposal that Greendale should make the sesame recipe, so that no sesame enters the Fernhollow site. Which risk response is being used, and why?
o: Reduce, because Greendale's audited controls make a cross-contact incident less likely.
Transfer, because Greendale takes on the financial impact of any sesame incident under the agreement.
Avoid, because moving production removes the cause of the threat from the Fernhollow site.
Share, because Fernhollow and Greendale will split the costs and gains of making the sesame recipe.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Avoiding a threat makes the uncertain situation certain by removing the risk, for example by removing its cause (see manual 9.2.3, table 9.1). With no sesame on the Fernhollow site, the threat of cross-contact there can no longer occur.

n.0: Reducing a threat changes its probability or impact while a residual risk remains; here the cause of the threat is taken off the Fernhollow site.
n.1: Transfer passes part of the financial impact to a third party, for example through insurance or a contract clause; nothing here moves financial liability.
n.3: Sharing is a pain and gain arrangement with a partner; the scenario describes no split of costs or gains.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'initiating a project' process. Imogen Fairley has made clear that the company has a very low appetite for food safety and allergen risks. Nadia Osei is drafting the risk management approach and needs a measurable threshold for the allergen-related risk exposure that can be accepted before it must be escalated. Who should set this risk tolerance?
o: Imogen Fairley, as the business layer, because she has set the company's risk appetite.
Nadia Osei, as project manager, because she is writing the risk management approach.
Luke Barraclough, because he is responsible for allergen control and food safety audits.
The project board, applying the risk appetite that the business has set.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Risk appetite is the business's attitude to risk, set here by Imogen Fairley for the company. Risk tolerance is the measurable threshold for each objective at risk, and it is set by the project board based on the business's overall risk appetite (see manual 9.2.1).

n.0: The business layer determines the appetite; the project board turns it into measurable tolerances for the project.
n.1: The project manager documents the tolerance in the risk management approach but does not set it.
n.2: Luke's expertise can inform the threshold, but setting risk tolerance is a project board decision.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'initiating a project' process. At a risk workshop, Dariusz Nowicki says the line installation after the Christmas peak will go to plan because his team has not missed a shutdown deadline in ten years. The other directors agree without discussion, and the risk that trials will be squeezed into five weeks is scored as low probability. Nadia Osei records the score in the risk register. Is this an effective application of the risk practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the operations director knows the factory best, so his view should decide the score.
Yes, because the board has said it is willing to take commercial risk to build the brand.
No, because the assessment shows groupthink, with the directors agreeing rather than testing the estimate.
No, because the timing of the line should be recorded as an issue, since the Christmas peak is certain.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Decision bias can distort risk assessment, and groupthink, valuing group cohesion over dissent or the right decision, is one of the named biases (see manual 9.2.4). The directors accepted one confident view without challenge, so the probability score is unreliable; Nadia should test it, for example with data on past shutdowns and the supplier's commissioning record.

n.0: Expert knowledge is valuable, but an unchallenged view from one person is how bias enters an assessment.
n.1: The appetite for commercial risk does not excuse a poor assessment of a risk that threatens the fixed launch week.
n.3: The peak is certain, but whether trials will be squeezed is still uncertain, so it is a risk; the problem is how it was scored.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage. The product description for the meal sleeves requires them to be recyclable at the kerbside. The packaging supplier's first production batch uses a film that cannot be recycled at the kerbside, and the supplier says a compliant film would add three weeks. How should Nadia Osei treat this?
o: As an off-specification, handled through change control, with options to correct it or grant a concession.
As a request for change, because the board will need to relax the recyclability requirement for the launch.
As a risk, recorded in the risk register, because the three-week delay to the compliant film may not happen.
As an informal problem, recorded in the daily log and settled between Nadia and the packaging supplier.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its quality specifications. It is a formal issue that goes through change control, where the decision may be to correct it or to grant a concession (see manual 10.1 and 10.2.3). The batch has already failed the recyclability requirement, so it is an issue, not a risk.

n.1: A request for change proposes a change to a baseline; here a product has failed an existing specification, which is an off-specification whatever is later decided.
n.2: The non-compliant batch already exists, so this is an issue; the possible delay is part of its impact.
n.3: A product failing a board-level sustainability requirement needs formal handling through the issue register, not an informal note.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the concept and recipe stage. The fortnightly tastings produce frequent requests to change recipes and pack designs. The board appoints Charlotte Vane as change authority for recipe and packaging changes costing up to £8,000 each, gives her a change budget of £50,000 for the stage, and records the arrangement in the issue management approach. Larger changes still come to the board. Is this an effective application of the issues practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the senior user is accountable for the business case and so should approve changes.
Yes, because delegating approval within limits, backed by a change budget, suits frequent iterative changes.
No, because the project board is the authority for requests for change and cannot pass this to one member.
No, because approved changes should be funded from the risk budget so that costs are tracked in one place.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The project board is the ultimate authority for changes but may delegate approval to a change authority within limits, and delegated authority should come with a change budget so that approved changes can be funded (see manual 10.2.4 and 10.2.5). With changes arising every two weeks, this keeps decisions quick while larger changes still reach the board.

n.0: The executive, not the senior user, is accountable for the business case.
n.2: The board is the ultimate authority but may delegate the approval of changes within limits, which is what it has done.
n.3: The risk budget funds responses to risks; approved changes are funded from the change budget.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is about to start the trials stage. Factory trials, shelf-life tests and the Harbridge's audit all fall within a few weeks, and two team managers will be reporting for the first time. The board asks for highlight reports every week during this stage instead of every month, and Nadia Osei asks the team managers for checkpoint reports twice a week. Which statement BEST explains why this is an appropriate use of the progress practice?
o: Highlight and checkpoint reports are event-driven controls, so they should be triggered by each trial run.
More frequent highlight reports remove the need for exception reports during a high-risk stage.
Reporting frequency should reflect the control needed, and inexperienced teams need more frequent reports.
The frequency of highlight reports is set in each work package description, so team managers can agree it.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Reporting frequency should reflect the level of control required, and an inexperienced team needs more frequent reporting until confidence grows (see manual 11.2.4). A short, high-risk stage with new team managers justifies weekly highlights to the board and more frequent checkpoints.

n.0: Highlight and checkpoint reports are time-driven controls produced at agreed intervals, not triggered by events.
n.1: Exception reports are still needed if stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded; routine reports do not replace them.
n.3: Highlight report frequency is set by the board; work package descriptions set the frequency of checkpoint reports.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage, which has a time tolerance of two weeks. Gerrit Vos warns Nadia Osei that, on the current shipping schedule, the line is likely to arrive five weeks late. Nadia decides not to tell the board until the delay actually happens, because the supplier's forecasts have been wrong before. Is this an appropriate application of the progress practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the project manager is expected to resolve problems before involving the board.
Yes, because the board should be given confirmed facts rather than uncertain forecasts.
No, because the line supplier's penalty clause should be enforced before any escalation.
No, because a forecast breach of stage tolerance is an exception and should be escalated now.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: An exception is a situation where it can be forecast that tolerances will be exceeded, and the project manager should alert the board as early as possible through an exception report (see manual 11.1, 11.2.6 and 16.4.7). A credible forecast of five weeks against a two-week tolerance is enough to escalate; waiting removes the board's options.

n.0: The project manager acts within tolerance; a forecast breach of stage tolerance is outside her authority and goes to the board.
n.1: Manage by exception relies on forecasts so that the board can act before the breach occurs.
n.2: Contract penalties may recover some costs but do not change the forecast breach of the stage's time tolerance.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (issues). The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the planning and approvals stage. Where should each item be recorded or described? Lessons log
End project report
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The lessons log is the informal repository of lessons that could be applied on this or future projects, recorded as they are identified (see manual 11.5).

n.0: A highlight report gives stage status to the board; a lesson noted during the stage is recorded in the lessons log.
n.1: A checkpoint report gives work package status to the project manager; lessons are recorded in the lessons log.
n.3: The end project report is written at closure; the lesson is captured now in the lessons log.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (progress). Which report or log of the Carrowford Half Marathon project should each item be recorded in? Statement 3 of 3: The status of the build-up stage against its tolerances, sent to the board every two weeks.
o: Highlight report
Checkpoint report
Lessons log
End project report
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The highlight report is a time-driven summary of stage status that the project manager sends to the board at intervals the board defines (see manual 11.2.2 and 11.5).

n.1: A checkpoint report goes from a team manager to the project manager about a work package; stage status for the board is a highlight report.
n.2: The lessons log records lessons, not stage status.
n.3: The end project report is produced at closure.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the build-up stage. Harriet Bloom says the building society would value the event far more if it were shown on regional television, which is possible but not certain. To raise the chance of coverage, Kezia Oduya invites the regional broadcaster to a site visit and offers it free camera positions at the start and finish. Which type of risk response is being applied, and why?
o: Exploit, because the action makes sure that the television coverage will take place.
Enhance, because the action increases the probability of the opportunity without making it certain.
Share, because the broadcaster and the building society both gain if the coverage goes ahead.
Accept, because the project will wait to see whether the broadcaster decides to cover the race.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Enhance is a response to an opportunity that takes definite action now to increase its probability or impact; exploit would make the opportunity certain (see manual 9.2.3, table 9.1). An invitation and free positions make coverage more likely but do not guarantee it.

n.0: Exploit removes the uncertainty; the broadcaster may still decline, so coverage is not made certain.
n.2: Share is a pain or gain arrangement with a partner, usually through a contract; no such arrangement is made here.
n.3: Accept means taking no action now, but Kezia is acting to raise the chance of coverage.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'initiating a project' process. The council's risk management policy sets a low appetite for risks to public safety and reputation and a moderate appetite for financial risk on events. Kezia Oduya's draft risk management approach uses one probability and impact scale for every risk, and lets her accept any risk scored below 'high' without referring it to the board. Is this an effective way to apply the risk practice, and why?
o: Yes, because using one scale for every risk makes it easier to compare and prioritize risks across categories.
Yes, because the project manager sets the risk tolerances when writing the risk management approach.
No, because the low appetite for safety and reputation risk calls for tighter thresholds than for financial risk.
No, because the risk management approach should list each identified risk together with its owner and response.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The business sets the risk appetite and the project board sets risk tolerances based on it (see manual 9.2.1). With a low appetite for safety and reputation risk, the thresholds for escalating those risks should be tighter than for financial risk, not the same single cut-off.

n.0: A common scale helps comparison, but it ignores the different appetites the council has set for different kinds of risk.
n.1: Risk tolerance is set by the project board based on the business's risk appetite, not by the project manager.
n.3: Specific risks, owners and responses belong in the risk register; the approach describes procedures, scales and responsibilities.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the planning and approvals stage. The product description for the course requires a certified distance of 21.0975 km. The accredited course measurer reports that the route designed by Paceline is 40 metres short, so it cannot be certified until it is changed. Entries are due to open in three weeks. How should Kezia Oduya classify this issue, and why?
o: As a request for change, because the route design will have to be altered before entries open.
As a concern, because its effect on the date for opening entries still has to be assessed.
As a problem, because it has an immediate negative effect on the planning and approvals stage.
As an off-specification, because a product will not meet the specification in its product description.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its quality specifications (see manual 10.1, issue types). The route design is a product whose product description requires the certified distance, and it falls short.

n.0: A request for change proposes changing a baseline; here the baseline (the required distance) stays the same and the product fails to meet it.
n.1: The impact will be assessed, but the issue is already known to be a product failing its specification.
n.2: It is negative, but PRINCE2 classifies a product that will not meet its specification as an off-specification.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'initiating a project' process. The board agrees that Kezia Oduya may approve requests for change costing up to £5,000 each from a change budget of £20,000, and that any change affecting the route or the event safety plan comes to the board. The arrangement is written into the issue management approach and Kezia's role description. Is this an effective way to apply the issues practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the board may delegate approval of changes within limits, with a budget to fund approved changes.
Yes, because the project manager is the ultimate authority for requests for change once the project is authorized.
No, because changes should be funded from the risk budget, which pays for responses to threats and opportunities.
No, because change authority should be given to a separate group, not the project manager, to keep it independent.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The project board is the ultimate authority for changes but may delegate approval within limits to a change authority or the project manager, with a change budget so approved changes can be funded; the delegation is documented in the issue management approach and role descriptions (see manual 10.2.4 and 10.2.5).

n.1: The board remains the ultimate authority; the project manager approves changes only within the limits delegated.
n.2: The risk budget funds risk responses; approved changes are funded from the change budget.
n.3: The board may delegate change authority to the project manager as well as to a separate person or group.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon build-up stage has a cost tolerance of plus or minus £20,000. Inspector Ravi Sandhu asks for an extra staffed crossing at the hospital access road, costing £12,000. This is above Kezia Oduya's £5,000 change limit but within stage tolerance. Kezia registers the request, assesses its effect on the plan, budget and safety plan, and sends the board her options and a recommendation. Is this an appropriate application of the issues practice, and why?
o: Yes, because a request from the police is an external event, so the project manager may approve it herself.
Yes, because she captures and assesses the request and recommends options to those with authority to decide.
No, because a request from the safety advisory group should be treated as a risk rather than as an issue.
No, because a change above the project manager's limit should be raised with the board in an exception report.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The issues technique is capture, assess, recommend, decide and implement: the request is registered, its impact assessed, and options with a recommendation go to whoever holds the authority to decide (see manual 10.3.1). As the cost is within stage tolerance, an issue report is used rather than an exception report.

n.0: Its source does not change the approval rule: at £12,000 it is above Kezia's delegated limit, so the board decides.
n.2: The request has already been made, so it is an issue to be handled, not an uncertain future event.
n.3: An exception report is used when stage or project tolerance is forecast to be exceeded; this change is within stage tolerance.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the planning and approvals stage, and entries have just opened. Kezia Oduya sets up an online dashboard that takes entry numbers from the entry system each day, compares them with the planned entry curve and forecasts whether 6,000 entries will be reached by the end of June. Board members can view it between highlight reports. Is this an appropriate application of the progress practice, and why?
o: Yes, because data and systems help compare actual progress with the plan and forecast likely outcomes.
Yes, because the dashboard can set the entry tolerances from the daily figures as they change.
No, because progress control compares actual achievement with the plan rather than forecasting results.
No, because the board should receive progress information in highlight reports rather than on a dashboard.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The progress practice compares actual achievements with the plan and forecasts the project's objectives and viability; data and systems support tracking, forecasting and presentation in stakeholders' preferred format (see manual 11.1, 11.2.5 and 11.2.7). The end-of-June forecast matters because of the 6,000-entry trigger.

n.1: Tolerances are set by the management levels, not by data or systems.
n.2: Forecasting is part of the purpose of the progress practice, not separate from it.
n.3: Highlight reports continue; data and dashboards can supplement them in the format stakeholders prefer.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon build-up stage has a cost tolerance of plus or minus £20,000. Three weeks into the stage, Kezia Oduya forecasts that higher prices for barriers and grandstands will push stage costs £35,000 over plan. None of the extra money has been spent yet, so she decides to report the position in the end stage report and look for savings in the meantime. Is this an effective way to apply the progress practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the end stage report gives the board the information it needs to decide what to do next.
Yes, because tolerance is not exceeded until the extra money has actually been spent.
No, because a forecast breach of stage tolerance is an exception and should be reported to the board now.
No, because the extra costs should be approved by Cllr Yvonne Price as cabinet member for leisure.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: An exception is a situation where a deviation beyond agreed tolerance can be forecast; the project manager escalates it to the board in an exception report as soon as it is forecast, so the board can decide in good time (see manual 11.1 and 11.3.1).

n.0: The end stage report supports the next-stage decision; waiting until then denies the board the chance to act on the exception now.
n.1: Exceptions are based on forecasts, not only on money already spent.
n.3: Stage tolerance breaches are decided by the project board; the cabinet member is not part of the board.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (risk). Mairi Campbell is entering a new risk in the risk register for Project Skyline: if wave 3 overruns into the December change freeze, its remaining switch-overs could not take place until January. Which heading of the risk register should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 1 of 3: Could arise from month 12 of the project, when wave 3 is due to finish just before the freeze begins.
o: Risk description
Proximity
Impact
Risk response
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Proximity records how close in time the risk might occur (risk register composition, manual 9.2.2 and chapter 9 management products): here from month 12, just before the freeze.

n.0: The risk description sets out the cause, event and effect; timing information goes under proximity.
n.2: Impact is the estimated effect on objectives if the risk occurs, not when it might occur.
n.3: The risk response describes the actions chosen to deal with the risk, not its timing.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (risk). Mairi Campbell is entering a new risk in the risk register for Project Skyline: if wave 3 overruns into the December change freeze, its remaining switch-overs could not take place until January. Which heading of the risk register should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 2 of 3: Estimated at a five-week delay to the end of the wave migration stage and about £180,000 of extra Stratoshift day rates.
o: Risk description
Proximity
Impact
Risk response
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Impact is the estimated effect on objectives if the risk occurs, expressed in the units of those objectives, such as weeks and pounds (see manual 9.2.2 and chapter 9 management products).

n.0: The description names the cause, event and effect in words; the estimated size of the effect is recorded as impact.
n.1: Proximity records when the risk might occur, not its size.
n.3: These figures estimate the consequence; they are not actions taken in response.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (risk). Mairi Campbell is entering a new risk in the risk register for Project Skyline: if wave 3 overruns into the December change freeze, its remaining switch-overs could not take place until January. Which heading of the risk register should each piece of information be recorded under? Statement 3 of 3: Reduce: book the wave 3 switch-over weekends now and agree a standby weekend team with Stratoshift.
o: Risk description
Proximity
Impact
Risk response
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The risk response records the chosen response type and the actions to carry it out (see manual 9.2.3.1 and chapter 9 management products). Booking slots now and arranging a standby team is a reduce response.

n.0: The description explains what might happen and why; the actions agreed to deal with it are the risk response.
n.1: Proximity records when the risk might occur, not what will be done about it.
n.2: Impact estimates the consequences; the planned actions are recorded under the response.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Steven Clarke finds that 20 of the finance applications could be moved onto the cloud provider's managed database service instead of being copied as they are. This would raise the chance that running cost savings exceed the £1.4 million forecast, although the extra saving is not certain. Mairi Campbell agrees to the redesign. Which risk response is being used, and why?
o: Exploit, because the redesign is intended to capture the extra saving for the society.
Share, because the extra saving will be divided between the society and the cloud provider.
Enhance, because action is taken now to increase the probability and impact of an opportunity.
Accept, because the opportunity is being taken without changing any of the agreed plans.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Enhance takes proactive action to increase the probability and/or impact of an opportunity; exploit would make the opportunity certain (see manual 9.2.3.1, table 9.1). The redesign makes greater savings more likely, but they remain uncertain.

n.0: Exploit removes the uncertainty so that the opportunity is certain to occur; here the extra saving is still uncertain.
n.1: Share is a pain and gain sharing arrangement with a partner; nothing in the scenario divides the saving with the provider.
n.3: Accept means taking no action now; redesigning 20 applications is a definite action.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. To avoid weekend premium rates, Arjun Menon proposes moving the online banking application on a Tuesday evening. Fraser McIntyre agrees, saying that the ten pilot applications all moved without trouble, so the risk of an outage is low. The pilot applications were chosen because they were low risk and not member-facing. How well does this apply the risk practice, and why?
o: It applies it well, because the board's moderate appetite for cost risk supports saving on premium rates.
It applies it well, because data from the pilot wave is being used to assess the probability of an outage on this move.
It applies it poorly, because the outage risk should be transferred to Stratoshift under the framework contract.
It applies it poorly, because it conflicts with the very low appetite for outages and rests on optimism from the pilot.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Risk decisions should respect the risk appetite and the tolerances set from it, and should guard against decision bias such as optimism bias, which assumes success and discounts unfavourable risks (see manual 9.2.1 and 9.2.4). The pilot gives little evidence about a member-facing system, and the board has a very low appetite for outages.

n.0: The moderate appetite for cost risk does not outweigh the very low appetite for outages to member-facing services.
n.1: Data should inform risk assessment, but data from low-risk, non-member-facing applications is not good evidence for online banking.
n.2: Transferring financial impact does not remove the outage to members, which is what the board has a very low appetite for.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (issues). The society's change team provides a project support officer for Project Skyline, and Arjun Menon is the team manager for the migrations. Which role should carry out each of these actions in the issues practice? Statement 1 of 3: Update the issue register with the status of Aileen Docherty's request to add a data platform.
o: Senior user
Project manager
Team manager
Project support
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Project support administers the issue and change control procedures by maintaining the issue register (see manual chapter 10, table 10.2).

n.0: The senior user makes decisions on escalated issues; keeping the register up to date is an administrative task.
n.1: The project manager manages the procedure and keeps the register only where there is no project support; here a support officer is provided.
n.2: The team manager implements corrective actions in the work package; the issue register is maintained for the whole project.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (issues). The society's change team provides a project support officer for Project Skyline, and Arjun Menon is the team manager for the migrations. Which role should carry out each of these actions in the issues practice? Statement 2 of 3: Write new product descriptions and a new work package for the extra monitoring dashboards that the board has approved.
o: Senior user
Project manager
Team manager
Project support
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The project manager implements corrective actions, for example creating new product descriptions and work packages when extra scope has been agreed (see manual chapter 10, table 10.2).

n.0: The senior user decides on escalated issues; planning the approved change is the project manager's work.
n.2: The team manager implements corrective actions within a work package once it has been authorized; creating new work packages is the project manager's job.
n.3: Project support maintains the register; it does not write product descriptions or authorize work.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (issues). The society's change team provides a project support officer for Project Skyline, and Arjun Menon is the team manager for the migrations. Which role should carry out each of these actions in the issues practice? Statement 3 of 3: Decide on an escalated request to move the branch systems a month earlier, focusing on protecting the benefits expected for member services.
o: Senior user
Project manager
Team manager
Project support
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The senior user makes decisions on escalated issues with a focus on safeguarding the expected benefits (see manual chapter 10, table 10.2).

n.1: The issue has been escalated beyond the project manager's authority, so the decision sits with the board.
n.2: The team manager does not decide escalated issues; it implements corrective actions in its work package.
n.3: Project support records the decision in the register but does not make it.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. During testing, the mortgage servicing application recovers from a simulated failure in six hours. Its product description requires recovery within four hours. Arjun Menon tells Mairi Campbell that a fix would delay wave 2 by three weeks. Which type of issue is this, and why?
o: A request for change, because the four-hour recovery requirement may now need to be relaxed to six hours.
An off-specification, because the product will not meet a quality specification set in its product description.
A risk rather than an issue, because the application has not yet been switched over to the cloud.
A business opportunity, because six hours is still a large improvement on the current 24 hours.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its quality specifications (issue types, manual chapter 10). The product description requires recovery within four hours and testing shows six, so the application is off-specification; the board or change authority may later grant a concession or require a fix.

n.0: A request for change proposes a change to a baseline; relaxing the requirement might be one response, but the issue raised is that the product fails its specification.
n.2: The shortfall has already been found in testing, so it is an issue, not an uncertain future event.
n.3: A business opportunity is an unexpected positive consequence; failing the required recovery time is a defect against the specification.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage, which is forecast to stay within its tolerances. Aileen Docherty asks for a new data platform to be added to the project. Mairi Campbell records the request in the issue register and assesses its impact on cost, the lease deadline, the risks and the business case. It would cost £900,000, well beyond the change budget delegated to her, so she sends an issue report with options and a recommendation to the project board. How well does this apply the issues practice, and why?
o: It applies it well, because the request is captured, assessed and recommended, then referred to those with authority to decide.
It applies it well, because the project manager is the change authority for every request for change on the project.
It applies it poorly, because a request for change should stay in the daily log until the board says it is a formal issue.
It applies it poorly, because a request for change of this size should be escalated to the board in an exception report.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The issue technique is capture, assess, recommend, decide and implement; a request beyond the project manager's delegated authority is referred, with options and a recommendation, to whoever holds that authority, ultimately the project board (see manual 10.3.1 and 10.2.4). An issue report is the right vehicle when the stage is within tolerance.

n.1: The board is the ultimate authority and may delegate some authority, but here the cost is far beyond what was delegated to Mairi.
n.2: A request for change that needs a formal decision is a formal issue and belongs in the issue register; the daily log is for informal issues.
n.3: Exception reports are for forecast breaches of stage or project tolerance; the stage is within tolerance, so an issue report is used.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (progress). Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Which report or log should each item be recorded in? Statement 1 of 3: Arjun Menon tells Mairi Campbell, at the frequency set in the work package, how far the wave 2 migrations have progressed and what risks his team has found.
o: Checkpoint report
Highlight report
Exception report
Lessons log
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: A checkpoint report is produced by the team manager for the project manager on the status of a work package, at the frequency defined in the work package description (see manual chapter 11, progress management products).

n.1: Highlight reports go from the project manager to the board on the status of the stage.
n.2: Exception reports go from the project manager to the board when stage or project tolerance is forecast to be exceeded.
n.3: The lessons log records lessons, not regular work package status.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (progress). Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Which report or log should each item be recorded in? Statement 2 of 3: Mairi Campbell informs the board that wave 3 is now forecast to end five weeks late, beyond the stage's time tolerance, and sets out the options and her recommendation.
o: Checkpoint report
Highlight report
Exception report
Lessons log
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: An exception report is produced by the project manager when a stage plan or project plan is forecast to exceed its tolerances; it sets out the consequences, options and a recommendation (see manual chapter 11 and 11.3.1).

n.0: Checkpoint reports go from the team manager to the project manager on a work package.
n.1: Highlight reports give routine stage status; a forecast breach of stage tolerance needs an exception report.
n.3: The lessons log records lessons; it is not used to escalate a forecast breach.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Matching set (progress). Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Which report or log should each item be recorded in? Statement 3 of 3: The list of application dependencies at the Leeds site proved incomplete, so discovery work for future waves should start at least six weeks earlier.
o: Checkpoint report
Highlight report
Exception report
Lessons log
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The lessons log is the informal repository for lessons that apply to this or future projects; lessons are recorded as they arise and acted on throughout (see manual chapter 11 and 2.2).

n.0: A checkpoint report gives work package status; a lesson for future waves is recorded in the lessons log.
n.1: A highlight report may mention lessons, but the lesson itself is recorded in the lessons log.
n.2: Nothing is forecast to exceed tolerance; this is a lesson, not an exception.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. The stage plan sets a time tolerance of two weeks for each migration wave. Arjun Menon's checkpoint report forecasts that wave 3 will finish five weeks late because the core banking vendor has delayed a shared interface. Mairi Campbell cannot find a way to recover the time within tolerance. What should Mairi do NEXT?
o: Prepare an exception plan for the rest of the stage and submit it to the board for approval.
Take corrective action by moving applications between waves and report it in the next highlight report.
Raise an exception report to the project board, setting out the options and her recommendation.
Ask the business layer to increase the project's time tolerance so that wave 3 can finish later.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: When stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded, the project manager escalates by raising an exception report to the project board with options and a recommendation; the board then decides, for example by asking for an exception plan (see manual 11.2.6 and 11.3.1).

n.0: An exception plan is prepared after the board has considered the exception report and asked for one; it is not the first step.
n.1: Corrective action is for deviations that can be dealt with within tolerance; Mairi cannot recover the time.
n.3: Stage tolerance breaches go to the project board; the business layer deals with breaches of project tolerance.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Project Skyline is at the start of the foundations stage. Stratoshift's Pune team has not worked with the society's systems before. Mairi Campbell agrees in the work package that Arjun Menon will send checkpoint reports daily during switch-over weekends and twice a week at other times, moving to weekly once the pilot wave is complete. Is this an effective way to apply the progress practice, and why?
o: Yes, because reporting is more frequent while the team is new and the work riskier, and eases as confidence grows.
Yes, because time-driven checkpoint reports remove the need for event-driven controls during the stage.
No, because the frequency of checkpoint reports is set by the project board in the PID and should not vary.
No, because checkpoint reports during switch-over weekends should go directly to the project board.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: Reporting frequency should reflect the level of control needed: an inexperienced team, or risky work, warrants more frequent reporting until confidence grows (see manual 11.2.4). Checkpoint frequency is agreed in the work package between the project manager and team manager.

n.1: Time-driven and event-driven controls are both needed; regular reports do not replace stage-end decisions or exception reports.
n.2: Checkpoint frequency is agreed in each work package description and can differ between work packages and over time.
n.3: Checkpoint reports go from the team manager to the project manager; the board receives highlight reports from the project manager.

Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Mairi Campbell has been spending a day every fortnight combining spreadsheets from Edinburgh, Pune and Falkirk to produce her highlight report. She arranges for the migration tool's data to feed a shared dashboard automatically, from which Arjun Menon's checkpoint reports and her highlight reports are produced in the format the board prefers. Is this an appropriate application of the progress practice, and why?
o: Yes, because the dashboard can set the work package tolerances from the data it collects on each migration.
Yes, because data and automation remove manual consolidation and present progress in the form stakeholders prefer.
No, because highlight reports should be compiled by hand by the project manager so that she can check the figures.
No, because a shared dashboard cannot be used once the audit committee has asked for a monthly written update.
Practitioner: Risk, Issues & Progress.w: The progress practice encourages using data and systems to track progress and support decisions: automation removes the manual consolidation of separate sources, and information can be presented in the format stakeholders prefer (see manual 11.2.7).

n.0: Data supports tracking and forecasting, but tolerances are set by the management levels, not by tools.
n.2: Manual compilation is not required; automating the consolidation makes reporting faster and more consistent, and the project manager still reviews the report.
n.3: The written update to the audit committee can still be produced from the same data; the dashboard does not prevent it.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Permits Online is in the 'starting up a project' process. Hannah Okoro meets Graham Pell, Ruth Abernethy and Siobhan Kerr to agree what the project will deliver. Together they draft the project product description, including the users' quality expectations and the go-live conditions as acceptance criteria. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare the outline business case' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the executive, senior user and senior supplier are consulted to define what the project will deliver.
Yes, because the outline business case must contain the detailed costs from the project product description.
No, because the project product description is created in initiation as part of preparing the project plan.
No, because the senior supplier should not be involved until the project has been authorized by the board.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In 'prepare the outline business case' the project manager consults the executive, senior user and senior supplier to understand what the project is to deliver and creates the project product description, including the quality expectations and acceptance criteria (see manual 13.4.3).

n.1: The outline business case is high level at this point; detailed costs come from the project plan in initiation.
n.2: The project product description is created in starting up a project; it is then used in initiation and when closing the project.
n.3: The senior supplier is consulted in starting up so that what is to be delivered is understood from the supplier side too.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Permits Online is in the 'starting up a project' process. The chief executive's office has appointed Graham Pell as executive. Graham is now choosing the senior user and senior supplier and agreeing who will provide project assurance. Which role is accountable for the 'appoint the project management team' activity?
o: The executive, Graham Pell, who is choosing the other members of the board.
The project manager, Hannah Okoro, who will lead the project team day to day.
The project board, once all of its members have been appointed.
The business layer, here the chief executive's office that commissioned the project.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the recommended RACI for 'appoint the project management team', the business layer is accountable and the executive is responsible for making the appointments; the project manager is not involved (see manual 13.4.4 and table 13.2).

n.0: Graham Pell is responsible for carrying out the appointments; accountability for them sits with the business layer.
n.1: The project manager is not involved in appointing the project management team.
n.2: The board cannot be accountable for appointing itself; the business layer that commissions the project is accountable.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Permits Online is in the 'starting up a project' process. Worried about the fixed date of 31 October, Hannah Okoro asks Kestrel Lane to start building prototype screens straight away, before the project brief has been approved, so that the alpha stage can be shortened later. Is this an effective way to carry out starting up a project, and why?
o: Yes, because early prototypes help to show whether the project is viable before initiation is authorized.
Yes, because Kestrel Lane works iteratively and the project approach allows design work to begin early.
No, because starting up should do the minimum needed to decide whether initiation is worthwhile.
No, because the council's ICT team, not Kestrel Lane, should build any prototypes for the project.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Starting up a project is deliberately light: it does the minimum needed to decide whether there is a viable and worthwhile project to initiate, and it prevents resources being committed before that decision (see manual 13.1). Building prototypes is delivery work and should wait until the board has authorized it.

n.0: Viability at this point is judged from the outline business case and project brief, not from delivery work done before any authorization.
n.1: The project approach describes how the work will be delivered once authorized; it does not allow delivery to start before initiation.
n.3: Who builds the prototypes is not the problem: Kestrel Lane is the appointed supplier, but no delivery work should start before authorization.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The project brief and initiation stage plan for Permits Online have been sent to the board. Graham Pell, Ruth Abernethy and Siobhan Kerr each review them and agree by email that initiation should go ahead, without holding a meeting. Graham then emails Hannah Okoro a written instruction to start the six-week initiation stage. Is this an appropriate application of the 'authorize initiation' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the project manager may begin initiation as soon as the project brief is complete.
Yes, because all board members agreed and the executive gave the project manager a documented instruction.
No, because initiation must be authorized at a formal board meeting at which minutes are taken.
No, because the business layer, not the project board, authorizes the start of the initiation stage.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Authorize initiation can be done with or without a formal meeting, as long as all board members agree and the project manager receives a documented instruction from the executive (see manual 14.4.1).

n.0: The project manager needs the board's authority to initiate; completing the brief leads to the request, not the start.
n.2: A formal meeting is not required for this decision.
n.3: Authorizing initiation is a project board decision in directing a project; the business layer provides the mandate.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Permits Online is in the private beta stage. Tom Achebe's team asks whether residents without a council tax account should be able to apply for visitor vouchers online. The answer depends on how residents will use the service, and Hannah Okoro asks the board for guidance through the 'give ongoing direction' activity. Which role should be responsible for giving this user-related direction?
o: The executive.
The senior supplier.
The senior user.
Project assurance.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the recommended RACI for 'give ongoing direction', the senior user is responsible for user-related direction, with project assurance consulted (see manual 14.4.3 and table 14.2).

n.0: The executive gives direction on business matters such as justification and funding; user-related direction falls to the senior user.
n.1: The senior supplier directs on supplier and technical matters, not on how residents will use the service.
n.3: Project assurance is consulted and advises the board; it does not give the direction.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Permits Online is in the discovery and alpha stage. At a sprint review, Cllr Margaret Doyle, a member of the board, tells Tom Achebe's team to add a printable paper form to the online service for older residents, and the team starts work on it that afternoon. Hannah Okoro learns about it a week later. Is this an effective way for the board to direct the project, and why?
o: Yes, because individual board members may give ongoing direction at any time during a stage.
Yes, because the change helps residents without internet access, which ward councillors are worried about.
No, because Cllr Doyle is a councillor and so should not be a member of the project board.
No, because direction should go to the project manager, and new requirements go through issue control.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Board members, collectively or individually, give ongoing direction to the project manager rather than to the team; the team manager takes instructions from the project manager, and a new requirement is a request for change handled through the issue management approach (see manual 14.4.3 and 10.2.3).

n.0: Individual members can give direction, but to the project manager; instructing the team directly bypasses the project manager and change control.
n.1: The concern is valid, but a good idea still needs to be assessed against the baseline, the plan and the business case.
n.2: Being a councillor does not in itself rule her out of the board, and it is not why this way of directing is poor.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Permits Online is in the 'initiating a project' process. Hannah Okoro drafts the digital and data management approach from the council's data protection policy and security standards, and asks the waste collection app team what they learned about data confidentiality. She then uses the approaches to set up the project controls and the project plan. Is this an appropriate application of the 'agree the management approaches' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the digital and data management approach replaces the need for a risk management approach.
Yes, because the approaches draw on the council's policies and standards and on lessons from similar projects.
No, because the management approaches should be prepared after the project plan so that they match it.
No, because the digital and data management approach belongs to Kestrel Lane, which will host the service.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In 'agree the management approaches' the approaches are derived from the business's strategies, standards and practices that the project must comply with, lessons are sought from similar projects (including on data confidentiality), and once they are defined the project controls and project plan follow (see manual 15.4.2).

n.0: Each approach has its own purpose; managing data does not replace the procedures for managing risk.
n.2: The order is the reverse: the approaches are agreed first, and the controls and project plan follow.
n.3: The digital and data management approach is part of the PID and covers data across the project ecosystem, whoever hosts the service.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Permits Online is in the 'initiating a project' process. Hannah Okoro describes how residents' suggestions and problems found in testing will be captured, how their severity will be rated, and how changes to approved products will be assessed and decided. She also sets up a register for formal items of this kind. Which practice is being applied by the 'initiating a project' process?
o: Risk, because the register will hold uncertain events that may affect the project's objectives.
Issues, because an issue management approach and an issue register are being put in place.
Quality, because problems found in testing are results of quality control on the products.
Progress, because the register will be used to report status to the board at agreed intervals.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In initiating a project the issues practice is applied by developing the issue management approach, which sets out how issues are captured and how changes to the baseline are assessed and controlled, and by setting up the issue register (see manual table 15.3).

n.0: Problems already found and requested changes are issues, not uncertain future events.
n.2: Quality results are recorded in the quality register; capturing and deciding on issues and changes is the issues practice.
n.3: Progress reporting to the board uses highlight reports; the register described is for issues and changes.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Permits Online is in the 'initiating a project' process. Hannah Okoro proposes combining the communication and change management approaches into one short document, as the same people are affected by both, while writing a detailed digital and data management approach because of the council's very low appetite for data risk. The tailoring is recorded in the PID for the board to approve. Is this an effective way to carry out initiation, and why?
o: Yes, because management products can be merged or scaled, giving most detail where the risk is greatest.
Yes, because the change management approach and the issue management approach cover the same subject.
No, because each of the nine management approaches must be written as a separate document.
No, because tailoring decisions are made in starting up and cannot be changed during initiation.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Tailoring lets management products be merged, split or given different formats, and keeps controls proportionate to the project's scale, complexity and risk (see manual 2.7 and 15.4.1). Detail is placed where the business's appetite for risk is lowest, and the tailoring is documented in the PID for approval.

n.1: The change management approach covers organizational transition and the issue management approach covers change control; they are different subjects.
n.2: Management products can be merged or combined; there is no requirement for nine separate documents.
n.3: Tailoring requirements are agreed in initiating a project, in 'agree the tailoring requirements', and can be revisited at stage boundaries.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'starting up a project' process. With Hamish Grant, Leah Whitfield compares three ways of delivering the centre: the estates team managing separate trade contracts, a traditional design-then-build contract, and the architect's design followed by a design-and-build contract. She recommends the last, with the college as a relatively thick client, and records the reasons in the project brief. Is this an appropriate application of the 'select the project approach' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because this activity decides how the work will be delivered, such as in-house or by third parties, before initiation.
Yes, because the project approach is first set out in the PID, which the board approves when it authorizes the project.
No, because the procurement route belongs in the commercial management approach, which is written in initiation.
No, because choosing the delivery method is a decision the project board takes in 'authorize initiation'.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: 'Select the project approach' decides how the work will be approached, for example in-house or through third parties, build or buy, and which delivery method, so that alternatives are evaluated before initiation and recorded in the project brief (see manual 13.4.5).

n.1: The project approach is selected in starting up and recorded in the project brief; it is not first set out in the PID.
n.2: The commercial management approach later details procurement procedures, but the choice of delivery approach is made in starting up.
n.3: The board approves the project brief in 'authorize initiation'; evaluating and selecting the approach is work done in starting up.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'starting up a project' process. Acting for the college's leadership, which forms the business layer, Dr Elaine Fairbairn has asked Mark Ostrowski to be the executive. Mark is now agreeing Leah Whitfield's fixed-term appointment as project manager. Using the recommended RACI for 'appoint the executive and the project manager', which statement is correct?
o: Mark Ostrowski, as executive, is accountable, and Leah Whitfield, as project manager, is responsible.
The project board is accountable, and the business layer, here Dr Fairbairn, is consulted.
The business layer, here Dr Fairbairn, is responsible, and the governors are accountable.
The business layer, here Dr Fairbairn, is accountable, and Mark Ostrowski, as executive, is responsible.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the recommended RACI for 'appoint the executive and the project manager', the business layer is accountable and the executive is responsible; the project manager then manages the project day to day on the executive's behalf (see manual 13.4.1 and table 13.2).

n.0: The executive is responsible for this activity rather than accountable, and the business layer is accountable.
n.1: The project board is not yet formed; the business layer is accountable for these appointments.
n.2: The executive, not the business layer, is responsible for the activity; the business layer is accountable.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'starting up a project' process. Because the opening date cannot move, Mark Ostrowski asks Leah Whitfield to use starting up to prepare a full cost plan, a detailed risk register and the full business case, so that the board can authorize the whole project in one step. Starting up is now planned to take ten weeks. Is this an effective way to carry out starting up a project, and why?
o: Yes, because detailed work in starting up reduces the risk of missing the fixed opening date.
Yes, because the board can authorize initiation and the project together when the end date is fixed.
No, because starting up should do the minimum needed to decide whether initiation is worthwhile.
No, because the cost plan and risk register should be prepared by project assurance, not the project manager.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Starting up a project answers whether there is a viable and worthwhile project; it is a lighter process than initiation, doing the minimum necessary to decide whether initiation is worthwhile and to prevent poorly conceived projects being initiated (see manual 13.1). The full business case and detailed plans are prepared in initiating a project.

n.0: Detailed planning belongs in initiation, after the board has confirmed that initiation is worthwhile; starting up stays light.
n.1: Authorizing initiation and authorizing the project are separate decisions in directing a project, whatever the deadline.
n.3: Project assurance reviews for the board; it does not prepare the project's plans and registers.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the asbestos removal, strip-out and structural works stage. The contractor offers to work on Saturdays at no extra cost to recover four days lost to bad weather, but site traffic would then pass the campus on Saturday enrichment days. Leah Whitfield asks the board for advice. Mark Ostrowski consults Sunita Rao by phone and confirms the board's view to Leah in writing the same day. Is this an appropriate application of the 'give ongoing direction' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the executive can approve changes to the stage plan without involving the other board members.
Yes, because board members can give informal guidance in answer to requests for advice at any time in a stage.
No, because the board should give direction at stage boundaries, through its response to the end stage report.
No, because advice from the board has to be agreed at a formal meeting attended by all of its members.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: 'Give ongoing direction' lets the board, collectively or through individual members, give informal guidance and respond to requests for advice at any time during the project (see manual 14.4.3).

n.0: No change to the stage plan is being approved; Mark is responding to a request for advice, after consulting the senior user.
n.2: Ongoing direction can be given at any time during a stage, not only at stage boundaries.
n.3: Ongoing direction can be given informally, collectively or by individual board members.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is at the end of the detailed design and procurement stage. The board is reviewing the end stage report and the plan for stage 3, which includes signing the design-and-build contract. Using the recommended RACI for 'authorize a stage or exception plan', which statement is correct?
o: The executive is accountable, and the project manager is informed of the decision.
The project board as a whole is accountable, and the business layer is informed.
The business layer is accountable, and the executive is consulted on the decision.
The project manager is accountable, and the senior user and project assurance are informed.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the recommended RACI for 'authorize a stage or exception plan', the executive is accountable and responsible, the senior user and project assurance are consulted, and the project manager is informed (see manual 14.4.4 and table 14.2).

n.1: The RACI makes the executive, as the single point of accountability, accountable for this decision.
n.2: Authorizing a stage is a project board decision, with the executive accountable; the business layer is not accountable for it.
n.3: The project manager prepares the plan but is informed of the decision; the senior user and project assurance are consulted.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Leah Whitfield submits the project initiation documentation for authorization. The board approves the full business case, the project plan and the other management approaches, but says it will look at the benefits management approach at closure, as apprentices will not start until the centre opens. Is this an effective way to carry out directing a project, and why?
o: Yes, because benefits are realized after the project, so how they are measured is planned in closing a project.
Yes, because the senior user specifies the benefits and so is the one who approves the benefits management approach.
No, because 'authorize the project' includes reviewing how and when the benefits will be measured and confirmed.
No, because the board should carry out the benefits reviews itself before it authorizes the first delivery stage.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In 'authorize the project' the board confirms that the business case shows a viable project, approves the PID and reviews the benefits management approach, so that it knows how benefits will be measured and confirmed (see manual 14.4.2 and table 14.3).

n.0: The benefits management approach is updated in closing, but it is created in initiation and reviewed when the project is authorized.
n.1: The senior user specifies the benefits, but the benefits management approach is reviewed and approved by the board in directing a project when it authorizes the project.
n.3: Benefits reviews take place mainly after closure; at authorization the board reviews how they will be done.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'initiating a project' process. While assembling the project initiation documentation, Leah Whitfield cross-checks the project plan against the business case and the grant agreement. She finds that the planned spending profile would leave £600,000 of grant unclaimed by 31 March of the second year, and revises the plan before requesting authorization. Is this an appropriate application of the 'assemble the project initiation documentation' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the parts are checked for consistency before the version used for authorization is baselined.
Yes, because grant claims are a project benefit and so must be recorded in the benefits management approach.
No, because the project plan is fixed before the PID is assembled and can then change through change control.
No, because the business case should be adjusted to fit the project plan rather than the other way round.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In 'assemble the project initiation documentation' the project manager cross-checks the elements for compatibility; the version used to gain authorization is then baselined and placed under change control (see manual 15.4.6).

n.1: Grant income is funding, not a benefit of the centre; the point is that the PID's parts must be consistent.
n.2: The PID is not baselined until it is authorized; inconsistencies found while assembling it are fixed before then.
n.3: Either part may need to change; what matters is that they are compatible, and here the plan was at fault.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mark Ostrowski is the executive and Leah Whitfield the project manager. The outline business case is being developed into the full business case, using costs from the project plan and the risks in the project log. Using the recommended RACI for 'prepare the full business case', which statement is correct?
o: Dr Elaine Fairbairn, as the business layer, is accountable, and Mark Ostrowski is responsible.
Mark Ostrowski is accountable, Leah Whitfield is responsible and project assurance is consulted.
Leah Whitfield is accountable, and Hamish Grant, who prepares the cost plans, is responsible.
The project board is accountable, and Mark Ostrowski and Sunita Rao are jointly responsible.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the recommended RACI for 'prepare the full business case', the executive is accountable, the project manager is responsible, project assurance is consulted and the business layer is not involved (see manual 15.4.5 and table 15.2).

n.0: The business layer is not involved in this activity; the executive is accountable and the project manager responsible.
n.2: The project manager is responsible, not accountable; the executive is accountable for the business case.
n.3: The executive alone is accountable, and the project manager prepares the business case on the executive's behalf.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'initiating a project' process. To save time, Mark Ostrowski proposes not writing a communication management approach: the governors already receive the college's monthly finance report, and Leah Whitfield can tell other people about the project as the need arises. Is this an effective way to carry out initiating a project, and why?
o: Yes, because tailoring allows management products to be merged with reports the college already uses.
Yes, because highlight reports will tell all stakeholders about progress at a frequency agreed by the board.
No, because each management approach has to be a separate document that the board reviews and approves on its own.
No, because stakeholders from governors to students have distinct needs, so how and when to communicate must be agreed.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In 'agree the management approaches' the communication management approach defines the means and frequency of communication with, and feedback from, the project ecosystem (see manual 15.4.2 and 3.4). Here the governors want safety reports, the finance committee wants immediate overspend warnings, and students and employers are affected, so communication cannot be left to chance.

n.0: Products can be merged or reformatted, but the governors' finance report does not cover the project's other stakeholders' needs.
n.1: Highlight reports go to the board; they do not reach students, employers or the combined authority.
n.2: Management approaches can be combined or tailored; the problem is that communication would not be planned at all.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The SPA project is in the 'starting up a project' process. Ellie Chandran and Karen Lindqvist, the executive, compare buying a new referral system with switching on the unused referral module, which Medivault would configure under its existing support contract. They also decide that the trust's own staff will design the SPA and that it will be piloted in one locality before roll-out. Is this an appropriate application of the 'select the project approach' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because it decides how the work will be delivered, such as buy or configure and in-house or supplier, before initiation.
Yes, because selecting the approach confirms that the business case shows a viable project for the board.
No, because the project approach is chosen in initiating a project, once the project plan has been prepared.
No, because the supplier must be chosen through the commercial management approach before an approach is selected.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Selecting the project approach decides how the work will be approached, for example in-house or by third parties, building or buying, and the delivery method, so that initiation can be planned on that basis (see manual 13.4.5).

n.1: Viability is confirmed by the board when it authorizes the project on the full business case, not by selecting an approach.
n.2: The project approach is selected in starting up and recorded in the project brief; the project plan prepared in initiation builds on it.
