n.3: The commercial management approach is agreed in initiation; the broad choice of how to deliver comes first, in starting up.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The SPA project is in the 'starting up a project' process. The trust's executive team names Karen Lindqvist as executive, and Karen then appoints Ellie Chandran as project manager, using a role description that Karen drafted herself. Which role is accountable for the 'appoint the executive and the project manager' activity, and why?
o: The business layer, because it commissions the project and answers for these first appointments.
The executive, because Karen chose the project manager and wrote her role description herself.
The project board, because it will direct the project manager once the project is authorized.
The senior user, because the project manager will be delivering a new service for the users.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the starting up a project RACI, the business layer is accountable for appointing the executive and the project manager, and the executive is responsible for carrying the activity out (see manual 13.4.1).

n.1: Karen is responsible for the activity, but accountability sits with the business layer that commissions the project.
n.2: The project board does not yet exist; its members are appointed later in starting up.
n.3: Accountability for these appointments rests with the business layer; the senior user is appointed later, with the rest of the project management team.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The SPA project is in the 'starting up a project' process. Keen to impress the commissioner, Ellie Chandran spends ten weeks drawing up detailed rotas, a full cost model and product descriptions for every SPA product before asking the board for authority to initiate the project. Is this an effective way to carry out the starting up a project process, and why?
o: Yes, because the trust's low appetite for clinical safety risk means detailed plans are needed before any decision.
Yes, because a full cost model lets the board authorize the whole project at the end of starting up.
No, because starting up should do the minimum needed to decide whether the project is worth initiating.
No, because detailed planning of the SPA products is the senior supplier's job rather than the project manager's.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Starting up a project is lighter than initiation: it does the minimum necessary to decide whether initiation is worthwhile and to stop poorly conceived projects starting (see manual 13.1). Detailed products and plans belong to initiation and the later stages.

n.0: Safety-critical detail is planned and assured in initiation and the design stage; the decision at the end of starting up needs an outline, not detailed rotas.
n.1: At the end of starting up the board authorizes initiation, not the whole project; the project is authorized on the full business case after initiation.
n.3: The project manager prepares plans and product descriptions; the senior supplier commits supplier resources and is accountable for supplier products.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The SPA project is at the end of its final stage. The board reviews the end project report and checks that the updated benefits management approach plans reviews of referral times, lost referrals and unnecessary visits after closure, including whether nursing teams' loss of control over referrals has had unexpected effects. It then notifies the trust's executive team that the project is closing. Is this an appropriate application of the 'authorize project closure' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the board carries out the post-project benefits reviews itself once the project has closed.
Yes, because the board makes sure post-project reviews will cover the service in use, including side-effects.
No, because the benefits reviews should be completed by the project before the board authorizes closure.
No, because the closure notification should be sent by the project manager once the end project report is ready.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In authorizing project closure the board confirms closure, makes sure post-project benefits reviews are planned in the updated benefits management approach and will cover performance in operational use, including beneficial and adverse side-effects, and notifies the business layer (see manual 14.4.5).

n.0: Post-project benefits reviews are carried out by the business after the project has closed, not by the project board.
n.2: Most benefits are realized after closure; the project plans the reviews but does not carry them out.
n.3: The closure notification to the business layer is issued by the board in directing a project.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The SPA project is in the Eastfield pilot stage. Before each board meeting, Karen Lindqvist, the executive, and Moira Healy, the senior user, compare the figures in Ellie Chandran's highlight report with data from the referral module, to be sure the report gives a fair picture of the stage. Which practice is the board applying in directing a project, and why?
o: Quality, because the board is checking that a management product meets its quality specification.
Organizing, because checking the project manager's work is part of the board's assurance role.
Risk, because inaccurate reporting is a threat to the board's ability to control the stage.
Progress, because the board is making sure that progress reporting to it is fair and reliable.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In directing a project, the progress practice is applied when the board assures itself of fair reporting by validating highlight and end stage reports (see manual table 14.3).

n.0: Quality concerns the project's products and their specifications; validating progress reports applies the progress practice.
n.1: Assurance is a board responsibility set up under organizing, but checking that progress reports are fair applies the progress practice.
n.2: Unreliable reporting might create risk, but the action is validating reports, which applies the progress practice.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The SPA project is in the design and pilot preparation stage. Because Ellie Chandran is new to PRINCE2 7, the board decides to meet every week, review every work package before Ellie authorizes it and approve each change to the draft rotas. Is this an effective way to carry out the directing a project process, and why?
o: Yes, because a project manager new to PRINCE2 7 needs the board to approve her work packages until she is trained.
Yes, because giving ongoing direction allows the board to take part in the project's decisions whenever it wishes.
No, because the board should not meet during a stage and should review the project at stage boundaries.
No, because the board should leave day-to-day management to the project manager and control the stage by exception.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Directing a project lets the board stay accountable while delegating day-to-day management to the project manager; it manages by exception through stage tolerances, highlight reports and exception reports (see manual 14.1 and 14.4.3). Concern about inexperience is better met by more frequent reporting and stronger assurance than by taking over the project manager's decisions.

n.0: Authorizing work packages is a project manager activity in controlling a stage; the board can ask for more frequent reports and stronger assurance instead.
n.1: Ongoing direction is guidance and responses to requests or exceptions; it does not mean the board makes day-to-day decisions.
n.2: The board can give ongoing direction and respond to exception reports during a stage; it is not limited to stage boundaries.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The SPA project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Ellie Chandran agrees with the board that it will receive a fortnightly online highlight report and make its decisions at the end of each stage, and she sets out how she will control the team managers' work through work packages and checkpoint reports. Is this an appropriate application of the 'establish project controls' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because establishing controls lets the board set the project's cost and time tolerances.
Yes, because it agrees the board's level of control after initiation and how the team managers' work is controlled.
No, because project controls are set in each delivery stage plan rather than during initiation.
No, because reporting arrangements belong in the communication management approach, agreed in starting up.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Establishing project controls agrees the level of control the board needs after initiation and the mechanism for it, and how the project manager will control the team managers' work (see manual 15.4.3).

n.0: Project tolerances are set by the business layer, here the trust's executive team; the board sets stage tolerances.
n.2: Project controls are agreed in initiation for the whole project; stage plans then apply them.
n.3: The communication management approach is agreed in initiation, not starting up, and it does not replace agreeing the board's controls.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The SPA project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Ellie Chandran updates the outline business case with the time and cost figures from the project plan and the aggregated risks from the project log, and asks for the views of Neil Ashworth, who carries out business assurance. Which role is accountable for the 'prepare the full business case' activity, and why?
o: The project manager, because Ellie is preparing the full business case from the project plan.
The executive, because the executive is accountable for the business case on behalf of the business.
The business layer, because the commissioner's transformation money is funding the project.
Project assurance, because Neil Ashworth reviews the business case independently for the board.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the initiating a project RACI, the project manager is responsible for preparing the full business case, the executive is accountable, project assurance is consulted and the business layer is not involved (see manual 15.4.5).

n.0: Ellie is responsible for doing the work; accountability rests with the executive.
n.2: The business layer is not involved in this activity, whatever the source of the funding.
n.3: Project assurance is consulted on the full business case; it is not accountable for it.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The SPA project is in the 'initiating a project' process. In the draft digital and data management approach, Ellie Chandran states that, to win over doubtful Moorside GP practices, weekly pilot referral data including patient details will be emailed to them as spreadsheets. The trust allows patient data to be shared through approved systems and no other way. Is this an effective way to carry out the initiating a project process, and why?
o: Yes, because sharing pilot results is a good way to win support from practices that doubt the SPA.
Yes, because the digital and data management approach belongs to the progress practice and covers reporting.
No, because the approach should set out how data will be kept secure, in line with the trust's rules on sharing.
No, because sharing information with GP practices should be covered in the communication management approach.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Agreeing the management approaches draws on the business's policies and standards; the digital and data management approach sets out how data will be created, used and managed, including how it is kept secure and private (see manual 15.4.2 and chapter 11). Emailing patient-level spreadsheets breaks the trust's rule that patient data is shared through approved systems.

n.0: Winning support matters, but not by a method that breaks the trust's data rules.
n.1: The approach does sit in the progress practice, but it must still set out how data is kept secure, which this plan fails to do.
n.3: The communication management approach plans communication with stakeholders, but how patient data is handled and kept secure belongs in the digital and data management approach.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'starting up a project' process. Nadia Osei compares ways of delivering the range: making all six recipes in-house after adding pan-frying equipment, or using a co-manufacturer for the two pan-fried recipes; buying a new tray-sealing line or adapting an old one; and developing recipes in fixed phases or in two-week cycles with tastings. She recommends a hybrid approach using Greendale and a new line. Is this an appropriate application of the 'select the project approach' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because it decides how the work will be done: in-house or by third parties, build or buy, and the delivery method.
Yes, because the choice of suppliers is recorded in the project plan, which is baselined when initiation is authorized.
No, because the project approach is agreed in initiation as one of the nine management approaches.
No, because choosing co-manufacturers and equipment suppliers is a commercial decision for the business layer.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Selecting the project approach in starting up decides how the work will be approached, for example in-house or through third parties, building or buying, and the delivery method (see manual 13.4.5). Comparing these options before initiation gives the board a sound basis for authorizing initiation.

n.1: The project plan is prepared in initiation and baselined when the project is authorized; the project approach is selected earlier, in starting up.
n.2: The nine management approaches (risk, quality, issue and so on) are agreed in initiation; the project approach is a different product, selected in starting up.
n.3: The business layer commissions the project and sets its constraints; deciding how the work will be delivered is part of starting up the project.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'starting up a project' process. Imogen Fairley, who commissioned the project, has appointed Rob Hennessy as executive and Nadia Osei as project manager. The senior users, the senior supplier and the people who will provide project assurance now need to be chosen and appointed. Which role should be responsible for the 'appoint the project management team' activity?
o: The business layer, represented by Imogen Fairley.
The project manager, Nadia Osei.
The executive, Rob Hennessy.
The project board, acting together.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the recommended RACI for 'appoint the project management team', the executive is responsible for making the appointments and the business layer is accountable; the project manager is not involved (see manual 13.4.4 and table 13.2).

n.0: Imogen, as the business layer, is accountable for the appointments, but the executive carries them out.
n.1: The project manager is not involved in appointing the project management team.
n.3: The board does not yet exist as a whole; its members are being appointed through this activity, which the executive carries out.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'starting up a project' process. To be thorough, Nadia Osei spends eight weeks preparing detailed recipe specifications, running full tenders with three line suppliers and producing a week-by-week plan for every stage before she requests project initiation. The launch week is eleven months away. Is this an effective way to carry out the 'starting up a project' process, and why?
o: Yes, because detailed specifications stop time being wasted in initiation on unsound assumptions.
Yes, because the fixed launch week makes it important to finish as much planning as possible early.
No, because the tenders should be run by the business layer before the project mandate is issued.
No, because starting up should do the minimum needed to decide whether initiation is worthwhile.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Starting up is a lighter process than initiation: it does the minimum necessary to decide whether the project is viable and worthwhile enough to initiate (see manual 13.1). Detailed specifications, tenders and full planning belong in initiation and later stages; spending eight weeks of an eleven-month timetable before initiation even starts puts the fixed launch week at risk.

n.0: Starting up should check key assumptions, but it does so at outline level, not through detailed specifications and tenders.
n.1: The fixed date makes time precious, so starting up should be quick; detailed planning is done in initiation and stage by stage.
n.2: The mandate comes from the business layer, but procuring suppliers is project work, carried out once the project is under way.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'directing a project' process. The three board members, Rob Hennessy, Charlotte Vane and Dariusz Nowicki, each review the project brief and the initiation stage plan by email, and all agree that initiation should go ahead. Rob, the executive, then emails Nadia Osei a written instruction to start initiation. Is this an appropriate application of the 'authorize initiation' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the executive holds the authority to start initiation without consulting the other members.
Yes, because initiation can be authorized without a meeting if all members agree and the executive instructs in writing.
No, because authorizing initiation requires a formal board meeting to approve the project initiation documentation.
No, because the business layer must approve the initiation stage plan before any initiation work starts.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: 'Authorize initiation' reviews and approves the project brief and the initiation stage plan. It can be done with or without a formal meeting, as long as all board members agree and the project manager receives a documented instruction from the executive (see manual 14.4.1).

n.0: Authorizing initiation is a board decision; it could be done without a meeting here because all members agreed, with the executive then giving the written instruction.
n.2: The project initiation documentation is approved later, in 'authorize the project'; this activity approves the brief and the initiation stage plan, and no meeting is required.
n.3: The project board, not the business layer, approves the initiation stage plan in 'authorize initiation'.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'directing a project' process at the end of the development stage. Nadia Osei has submitted the end stage report and the trials stage plan, and the board is deciding whether to authorize the trials stage. Rob Hennessy is the executive and Charlotte Vane is a senior user. Which role should be accountable for this decision in the 'authorize a stage or exception plan' activity?
o: The project manager, Nadia Osei.
The senior user, Charlotte Vane.
Project assurance.
The executive, Rob Hennessy.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the recommended RACI for 'authorize a stage or exception plan', the executive is accountable (and responsible), the senior user and project assurance are consulted, and the project manager is informed (see manual 14.4.4 and table 14.2).

n.0: The project manager prepares the plan and is informed of the decision; she is not accountable for it.
n.1: The senior user is consulted on the decision; accountability rests with the executive.
n.2: Project assurance is consulted and advises the board; it is not accountable.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the concept and recipe stage. The directors, used to running the factory hands-on, ask Nadia Osei to attend a weekly board meeting where they review every tasting result and approve each change to the work packages, even though the stage is forecast to finish within its tolerances. Is this an effective way to carry out the 'directing a project' process, and why?
o: Yes, because closer involvement helps directors who are new to projects learn how the project is run.
Yes, because the board is accountable for the project's success, so it should approve each change.
No, because the board should make key decisions and manage by exception, leaving day-to-day control to Nadia.
No, because the weekly meetings should be replaced by daily checkpoint reports sent directly to the board.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Directing a project lets the board be accountable through key decisions and overall control while delegating day-to-day management to the project manager; the board manages by exception and is not burdened with routine control (see manual 14.1 and 14.3). Approving work package changes within tolerance is the project manager's job in controlling a stage.

n.0: Learning is valuable, but it can come from briefings or coaching without the board taking over day-to-day control.
n.1: The board's accountability is exercised through decision points and tolerances, not by approving every change.
n.3: Checkpoint reports go from team managers to the project manager; the board receives highlight reports.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'initiating a project' process. Before asking the board to authorize the project, Nadia Osei checks the parts of the project initiation documentation against each other. She finds that the project plan allows twelve weeks of trials, but the line delivery date in the commercial management approach and the supplier's contract leaves five. She resolves the conflict with Dariusz Nowicki before the PID is submitted. Is this an appropriate application of the 'assemble the project initiation documentation' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the elements of the PID should be cross-checked for consistency before it is baselined.
Yes, because the commercial management approach takes precedence over the project plan when they conflict.
No, because conflicts between products should be raised as issues and resolved after the PID is approved.
No, because the line delivery date is a matter for the operations director, not for the initiation documentation.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Assembling the PID includes cross-checking its elements for compatibility; the version used to gain authorization is then baselined and placed under change control (see manual 15.4.6). Finding the clash between the trials time and the line delivery date now avoids baselining an unworkable plan.

n.1: No management product takes precedence by default; the conflict has to be resolved so that both are consistent.
n.2: Resolving known conflicts before approval is the point of cross-checking; baselining a known inconsistency would push it into change control for no reason.
n.3: The line delivery date is a key planning constraint and must be shown consistently in the PID; the operations director's preference does not take it out of the project's control.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'initiating a project' process. Nadia Osei creates a product breakdown structure for the whole launch, a work breakdown structure that groups the work into packages for the chefs, Mint and Tallow, Greendale and the line supplier, and a product flow diagram showing the order in which the products are needed. Which practice is being applied?
o: Organizing
Plans
Quality
Progress
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Developing the product breakdown structure, the work breakdown structure and the product flow diagram is how the plans practice is applied in initiating a project (see manual table 15.3, and product-based planning in 7.3.1).

n.0: The work breakdown structure helps decide team structure, but producing these planning products applies the plans practice; organizing in initiation updates the project management team structure.
n.2: Quality in initiation is applied through the quality management approach and quality specifications, not the breakdown structures.
n.3: Progress in initiation concerns the project controls and reporting arrangements, not the breakdown of products and work.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Fernhollow Kitchen has just been authorized for initiation. Worried about the fixed launch week, Rob Hennessy tells Megan Cho's chefs to start the two-week recipe cycles and asks the design agency to begin branding work straight away, while Nadia Osei writes the project initiation documentation over the next four weeks. Is this an effective way to carry out the 'initiating a project' process, and why?
o: Yes, because iterative recipe and design work produces learning that will improve the initiation documentation.
Yes, because the executive is accountable for the project and can start delivery when time is short.
No, because the design agency's contract should be signed by the business layer before any work starts.
No, because delivery work and spending should wait until the board has authorized the project on solid foundations.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Initiating a project establishes solid foundations so that the business understands the work needed before committing significant expenditure; delivery starts once the board authorizes the project (see manual 15.1 and 14.4.2). Starting the chefs and the agency now commits money and effort before the plan, business case and controls are agreed.

n.0: Early learning can be useful, but committing delivery resources before authorization bypasses the board's decision point.
n.1: The executive is accountable, but authorizing the project is a board decision in directing a project, made on the PID.
n.2: Contracting is handled through the commercial management approach agreed in initiation; the problem is starting delivery before the project is authorized.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'starting up a project' process. Because race day cannot move, Kezia Oduya wants to save time. She proposes to send the board the project brief and to begin initiation as soon as it agrees, explaining the six weeks of initiation work as she goes rather than preparing an initiation stage plan. Is this an appropriate application of the 'plan the initiation stage' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the fixed race date means that any time saved in initiation can be used in the build-up stage.
Yes, because six weeks is short enough for the board to follow initiation through Kezia's highlight reports.
No, because initiation uses time and resources, so it should be planned and approved to avoid aimless work.
No, because the initiation stage plan is prepared in the 'managing a stage boundary' process, not here.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Initiating a project takes time and consumes resources, so the work is planned and approved to make sure initiation is not aimless and unstructured; starting up a project is not complete without the initiation stage plan (see manual 13.4.7 and 13.4.8).

n.0: The fixed date makes efficient initiation important, but an unplanned initiation is more likely to waste time than save it.
n.1: Highlight reports report against a stage plan; without an initiation stage plan there is nothing to control initiation against.
n.3: The initiation stage plan is the one stage plan produced in starting up a project; later stage plans are prepared at stage boundaries.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'starting up a project' process. The cabinet gave the mandate to Andrew Mallory, who has been appointed executive. Andrew is now choosing the other members of the project board and agreeing their role descriptions, including inviting Greg Halloran to represent Paceline. Which role is accountable for the 'appoint the project management team' activity?
o: The business layer, represented here by the council's cabinet
The executive, Andrew Mallory, who is choosing the members
The project manager, Kezia Oduya, who will lead the team
The senior supplier, Greg Halloran, who commits Paceline's staff
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the recommended RACI for 'appoint the project management team', the business layer is accountable and the executive is responsible; the project manager is not involved (see manual 13.4.4 and table 13.2). The cabinet commissioned the project, so it is the business layer here.

n.1: Andrew Mallory carries out the appointments, which makes him responsible; accountability sits with the business layer.
n.2: The project manager is not involved in appointing the project management team.
n.3: Greg Halloran is being appointed; he has no RACI role in making the appointments.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'starting up a project' process. Before asking the board for authority to initiate, Andrew Mallory asks Kezia Oduya to have Paceline produce a detailed course design, a full rota for 1,200 volunteers and a draft event safety plan, so that the board knows exactly what it is approving. This will take about three months. Is this an effective way to carry out starting up a project, and why?
o: Yes, because detailed products reduce the risk that the safety advisory group rejects the event later on.
Yes, because the board needs a full business case and detailed plans before it can authorize initiation.
No, because the course design and the volunteer rota are Zara Quinn's responsibility rather than Paceline's.
No, because starting up should do the minimum needed to decide whether initiation is worthwhile.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Starting up a project asks whether there is a viable and worthwhile project; it is a lighter process than initiation and does the minimum necessary to decide whether initiation is worth the investment (see manual 13.1). Three months of detailed delivery work before initiation is authorized is far more than this, and eats into a fixed timescale.

n.0: Reducing safety risk matters, but detailed delivery products belong in later stages after the project is authorized, not before initiation.
n.1: The board authorizes initiation on the project brief, with an outline business case, and the initiation stage plan; the full business case comes from initiation.
n.2: Course design is Paceline's contracted work; in any case the problem is doing detailed work too early, not who does it.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The project brief and the initiation stage plan for the Carrowford Half Marathon have been sent to the three board members. As their diaries make a meeting difficult, Andrew Mallory asks each member by email whether they are content. All three agree, and Andrew then sends Kezia Oduya a written instruction to begin initiation. Is this an appropriate application of the 'authorize initiation' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the executive can authorize initiation on his own once he has read the project brief.
Yes, because all board members agreed and the executive gave Kezia a documented instruction to begin.
No, because the brief and the initiation stage plan should be approved at a formal meeting of the board.
No, because initiation should be authorized by the cabinet, which issued the project mandate.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Authorize initiation can be done with or without a formal meeting, as long as all board members agree and the project manager receives a documented instruction from the executive (see manual 14.4.1). Both conditions are met here.

n.0: The decision is the board's, so all members must agree; the executive's documented instruction confirms it.
n.2: A formal meeting is not required for this activity when all members agree and the executive documents the instruction.
n.3: The cabinet, as the business layer, issued the mandate; the project board authorizes initiation in directing a project.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon planning and approvals stage is ending. Kezia Oduya has submitted the end stage report and the build-up stage plan, and the board is reviewing them in the 'authorize a stage or exception plan' activity. According to the recommended RACI, how is the project manager involved in this activity?
o: Responsible for the activity
Accountable for the activity
Consulted during the activity
Informed of the outcome
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the recommended RACI for 'authorize a stage or exception plan', the executive is accountable and responsible, the senior user and project assurance are consulted, and the project manager is informed (see manual table 14.2).

n.0: The executive is responsible for this activity; the project manager prepared the inputs in managing a stage boundary.
n.1: The executive is accountable; this is a board decision.
n.2: The senior user and project assurance are consulted; the project manager is informed of the decision.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the build-up stage. After a news story about medical cover at another race, Andrew Mallory phones Lisa Ventnor directly and tells her to add four more medical posts on the course. Lisa's team starts the work, and Kezia Oduya finds out a week later from the stage budget figures. Is this an effective way to carry out directing a project, and why?
o: Yes, because board members may give direction at any time, either collectively or individually.
Yes, because the executive is accountable for the project, including the safety of those taking part.
No, because the board should direct through the project manager, who instructs team managers.
No, because extra medical posts change the safety plan, which the safety advisory group should decide.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Directing a project lets the board stay accountable while delegating day-to-day management to the project manager; the board is not involved in managing product delivery, and team managers take their instructions from the project manager through work packages (see manual 14.1, 14.3 and 17.4.2). Direction should have gone to Kezia.

n.0: Ongoing direction can come from individual board members, but it is given to the project manager, not straight to a team manager.
n.1: The executive is accountable, but that does not mean bypassing the project manager to instruct suppliers' teams.
n.3: The safety advisory group approves the event safety plan, but the problem here is the board bypassing the project manager.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Kezia Oduya drafts the sustainability management approach from the council's targets for major events: refill stations instead of bottles, 70% of waste recycled, free buses for runners and a carbon report within two months. She also asks two other cities how their races met similar targets. Is this an appropriate application of the 'agree the management approaches' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the approaches draw on business standards the project must meet and on lessons from similar projects.
Yes, because the sustainability management approach is where the business layer sets out its environmental policy.
No, because sustainability targets are recorded in the business case, so a separate approach is not needed.
No, because the management approaches should be agreed in starting up a project, before the brief is approved.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: The management approaches are derived from business strategies, standards and practices the project must comply with and from users' expectations, and lessons from similar projects are sought when agreeing them (see manual 15.4.2). The council's event targets and other cities' experience are exactly these inputs.

n.1: The approach describes how the project will achieve its sustainability targets; the business's own policy is an input to it, not its content.
n.2: Sustainability targets and tolerances are documented in the sustainability management approach, which supports the business case.
n.3: The management approaches are agreed during initiation; starting up produces the project brief.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Andrew Mallory is the executive, Kezia Oduya is the project manager and Bernadette Lowe has been appointed to provide business assurance. Which describes the recommended RACI for the 'prepare the full business case' activity?
o: Andrew responsible, Kezia accountable, Bernadette consulted
Kezia responsible, Andrew accountable, Bernadette consulted
Kezia responsible and accountable, Bernadette informed
Andrew responsible, the cabinet accountable, Kezia consulted
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: For 'prepare the full business case' the project manager is responsible, the executive is accountable, project assurance is consulted and the business layer is not involved (see manual 15.4.5 and table 15.2).

n.0: The roles are reversed: the project manager prepares the business case and the executive is accountable for it.
n.2: The executive is accountable for the business case; the project manager cannot hold that accountability, and assurance is consulted.
n.3: The business layer is not involved in this activity, and the project manager prepares the full business case.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'initiating a project' process. Kezia Oduya hears that grandstand prices will rise next month. She proposes signing a £180,000 contract for grandstands and barriers now, two weeks before she asks the board to authorize the project, so that the lower price is secured. Is this an effective way to carry out initiating a project, and why?
o: Yes, because the fixed race date makes early booking essential, and initiation can include urgent delivery work.
Yes, because a lower price improves the business case, which the board reviews when it authorizes the project.
No, because infrastructure is booked in the event week stage, close to when it will be used on race day.
No, because initiation should lay solid foundations before significant spending is committed to the project.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Initiating a project establishes solid foundations so that the business understands the work needed before committing to significant expenditure (see manual 15.1). Committing £180,000 before the board has authorized the project bypasses that decision point.

n.0: The fixed date is a real pressure, but delivery spending waits for the board to authorize the project.
n.1: A saving may help the business case, but the board has not yet decided whether the project should go ahead.
n.2: In this plan infrastructure is booked in the build-up stage; in any case the issue is committing money before authorization.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Project Skyline is in the 'starting up a project' process. Mairi Campbell works with Steven Clarke and Nicola Graham to compare moving applications unchanged with redesigning them for the cloud, and in-house delivery with using a partner. Drawing on the lesson from the society's earlier fixed-scope contract dispute, they recommend using Stratoshift under its framework contract, with work agreed one package at a time, and migrating in waves. Is this an appropriate application of the 'select the project approach' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because it decides how the work will be delivered, including the use of third parties and the delivery method.
Yes, because the chosen approach removes the need to compare business options in the outline business case.
No, because the project approach is agreed in initiation as one of the management approaches.
No, because choosing a supplier belongs to the commercial management approach, which is agreed after authorization.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In 'select the project approach' the project manager decides how the work will be approached, for example in-house or through third parties, build or buy, and which delivery method to use, so that initiation starts on a sound basis (see manual 13.4.5). Using lessons from the earlier dispute strengthens the choice.

n.1: The project approach is about how to deliver; the outline business case still compares the business options to justify the investment.
n.2: The project approach is selected in starting up a project and included in the project brief; the management approaches are agreed later, in initiation.
n.3: The commercial management approach is agreed in initiation, before the project is authorized, and it builds on the project approach chosen in starting up.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Project Skyline is in the 'starting up a project' process. The society's board has given the mandate to Fraser McIntyre, who will be the executive. Fraser now chooses Mairi Campbell from the change team as project manager and agrees her responsibilities with her. Which role is responsible for the 'appoint the executive and the project manager' activity?
o: The business layer, which commissioned the project and identified its executive.
The executive, who appoints the project manager to manage the project on his behalf.
The project board, once the senior user and senior supplier have been appointed.
The project manager, who confirms her own role description with the executive.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the recommended RACI for 'appoint the executive and the project manager', the business layer is accountable and the executive is responsible; the project manager then manages the project day to day on the executive's behalf (see manual 13.4.1 and table 13.2).

n.0: The business layer is accountable for the activity; the executive is responsible for carrying it out, including appointing the project manager.
n.2: The rest of the board is appointed later, in 'appoint the project management team'; it does not carry out this activity.
n.3: The project manager is the person being appointed; she is not responsible for her own appointment.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Project Skyline is in the 'starting up a project' process. Fraser McIntyre tells Mairi Campbell that, because the society's board has already approved the cloud strategy, there is no need for a project brief or an initiation stage plan. He asks her to start initiation work with Stratoshift next week and report back in two months. Is this an effective way to carry out starting up a project, and why?
o: Yes, because approval of the strategy by the society's board acts as the authority to initiate the project.
Yes, because starting up can be shortened when a programme has supplied most of the project brief.
No, because starting up puts the prerequisites for initiation in place before an explicit decision to initiate.
No, because the business layer, rather than the executive, should carry out starting up on a project this size.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Starting up a project makes sure the prerequisites for initiation are in place, including the project brief and the initiation stage plan, and the decision to initiate must be explicit, taken by the board in 'authorize initiation' (see manual 13.1 and 13.4.8). A strategy approval is not that decision.

n.0: A strategy sets direction for the business; the project board still has to authorize initiation explicitly on the basis of a project brief.
n.1: It is true that a programme can supply much of the brief, but Project Skyline is not part of a programme and no brief exists.
n.3: Starting up is led by the project manager, with the business layer and executive making the appointments; the business layer does not run the whole process.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Mairi Campbell asks Joanne Pettigrew which weekend in March would least disrupt the branches and contact centre when the branch systems move. Joanne checks with her branch managers and replies the next day with a preferred weekend and the dates to avoid. Is this an appropriate application of the 'give ongoing direction' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the senior user is accountable for approving the stage plan, which includes the switch-over dates.
Yes, because board members can give informal guidance, and the senior user gives direction on user matters.
No, because direction from the board should be given collectively at a formal meeting of the board.
No, because a request for advice has to be raised as an issue in the issue register before the board responds.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: Giving ongoing direction includes informal guidance and responses to requests for advice at any time, given collectively or by individual board members; in the recommended RACI the senior user is responsible for user-related direction (see manual 14.4.3).

n.0: The executive approves stage plans; the senior user's part here is giving user-related direction.
n.2: Ongoing direction can be given informally and by individual board members, not only at formal meetings.
n.3: Requests for advice can be made informally; not every question to the board is an issue for the register.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Before each board meeting, the board's business assurance checks the figures in Mairi Campbell's highlight report against the migration tool's records and the stage plan, and tells Fraser McIntyre whether the report gives a fair picture. Which practice is being applied by the directing a project process, and why?
o: Quality, because the checks confirm that the migrated applications meet their quality specifications.
Organizing, because project assurance is a role that the project board appoints to support its work.
Risk, because checking the figures reduces the chance of an unexpected breach of tolerance.
Progress, because the board makes sure that reporting is fair by validating the highlight reports.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In directing a project the progress practice is applied by the board assuring itself that reporting is fair, validating highlight and end stage reports, and responding to exception reports (see manual chapter 14, table 14.3).

n.0: The checks are on reported progress figures, not on whether products meet their quality specifications.
n.1: Assurance is a role from the organizing practice, but the activity described is validating progress reporting.
n.2: Accurate reporting supports control, but checking reported progress is part of the progress practice, not risk management.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Project Skyline is at the end of the 'initiating a project' process. Board members are busy with the year end, so Fraser McIntyre emails Mairi Campbell telling her to start the foundations stage at once. He says the board will review the PID, the project plan and the foundations stage plan at its next meeting in six weeks. Stratoshift is ready to begin building the landing zone. Is this an effective way to carry out directing a project, and why?
o: Yes, because the board can give approval without a meeting when the executive gives a documented instruction.
Yes, because the executive is accountable for the project and can authorize the stage on his own.
No, because the decision to start a delivery stage belongs to the business layer rather than the board.
No, because delivery should not start until the board has approved the PID and authorized the first delivery stage.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In directing a project the board authorizes the project by approving the PID, and a stage starts when the board authorizes its stage plan; delivery should not begin before these decisions (see manual 14.4.2 and 14.4.4). Here the board has not yet reviewed any of the documents.

n.0: Decisions can be made without a formal meeting when the members agree, but here the board has not reviewed the PID or stage plan at all.
n.1: The executive is accountable, but authorizing the project and the stage are board decisions based on the PID and stage plan.
n.2: The project board authorizes each stage; the business layer sets project tolerances and decides on project-level exceptions.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell agrees with the board that it will receive highlight reports every two weeks, that each stage will end with a stage boundary review, and that each migration wave has a time tolerance of two weeks within the stage plan. She also agrees how she will control Stratoshift's work through work packages and checkpoint reports. Is this an appropriate application of the 'establish project controls' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because it agrees the board's control after initiation and how the project manager will control the teams.
Yes, because once project controls are agreed, the board no longer needs to authorize each stage separately.
No, because project controls are agreed in starting up a project, before initiation is authorized.
No, because tolerances for each wave should be set by the business layer in the project mandate.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: 'Establish project controls' agrees the level and mechanism of control the board will have after initiation, and how the project manager will control the work of team managers (see manual 15.4.3). Reporting frequency, stage boundaries, tolerances and work package controls are all part of this.

n.1: Project controls include the stage boundaries; the board still authorizes each stage.
n.2: Project controls are established in initiation, once the management approaches are agreed.
n.3: The business layer sets project tolerances; tolerances within a stage plan are set by the board.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell updates the outline business case with the costs and timescales from the project plan and the aggregated risks from the project log. Fraser McIntyre will be asked to approve it. Which role should be consulted during the 'prepare the full business case' activity?
o: The business layer, represented by the society's executive committee.
The project manager, Mairi Campbell, who is preparing the document.
Project assurance, acting on behalf of the project board.
The executive, Fraser McIntyre, who will be asked to approve it.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: In the recommended RACI for 'prepare the full business case', the executive is accountable, the project manager is responsible, project assurance is consulted and the business layer is not involved (see manual 15.4.5).

n.0: The business layer is not involved in preparing the full business case.
n.1: The project manager is responsible for preparing it, not consulted.
n.3: The executive is accountable for the business case, not consulted.

Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.q: Project Skyline is in the 'initiating a project' process. Mairi Campbell plans to leave the digital and data management approach until the foundations stage, saying that member data will not move until the pilot wave. The project will copy member data between the sites and the cloud, and old hardware must be disposed of with certificates confirming that member data has been destroyed. Is this an effective way to carry out initiating a project, and why?
o: Yes, because handling member data is a technical matter for Stratoshift's work package descriptions.
Yes, because the management approaches are reviewed at each stage boundary, so this one can be added at the first.
No, because data protection requirements belong in the quality management approach rather than a separate approach.
No, because how data is kept secure through the lifecycle and afterwards should be agreed before the project is authorized.
Practitioner: Starting Up, Directing & I.w: The digital and data management approach is one of the management approaches agreed in initiation and approved with the PID; it describes how data will be created, used, secured and managed through the lifecycle and afterwards (see manual 15.4.2 and chapter 11, progress management products). With member data moving and being destroyed, it is needed before authorization.

n.0: Work packages apply the approaches; the approach itself must first be agreed at project level so the board can approve it.
n.1: Approaches are reviewed and updated at stage boundaries, but they are first agreed in initiation as part of the PID.
n.2: The digital and data management approach is a separate approach in PRINCE2 7; the quality management approach covers quality standards and responsibilities.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Permits Online is in the discovery and alpha stage. Hannah Okoro and Tom Achebe draft the work package description for the eligibility checks together. They agree time and cost tolerances, a scope tolerance on optional features, checkpoint reports after each sprint review and how finished products will be handed over. Tom confirms his team can deliver it before Hannah authorizes the work. Is this an appropriate application of the 'authorize a work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the team manager sets the tolerances for the work package and the project manager records them.
Yes, because the project manager co-creates the work package with the team manager and confirms acceptance.
No, because the work package description should also set a benefits tolerance for processing time.
No, because work packages should be authorized by the project board as part of approving the stage plan.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'authorize a work package' the project manager defines the work package, co-creates and reviews it with the team manager, confirms that the team manager accepts it and then authorizes the work (see manual 16.4.1). Work package tolerances cover scope, cost and time.

n.0: The project manager sets work package tolerances; the team manager agrees to work within them.
n.2: Benefits and quality tolerances are not set in a work package description; its tolerances are scope, cost and time.
n.3: The board approves stage plans; authorizing work packages within the stage is the project manager's activity in controlling a stage.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Permits Online is in the private beta stage. While evaluating stage status, Hannah Okoro finds that the telephone assisted route is behind schedule but still within stage tolerance. She moves two Kestrel Lane developers onto the work through an amended work package. Which role is accountable for the 'take corrective action' activity?
o: The executive.
The project manager.
The team manager.
Project support.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In the recommended RACI for 'take corrective action', the executive is accountable, the project manager is responsible for selecting and triggering the action, and project support is informed (see manual 16.4.6 and table 16.2).

n.1: The project manager is responsible for taking the corrective action; accountability for the activity sits with the executive.
n.2: The team manager carries out the amended work package but is not accountable for the activity.
n.3: Project support is informed of corrective action, not accountable for it.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Permits Online is in the private beta stage and is forecast to finish within its tolerances. Dev Mistry tells Hannah Okoro that contact centre staff have not been briefed on the online service and are giving residents wrong advice. Without recording or assessing the problem, Hannah sends the board an exception report the same day. Is this an effective way to carry out controlling a stage, and why?
o: Yes, because the waste app lesson shows that contact centre problems must go straight to the board.
Yes, because the board should be alerted as early as possible to anything affecting residents.
No, because the issue should be captured and assessed first, and no stage tolerance breach is forecast.
No, because contact centre problems are business as usual and so lie outside the project's control.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'capture issues and risks' each issue is registered and assessed before a course of action is chosen (see manual 16.4.5). An exception report is for a forecast breach of stage tolerance (16.4.7); here the stage is within tolerance, so the project manager should handle the problem, for example by arranging briefings, and report it in the next highlight report.

n.0: The lesson is about telling the contact centre, which this problem shows is needed; it does not change how issues are escalated.
n.1: Alerting the board early applies to forecast exceptions; issues within tolerance are handled by the project manager.
n.3: Preparing the contact centre for the new service is part of the project's communication and change work, so this is a project issue.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Permits Online is in the discovery and alpha stage. Tom Achebe receives the draft work package for the council tax integration interface. It relies on Alan Briggs's ICT team, who are free for two days a week, so the planned four sprints are not achievable. Before agreeing to it, Tom discusses the timescale and the dependency with Hannah Okoro, and they agree a revised work package. Is this an appropriate application of the 'accept a work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the team manager sets the tolerances for the work package once it has been accepted.
Yes, because the team manager agrees with the project manager what will be delivered and whether it is achievable.
No, because the team manager should accept the work package as authorized and report problems in checkpoints.
No, because Tom Achebe should take the dependency on the ICT team to the project board to resolve.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'accept a work package' the team manager agrees with the project manager what is to be delivered, the reporting requirements, constraints and procedures, and confirms that it is achievable before committing to it (see manual 17.4.1).

n.0: The project manager sets work package tolerances; the team manager agrees to work within them.
n.2: Acceptance is an agreement, not a formality; problems known at the start should be resolved before the team manager commits.
n.3: The team manager works with the project manager, not the board; the board is not involved in managing product delivery.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Permits Online is in the private beta stage. Tom Achebe's team is building and testing the permit renewal feature under an authorized work package, holding daily stand-ups and recording completed quality checks. Which role is accountable for the 'execute a work package' activity?
o: The team manager.
The senior supplier.
The project manager.
The executive.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In the recommended RACI for 'execute a work package', the project manager is accountable while the team manager leads the work; project assurance is consulted, and the business layer and executive are not involved (see manual 17.4.2 and table 17.2).

n.0: The team manager leads the work in the work package but is not accountable for the activity in the recommended RACI.
n.1: The senior supplier commits supplier resources at board level, but the board is not involved in managing product delivery.
n.3: The executive is not involved in executing work packages.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Permits Online is in the private beta stage. Tom Achebe's team finds that the vehicle record check fails for about 5% of lease cars. Tom decides to add a step where residents upload a lease agreement, which changes the agreed product description for the application form, and tells Hannah Okoro when he notifies completion of the work package. Is this an effective way to execute the work package, and why?
o: Yes, because the team manager may make decisions within the work package to deliver its products.
Yes, because the extra step solves the problem for residents and keeps the private beta on schedule.
No, because new issues should be raised with the project manager when found, not decided by the team.
No, because the team manager should have taken the issue to the senior user to decide.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'execute a work package' the team manager notifies the project manager of new issues, risks or lessons and takes any action the project manager requires (see manual 17.4.2). Changing a baselined product description is a change to be assessed through the issue management approach, not decided within the team.

n.0: Team managers decide within their work package tolerances, but altering an agreed product description goes beyond the work package and needs change control.
n.1: Solving the problem quickly does not justify changing the baseline without assessment and approval.
n.3: The team manager raises issues with the project manager, who escalates them if needed; the board is not involved in managing product delivery.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Permits Online is in the public beta stage. Hannah Okoro's exception report showed that migration problems would take the stage beyond its cost tolerance, and the board asked for an exception plan. Hannah records the request in the project log, prepares a plan from the current position to the end of the stage, and checks whether the business case and project plan need updating. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare exception plan' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because it replaces the stage plan from now to the end of the stage, and the PID is reviewed with it.
Yes, because an exception plan covers the rest of the whole project rather than the current stage.
No, because exception plans are prepared in controlling a stage as part of taking corrective action.
No, because the exception plan should replace the team plan for the migration work package.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: When the board asks for an exception plan after an exception report, the project manager prepares it in managing a stage boundary: the request is recorded in the project log, the plan replaces the stage plan from the current position to the end of the stage, and the PID, including the business case and project plan, is reviewed and updated (see manual chapter 18 and 7.2.2.4). Its approval marks a stage boundary.

n.1: A stage-level exception plan covers the rest of the stage it replaces; a project-level plan would be needed for a forecast breach of project tolerance.
n.2: Corrective action within tolerance happens in controlling a stage; exception plans are prepared in managing a stage boundary.
n.3: Exception plans replace stage or project plans; they are not produced for team plans.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Permits Online is approaching the end of the discovery and alpha stage. As part of managing the stage boundary, Hannah Okoro reviews how the combined council and Kestrel Lane team has performed, including workload and well-being during the integration delays, and records lessons for the end stage report. Which practice is being applied by the 'managing a stage boundary' process?
o: Progress, because the findings will be summarized for the board in the end stage report.
Quality, because the team's performance is checked against the quality register for the stage.
Plans, because the team's workload will be used to prepare the next stage plan.
Organizing, because the team's performance, health and well-being are reviewed at the boundary.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In managing a stage boundary the organizing practice is applied by reviewing the project team's performance, health and well-being, both for lessons and for the end stage report (see manual table 18.3).

n.0: Progress is applied by creating and issuing the end stage report; reviewing the team's performance and well-being is organizing.
n.1: The quality register records quality activities on products, not team performance or well-being.
n.2: The next stage plan is prepared in this process, but reviewing the team's health and well-being is not the plans practice.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Permits Online is approaching the end of the discovery and alpha stage. The project plan, approved in initiation, already shows the private beta's main products and dates. To save time, Hannah Okoro asks the board to authorize the private beta stage on the basis of the project plan, without preparing a stage plan, although the alpha research has changed several user needs. Is this an effective way to manage the stage boundary, and why?
o: Yes, because the project plan already contains enough detail for the board to control each stage.
Yes, because the project manager can approve the start of the next stage within project tolerance.
No, because stage plans should be prepared during initiation for every stage of the project.
No, because the next stage plan is prepared near the end of this stage, reflecting what has been learned.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: As only the near future can be planned in detail, each delivery stage plan is prepared near the end of the current stage, close to when the work happens, and approved by the board (see manual 7.2.2.2 and chapter 18). The alpha research has changed user needs, so a fresh stage plan is needed.

n.0: The project plan is high level; the detailed stage plan is the basis for the project manager's control within a stage.
n.1: A stage starts when the board authorizes it; the project manager cannot approve it.
n.2: The initiation stage plan is prepared in starting up; each later stage plan is prepared at the boundary before that stage.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Permits Online is in the closing part of the public beta stage. All permits are migrated and the paper process has ended. Hannah Okoro confirms with Ruth Abernethy that the service meets its acceptance criteria and has passed the audit and IT health check, transfers running of the service to parking services and checks that Kestrel Lane's hosting and support arrangements are in place. Is this an appropriate application of the 'confirm project acceptance' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because acceptance is confirmed and the products pass to the people who will operate and support them.
Yes, because handing the service over to parking services is the final post-project benefits review.
No, because acceptance should wait until benefits reviews confirm that permit calls have halved.
No, because the project should be closed as a separate stage once the public beta has finished.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: Confirm project acceptance ensures that the products are passed into the operational and maintenance environment and that acceptance of the project product is confirmed against its acceptance criteria (see manual 19.4.3). Checking the support arrangements meets the objective that the business can support the products after closure.

n.1: Handover is not a benefits review; post-project benefits reviews are planned in the project and carried out by the business later.
n.2: Benefits such as halving calls are measured after closure in post-project benefits reviews; acceptance is judged against the acceptance criteria.
n.3: Closing a project is the last part of the final stage, not a separate stage.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Permits Online is in the 'closing a project' process. Hannah Okoro checks that every product listed for the project, from the online application to the staff guidance, has been delivered and approved, notes each product's final status and closes the register that tracks them. Which practice is being applied by the 'closing a project' process?
o: Quality, because the quality register is checked and closed to confirm every quality activity was completed.
Progress, because the end project report compares what was delivered with the baselined PID.
Issues, because the status of each product shows whether any changes to the baseline remain open.
Plans, because the product register is checked and closed as the record of the plan's products.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In closing a project the plans practice is applied by checking and closing the product register, the list of all products required by a plan and their status (see manual table 19.3).

n.0: Checking and closing the quality register is how quality is applied in closing; the register described lists products and their status, which is the product register.
n.1: The end project report applies the progress practice, but the action described is closing the product register.
n.2: Open issues are handled through the issue register and follow-on action recommendations; the product register is a plans record.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Permits Online has gone live and is in the 'closing a project' process. To show that permit calls to the contact centre halve within a year, Hannah Okoro proposes keeping the project open, with herself and two Kestrel Lane staff, for twelve months after launch to run the benefits reviews before asking for closure. Is this an effective way to carry out closing a project, and why?
o: Yes, because the senior user is responsible for the continued realization of benefits after closure.
Yes, because the business case cannot be confirmed until all of the expected benefits have been measured.
No, because the benefits management approach should be closed along with the other project records.
No, because post-project benefits reviews are planned by the project but carried out by the business after closure.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: Closing a project updates the benefits management approach to plan the post-project benefits reviews; carrying them out is not a project activity but is done by the business after closure (see manual 19.2, 19.4 and 5.3.1). Keeping the project open would prolong its costs and blur the handover.

n.0: The senior user stays responsible for the continued realization of benefits after closure, which is why the project need not stay open to measure them.
n.1: Benefits are mostly confirmed after the project has closed; the project does not wait for them before closing.
n.2: The benefits management approach is not closed; it is updated in closing so that the business can run the post-project reviews.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the asbestos removal, strip-out and structural works stage. More asbestos is found behind a wall lining. Leah Whitfield captures and assesses the problem: it adds two weeks and £35,000, within the stage tolerances of three weeks and £60,000, and can be funded from the risk budget held for asbestos. She issues a revised work package to the removal subcontractor and reports the action in her next highlight report. Is this an appropriate application of the 'take corrective action' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because asbestos is a safety matter, which the project manager may resolve without involving the board.
Yes, because within stage tolerance the project manager selects a solution and applies it through a work package.
No, because the extra cost should be referred to the board in an exception report before the work is changed.
No, because the subcontractor's team manager should decide the response and revise the work package.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: 'Take corrective action' collects information about a deviation, identifies and selects solutions that keep the stage within tolerance, and puts them into effect through 'authorize a work package' (see manual 16.4.6). The board is kept informed through the highlight report.

n.0: Safety is not what gives Leah authority to act; it is that the deviation is forecast to stay within stage tolerance.
n.2: An exception report is needed when stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded; this deviation stays within it.
n.3: The team manager raises the problem and carries out the revised work, but the project manager decides corrective action and authorizes work packages.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the mechanical and electrical fit-out stage. Remembering the lab refurbishment, Leah Whitfield writes into each work package description how the contractor's team must raise problems and requests for change, so that nothing is agreed on site without assessment, and she updates the issue register as they arrive. Which practice is being applied by the 'controlling a stage' process?
o: Progress, because the contractor will report problems to the project manager through its checkpoint reports.
Plans, because the work package descriptions are prepared, agreed and then authorized by the project manager.
Organizing, because each team's responsibilities for raising problems are defined in the work packages.
Issues, because the issue management approach is built into the work packages and the issue register is kept current.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In controlling a stage the issues practice is applied by including the issue management approach in work package descriptions and keeping the issue register up to date (see manual table 16.3).

n.0: Checkpoint reports carry progress information, but the action described applies the issue management approach.
n.1: Work package descriptions are plans products, but their content here is how issues and changes are handled.
n.2: Responsibilities are mentioned, but the procedure for capturing problems and changes belongs to the issues practice.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the mechanical and electrical fit-out stage. Greystack's site manager tells Leah Whitfield by phone that the welding bays work package is finished. As the stage is behind schedule, she marks it complete in the stage plan and authorizes the next work package, although the product description says the bays must pass the fume extraction test and be approved by Craig Dunmore. Is this an effective way to carry out controlling a stage, and why?
o: Yes, because the team manager is responsible for the quality of the products in the work package.
Yes, because the quality checks can be carried out during commissioning and handover in stage 5.
No, because a work package is received as complete once each product has the approvals in its product description.
No, because completion of a work package should be notified to the project board by the senior supplier.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'receive completed work package' the project manager makes sure each product has the approval required by the quality and sustainability responsibilities in its product description, then updates the product register and stage plan (see manual 16.4.3).

n.0: The team manager delivers to the product descriptions, but the project manager must confirm the required approvals before accepting the work package as complete.
n.1: The product description sets when and by whom the bays are approved; delaying the checks leaves an unapproved product treated as complete.
n.3: Work package completion is notified by the team manager to the project manager; the board is not involved in managing product delivery.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the mechanical and electrical fit-out stage. Greystack's site manager is leading the fit-out work package. After the fire-stopping inspection passes, his team records the result in the quality register. He also notices that the planned heat pump compound may block the delivery route for the nacelle rig, and reports this new risk to Leah Whitfield in his weekly checkpoint report. Is this an appropriate application of the 'execute a work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the team manager reports new risks to the project manager and keeps quality records up to date.
Yes, because the team manager owns all the risks within the work package and decides how to respond to them.
No, because new risks should be raised directly with the senior supplier, who represents the contractor.
No, because project support, not the team, should update the quality register with inspection results.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'execute a work package' the team manager manages development of the products, notifies the project manager of new issues, risks or lessons, takes any action the project manager requires, records completed quality activities in the quality register and reports through checkpoint reports (see manual 17.4.2).

n.1: The team manager notifies new risks to the project manager and takes any action the project manager requires.
n.2: In managing product delivery the team manager deals with the project manager, not with board members.
n.3: In managing product delivery the team records completed quality activities and updates the quality register.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the asbestos removal, strip-out and structural works stage. Greystack's site manager has finished the strip-out work package and is notifying Leah Whitfield, the project manager. Using the recommended RACI for 'notify work package completion', which other role should be informed?
o: The business layer, so that the governors know the strip-out has been completed.
The senior user, so that Sunita Rao can plan the next curriculum activities.
Project support, so that the project's records and registers can be updated.
The senior supplier, so that Owen Pryce can confirm the completed work to the board.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In the recommended RACI for 'notify work package completion', project support is informed, while the business layer, senior user and senior supplier are not; the board is not involved in managing product delivery (see manual 17.4.4 and table 17.2).

n.0: The business layer is not informed of work package completion; it receives project-level information through the board.
n.1: The recommended RACI does not inform the senior user of work package completion.
n.3: The recommended RACI does not inform the senior supplier; completion is a matter between the team manager and the project manager.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the mechanical and electrical fit-out stage. Ingrid Sorensen's installation team is installing the nacelle rig under a work package. Visiting the site, Ade Okafor of Brackmoor asks the team to add a second control panel like the one on Brackmoor's turbines. The team agrees, as the change is small and Brackmoor is a key employer, and tells Leah Whitfield once it is done. Is this an effective way to carry out managing product delivery, and why?
