o: Yes, because Brackmoor's support is the main reason the wind operators are committing apprentices.
Yes, because a team manager may agree minor product changes directly with key stakeholders during installation.
No, because changes to the rig have to be approved by Sunita Rao as senior user before work starts.
No, because the team should work under the project manager's direction and raise the request as an issue.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: Managing product delivery controls the link between the project manager and the team manager: the team works to the agreed work package, notifies the project manager of new issues and takes action required by the project manager, not by others (see manual 17.1 and 17.4.2). A request to change the product goes through issue control.

n.0: Brackmoor's importance makes the request worth assessing, but it does not authorize the team to change the product.
n.1: A change to an agreed product is a request for change: the team raises it with the project manager for issue control, and the team manager does not agree it directly with stakeholders.
n.2: Requests for change are decided by the board or a delegated change authority, not by the senior user acting alone.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is near the end of the mechanical and electrical fit-out stage. Leah Whitfield briefs the board on the stage's performance, gives an overview of the commissioning and handover stage, confirms that the eight instructors have been recruited, and highlights that four welding bays were accepted under a concession because their screens differ slightly from the specification. Is this an appropriate application of the 'request next stage' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the board needs the stage's performance, readiness for the next stage and any concessions to decide.
Yes, because the project manager authorizes the next stage once the board has read the end stage report.
No, because concessions should be reported in the end project report at closure rather than at a stage end.
No, because instructor recruitment is business as usual and lies outside the scope of the project.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'request next stage' the project manager briefs the board on current stage performance, gives an overview of the next stage and the people and resources it needs, confirms readiness to proceed and highlights any concessions for off-specifications in the stage (see managing a stage boundary, manual chapter 18).

n.1: The next stage starts only when the board authorizes it in directing a project; the project manager requests it.
n.2: Concessions granted in a stage are highlighted when requesting the next stage, as well as being reviewed at closure.
n.3: Course and staff readiness is part of the project's final stage, so instructor recruitment is relevant to readiness.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is near the end of the asbestos removal, strip-out and structural works stage, and Leah Whitfield is preparing the end stage report. Using the recommended RACI for 'evaluate the stage', which roles should she consult?
o: The executive and the senior user, who will decide whether to authorize the next stage.
The team manager, project support and project assurance, who hold the information and checks needed.
The business layer and the senior supplier, as the contractor's work makes up most of the stage.
The senior user, the senior supplier and the business layer, to agree what the report will say.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In the recommended RACI for 'evaluate the stage', the project manager is responsible for preparing the end stage report, and the team manager, project support and project assurance are consulted (see managing a stage boundary, manual chapter 18).

n.0: The RACI for 'evaluate the stage' consults the team manager, project support and project assurance; the board decides later in directing a project.
n.2: The business layer is not consulted in this activity, and the senior supplier is not among the roles consulted.
n.3: The project manager is responsible for the report; the roles consulted are the team manager, project support and project assurance.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is near the end of the asbestos removal, strip-out and structural works stage. Leah Whitfield updates the project plan with actual progress and prepares the fit-out stage plan. Heat pump quotes have risen by £120,000 and Brackmoor has cut its pledge from 40 to 25 apprentice places a year, but she leaves the business case unchanged because the grant amount has not changed. Is this an effective way to manage the stage boundary, and why?
o: Yes, because the business case is updated in initiation and is then confirmed after the centre has opened.
Yes, because changes in costs and pledges should be handled as issues within controlling a stage, not at the boundary.
No, because the fall in pledges should be referred to the combined authority before the stage boundary.
No, because the business case should show the new costs and benefit forecasts so the board can confirm justification.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In managing a stage boundary the business case is updated to reflect changes in the project and its environment, with revised costs, benefit forecasts and aggregated risk, so that the board can confirm continued business justification before authorizing the next stage (see manual chapter 18 and 5.3.1).

n.0: The business case is maintained at every stage boundary, not left until benefits are confirmed after closure.
n.1: Issues are captured during the stage, but their effect on justification is brought together in the business case at the boundary.
n.2: The combined authority is the funder, not part of the project's decision-making; the board needs the updated business case.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the asbestos removal, strip-out and structural works stage. After a funding review, the combined authority withdraws the grant, and the board instructs Leah Whitfield to close the project early. She records the instruction, makes the site safe and secure, agrees with the contractor which completed work is kept and which is abandoned, and makes sure the project's records are archived. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare premature closure' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the project manager decides when the project should close once its business case is no longer valid.
Yes, because a premature close still needs an orderly closure, with useful work salvaged and products made safe.
No, because when the grant is withdrawn the board closes the project in directing a project, without closing a project.
No, because an exception plan should be prepared first to show how the project could continue with less money.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: When the board orders a premature close, closing a project is still used: 'prepare premature closure' records the request, salvages anything useful, makes products safe and agrees what is completed or abandoned, so that the project is closed in an orderly way rather than abandoned (see manual 19.3 and 19.4.2).

n.0: Premature closure is triggered by the project board, not by the project manager.
n.2: Closing a project is still run, tailored as needed, when the board orders a premature close.
n.3: The board has already decided to close the project; preparing an exception plan would ignore that decision.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Tarnside's Engineering Skills Centre project is in the 'closing a project' process. Leah Whitfield is preparing the end project report and the lessons report, comparing the project's performance with the baselined project initiation documentation. Using the recommended RACI for 'evaluate the project', which statement is correct?
o: The executive is accountable, the project manager responsible, and the senior supplier and project assurance consulted.
The project manager is accountable, project support is responsible, and the business layer is consulted on the report.
The senior user is accountable, the project manager responsible, and the team managers informed of the findings.
The business layer is accountable, the executive responsible, and the project manager consulted on the findings.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In the recommended RACI for 'evaluate the project', the executive is accountable, the project manager is responsible, and the senior supplier and project assurance are consulted (see manual 19.4.4 and table 19.2).

n.1: The project manager is responsible for this activity and the executive accountable; the business layer is not consulted.
n.2: The executive, not the senior user, is accountable for evaluating the project.
n.3: The project manager, not the executive, is responsible for evaluating the project, with the executive accountable.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Engineering Skills Centre opened on time, and the project is in the 'closing a project' process. Leah Whitfield proposes keeping the project open for six months after opening, so that the project team can deal with snags during the contractor's defects period and check that 300 apprentices have enrolled before the project closes. Is this an effective way to carry out closing a project, and why?
o: Yes, because benefits have to be confirmed before the project closes, so the project should stay open until enrolment is known.
Yes, because defects found in the first months of use are part of the project's scope and need its team to resolve them.
No, because a clear end is needed: open matters go to follow-on actions and the business reviews benefits after closure.
No, because closing a project should be planned as a separate stage after the commissioning and handover stage.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: Closing a project gives a fixed point at which acceptance is confirmed; a clear end is better than a slow drift into use. Open issues and risks are passed on as follow-on action recommendations, and post-project benefits reviews are planned in the benefits management approach and carried out by the business (see manual 19.1 to 19.3).

n.0: Benefits are mostly confirmed after closure by the business, through reviews planned in the benefits management approach.
n.1: Defects handled under the contract can be passed on as follow-on actions; they do not justify keeping the project running.
n.3: Closing a project is not a stage; it is part of the final stage, so planning it as a separate stage is wrong.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The SPA project is in the design and pilot preparation stage. The team manager hands over the completed triage criteria work package. Before updating the product register and the stage plan, Ellie Chandran checks that each set of criteria has been signed off by the clinical safety officer and the medical director, as their product description requires. Is this an appropriate application of the 'receive completed work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because each product should have the approvals its product description requires before it is treated as complete.
Yes, because receiving a completed work package is when the board accepts the project product on behalf of users.
No, because the senior user accepts each product when the work package is received, so Moira's approval is enough.
No, because checking approvals is a task for project assurance rather than for the project manager.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In receiving a completed work package the project manager makes sure each product has the requisite approval defined by the quality and sustainability responsibilities in its product description, then updates the product register and the stage plan (see manual 16.4.3).

n.1: Acceptance of the project product is confirmed in closing a project; this is receipt of one work package's products.
n.2: Who approves a product is set in its product description; here that requires the clinical safety officer and the medical director.
n.3: Project assurance may check on the board's behalf, but confirming approvals when receiving the work package is the project manager's activity.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The SPA project is in the Eastfield pilot stage. When the patients' forum asks for carers to be able to refer patients directly, Ellie Chandran records the request formally, works out its effect on the stage plan, the business case and the risks, and sets out the options. Which practice is she applying in controlling a stage, and why?
o: Business case, because she is judging whether the change would still leave the project justified.
Risk, because the request creates uncertainty about the cost and timescale of the stage.
Issues, because she is capturing and assessing a request to change the approved scope.
Progress, because she is forecasting the effect of the request on the stage plan.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: Capturing a request for change and assessing its impact on plans, the business case and risks are the first steps of the issues technique, which controls changes to the project's baseline (see manual 10.3.1 and table 16.3).

n.0: The business case is one of the things assessed, but handling a request for change applies the issues practice.
n.1: The request is an issue that has arisen, not an uncertain event; its effect on risks is part of assessing it.
n.3: Forecasting belongs to progress, but the action as a whole is capturing and assessing a request for change.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The SPA project is in the Eastfield pilot stage, which has a time tolerance of two weeks. Training for hub nurses is running late, and Ellie Chandran forecasts that the stage will finish one week behind plan. Wanting the board to feel involved, she sends it an exception report asking it to choose between adding training sessions and shortening the induction. Is this an effective way to carry out the controlling a stage process, and why?
o: Yes, because an exception report keeps the board informed of any forecast deviation from the stage plan.
Yes, because a project manager new to PRINCE2 7 should refer decisions on corrective action to the executive.
No, because the delay is within stage tolerance, so she should take corrective action and report it to the board.
No, because the team manager should have sent the exception report to the board from the training work package.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: If a deviation can be resolved within stage tolerance, the project manager takes corrective action in controlling a stage and reports it in the highlight report; an exception report is raised when stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded (see manual 11.2.6, 16.4.6 and 16.4.7).

n.0: Exception reports are for forecast breaches of tolerance, not any deviation; using them within tolerance wastes the board's time.
n.1: Corrective action within tolerance is the project manager's activity; inexperience is addressed through support and assurance, not by passing decisions up.
n.3: Team managers raise work package problems with the project manager as issues; they do not send exception reports to the board.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The SPA project is in the design and pilot preparation stage. Josie Barker, team manager for the referral form configuration, receives a draft work package from Ellie Chandran. Because one of her three analysts is leaving, she checks with her team whether the four-week timescale is achievable, agrees the reporting arrangements with Ellie and prepares a team plan before agreeing to deliver. Is this an appropriate application of the 'accept a work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because accepting a work package lets Josie change its tolerances to suit her team's capacity.
Yes, because the team manager agrees what will be delivered and confirms it is achievable before committing.
No, because the team plan should be approved by the project board before Josie accepts the work.
No, because the work package should be accepted by the senior supplier on behalf of Josie's team.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In accepting a work package the team manager agrees with the project manager what is to be delivered, the reporting requirements, constraints and procedures, and whether it is achievable, producing a team plan if needed, before agreeing to deliver (see manual 17.4.1).

n.0: Tolerances are agreed with the project manager; if they are not achievable Josie should say so, not change them herself.
n.2: Team plans are optional and produced by the team manager; the board is not involved in managing product delivery.
n.3: The team manager accepts the work package from the project manager; the senior supplier commits resources at board level.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The SPA project is in the design and pilot preparation stage. After accepting the configuration work package, Josie Barker sets out which analyst will configure each referral form, in what order, and the date by which each form will be ready for testing. Which practice is she applying in managing product delivery, and why?
o: Organizing, because she is assigning responsibilities to the members of her team.
Progress, because the dates will be used to monitor the team's progress against plan.
Quality, because the dates show when each form will be ready for its quality check.
Plans, because she is developing a team plan for the products in her work package.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In managing product delivery the plans practice is applied when the team manager develops a team plan for the work package and updates the product register (see manual table 17.3).

n.0: Organizing defines the project's structure of accountability; setting out who does which product, and when, within a work package is team planning.
n.1: Progress will later be monitored against this plan, but producing the plan applies the plans practice.
n.2: The dates link to quality checks, but setting out who does what and when is the team plan.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The SPA project is in the design and pilot preparation stage. Josie Barker's team finds that the referral module cannot receive faxes, which several Moorside practices still send. Tim Rawlings, the senior supplier, tells Josie to build a workaround at once. It will take her team two weeks beyond the work package's time tolerance, and she starts it without telling Ellie Chandran. Is this an effective way to carry out managing product delivery, and why?
o: Yes, because the senior supplier is accountable for the supplier's products and may direct the team's work.
Yes, because a team manager may go beyond tolerance where the change protects referrals from being lost.
No, because Josie should send an exception report to the project board, as the work package will overrun.
No, because Josie should raise the forecast breach with Ellie as an issue and act on Ellie's instructions.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In executing a work package the team manager notifies the project manager of new issues and risks and takes the action the project manager requires, not instructions from board members; a forecast breach of work package tolerance is raised with the project manager as an issue (see manual 17.4.2 and 11.2.1).

n.0: The senior supplier is accountable for supplier products at board level, but team managers take their instructions from the project manager.
n.1: Protecting referrals matters, but going beyond tolerance needs the project manager's decision.
n.2: Team managers escalate to the project manager, who decides whether stage tolerance is threatened and an exception report is needed.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The SPA project is approaching the end of the design and pilot preparation stage. Ellie Chandran briefs the board on how the stage went, gives an overview of the pilot stage and the backfill needed for the hub rota, shows that the triage criteria are signed off and the union has reviewed the rotas, and highlights a concession for a referral form field that was accepted without correction. Is this an appropriate application of the 'request next stage' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because it covers stage performance, the next stage, the resources needed, readiness and any concessions.
Yes, because requesting the next stage gives Ellie authority to start the pilot once she has briefed the board.
No, because concessions should be reported in the end project report rather than at a stage boundary.
No, because readiness for the pilot should be confirmed by the business layer, which set the project tolerances.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: Requesting the next stage briefs the board on the current stage's performance, an overview of the next stage, the people and resources needed, readiness to proceed and any concessions for off-specifications in the stage, so the board can decide whether to authorize it (see manual chapter 18).

n.1: The next stage starts when the board authorizes it in directing a project; the briefing is a request.
n.2: Concessions in the stage are highlighted when requesting the next stage, as well as later in the end project report.
n.3: The board decides on the next stage; the business layer is involved in project-level tolerances and exceptions.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The SPA project is approaching the end of the Eastfield pilot stage. The end stage report must draw on the updated business case, project plan and project log, and the team managers, project support and Neil Ashworth, who carries out business assurance, will all contribute to it. Which role is responsible for the 'evaluate the stage' activity, and why?
o: Project assurance, because it reviews the stage's results independently for the board.
The project manager, because she prepares the end stage report for the board.
The team managers, because their teams delivered the products of the stage.
Project support, because it maintains the project log that the report draws on.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In the managing a stage boundary RACI, the project manager is responsible for evaluating the stage and preparing the end stage report; team managers, project support and project assurance are consulted (see manual chapter 18).

n.0: Project assurance is consulted on the evaluation; it does not prepare the report.
n.2: Team managers are consulted on their work packages' results; they are not responsible for the report.
n.3: Project support is consulted and may help compile information; the project manager is responsible.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The SPA project is approaching the end of the Eastfield pilot stage. Pilot data show referral to first contact falling to four days instead of the three in the business case, which is within the benefits tolerance in the benefits management approach. Ellie Chandran prepares an exception plan for the roll-out stage so that the board can approve the lower forecast. Is this an effective way to carry out managing a stage boundary, and why?
o: Yes, because any reduction in forecast benefits must be approved through an exception plan before the next stage.
Yes, because the exception plan replaces the project plan and resets the benefits targets for the roll-out.
No, because an exception plan is prepared when the board asks for one after a forecast breach of tolerance.
No, because benefits should not be reforecast until the post-project benefits review after closure.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: An exception plan is prepared when the board requests one in response to an exception report about a forecast breach of tolerance. A change in benefit forecasts within tolerance is handled by updating the business case at the stage boundary for the board to review (see manual chapter 18 and 11.3.1).

n.0: Changes in forecast benefits within tolerance are dealt with by updating the business case, not by an exception plan.
n.1: No exception has been raised, so there is nothing for an exception plan to respond to.
n.3: The business case is updated with revised benefit forecasts at every stage boundary; confirmation of benefits comes later.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The SPA project is in the 'closing a project' process at the end of the roll-out stage. Ellie Chandran obtains confirmation from Moira Healy, the senior user, that users accept the SPA, and confirms that community services management is ready to run the triage hub rota and that Medivault will support the module under its contract. Is this an appropriate application of the 'confirm project acceptance' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because confirming acceptance includes carrying out the post-project benefits reviews before the team disbands.
Yes, because acceptance is confirmed and the business is shown to be able to support the products after closure.
No, because each locality accepted the SPA at its go-live, so acceptance need not be confirmed again at closure.
No, because Medivault, as the supplier, should confirm acceptance of the configured module on the users' behalf.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: Confirming project acceptance passes the products to the operational and maintenance environment, in one release or in phases, and confirms user acceptance; closing a project also makes sure the business can support the products after the project ends (see manual 19.2 and 19.4.3).

n.0: Post-project benefits reviews are planned during the project but carried out by the business after closure.
n.2: Phased handover is allowed, but acceptance of the project product as a whole is still confirmed at closure.
n.3: Users, through the senior user, accept the products; the supplier delivers them.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The SPA project is in the 'closing a project' process. Ellie Chandran is comparing the project's performance with its baselined project initiation documentation and preparing the end project report and the lessons report, consulting Tim Rawlings, the senior supplier, and Neil Ashworth, who carries out business assurance. Which role is accountable for the 'evaluate the project' activity, and why?
o: The project manager, because Ellie compares performance and prepares the end project report.
The senior supplier, because Medivault's work is a major part of what is being evaluated.
Project assurance, because Neil Ashworth reviews the project's performance for the board.
The executive, because the executive is accountable for this activity and for the project's success.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In the closing a project RACI, the executive is accountable for evaluating the project, the project manager is responsible, and the senior supplier and project assurance are consulted (see manual 19.4.4).

n.0: Ellie is responsible for the work; the executive is accountable.
n.1: The senior supplier is consulted on the evaluation, not accountable for it.
n.2: Project assurance is consulted; it is not accountable.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The SPA project is in the 'closing a project' process. The trust board asked for a written record of what the project learns, as nobody recorded why the 2021 central booking attempt failed. Ellie Chandran reviews the lessons log, talks to Gareth Pugh and hub nurses about what helped Moorside adopt the SPA, and produces a lessons report for the trust. Is this an effective way to carry out closing a project, and why?
o: Yes, because evaluating the project includes reviewing lessons and producing a lessons report for future work.
Yes, because the lessons report replaces the end project report when the project closes on time and budget.
No, because lessons reports are for the project's own use and are archived with the project log at closure.
No, because lessons should come from the project management team rather than from staff outside it.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: Evaluating the project reviews the project log for lessons and produces a lessons report, in consultation with the project management team, so that lessons can be passed on to future projects (see manual 19.4.4 and 2.2). Drawing on the nurses' experience captures knowledge held across the wider project ecosystem.

n.1: Both reports are produced when evaluating the project; the lessons report does not replace the end project report.
n.2: A lessons report exists to pass lessons on to the business and future projects, not to sit in the archive.
n.3: Much valuable knowledge sits with people across the project ecosystem; learning from experience draws on them too.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage. Nadia Osei and Felix Haddad of Mint and Tallow work through the packaging artwork work package together. They agree the products, the constraint that sleeves must be kerbside-recyclable and carry the carbon label, tolerances of one week and £6,000, fortnightly checkpoint reports to match the agency's cycles, and how finished artwork will be approved. Felix confirms he can deliver it, and Nadia then authorizes the start. Is this an appropriate application of the 'authorize a work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the work package is co-created with the team manager and his acceptance is confirmed before work starts.
Yes, because the work package description should also hold benefits and quality tolerances for the artwork.
No, because the checkpoint frequency should follow the board's highlight reporting cycle, not the agency's cycles.
No, because a fixed-price supplier's work is controlled through its contract rather than through a work package.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: Authorizing a work package involves defining it, building the relationship with the team manager, co-creating and reviewing it with them, confirming their acceptance and then authorizing the start (see manual 16.4.1). The description carries scope, cost and time tolerances, constraints, reporting arrangements and how the products will be approved.

n.1: Work package descriptions carry scope, cost and time tolerances; benefits and quality tolerances are not agreed in a work package description.
n.2: Checkpoint frequency is agreed for the work package and can sensibly follow the team's own working cycle.
n.3: External suppliers' work is still passed to them formally through work packages, which sit alongside the contract.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage, and the fortnightly report to the board is due. The latest checkpoint reports from the team managers, the project log and the revised stage plan are pulled together, the corrective actions taken are listed, and the report is issued to the board. Which role should be responsible for the 'report highlights' activity?
o: The team managers, who produce the checkpoint reports.
Project support, which maintains the project log.
The project manager.
Project assurance, which checks that reporting is fair.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In the recommended RACI for 'report highlights', the project manager is responsible, with team managers, project support and project assurance consulted (see manual 16.4.8 and table 16.2).

n.0: Team managers are consulted; their checkpoint reports feed the highlight report, but they do not produce it.
n.1: Project support is consulted and may help to compile the report, but the project manager is responsible for it.
n.3: Project assurance is consulted; it does not produce the project manager's report to the board.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage, which has a time tolerance of two weeks. Gerrit Vos phones to say that a component shortage might delay the shipment of the line. Without recording the problem or finding out how long the delay could be, Nadia Osei immediately sends the board an exception report recommending an exception plan. Is this an appropriate way to carry out the 'controlling a stage' process, and why?
o: Yes, because a possible delay to the line threatens the fixed launch week, so the board should be involved early.
Yes, because the executive is accountable for the project and should decide on any threat to the line.
No, because the line supplier's project engineer should have escalated the delay directly to the board.
No, because the issue should first be captured and assessed to see whether stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'capture issues and risks' each issue or risk is registered and then assessed before a course of action is decided (see manual 16.4.5). An exception report is raised only when stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded (16.4.7); otherwise the project manager deals with the matter within the stage.

n.0: Early warning matters, but escalation is for a forecast breach of stage tolerance, and that has not been assessed.
n.1: The executive is accountable, but decisions within stage tolerance are delegated to the project manager.
n.2: Team managers and suppliers raise issues with the project manager, not directly with the board.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage. Gerrit Vos reviews the installation work package with Nadia Osei. He points out that the commissioning tests cannot fit inside the three-week shutdown, so they agree to move the tests into the first week of trials and to adjust the constraints. Gerrit then agrees to deliver the work package and prepares a team plan. Is this an appropriate application of the 'accept a work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the team manager can change the stage plan so that it fits the work package.
Yes, because the team manager agrees what will be delivered and confirms it is achievable before accepting.
No, because a team plan should be prepared by the project manager before the work package is offered.
No, because the constraints of a work package are fixed once the project manager has issued it.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'accept a work package' the team manager agrees with the project manager what is to be delivered, the reporting requirements, constraints and procedures, and whether it is achievable, before agreeing to deliver it; a team plan may be produced (see manual 17.4.1).

n.0: The team manager does not change the stage plan; changes are agreed with the project manager, who updates the stage plan.
n.2: Team plans are optional and are produced by team managers, not the project manager.
n.3: Work packages are agreed jointly; raising constraints that make the work unachievable is exactly what acceptance is for.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage. Felix Haddad's team at Mint and Tallow is producing the packaging artwork under its work package, reporting progress through checkpoint reports and recording completed quality checks. Which role should be accountable for the 'execute a work package' activity?
o: The team manager, Felix Haddad.
The senior supplier.
The executive.
The project manager.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In the recommended RACI for 'execute a work package', the project manager is accountable while the team manager's team carries out the work; project assurance is consulted, and the business layer and executive are not involved (see manual 17.4.2 and table 17.2).

n.0: Felix's team does the work; accountability for the activity sits with the project manager.
n.1: The senior supplier commits supplier resources at board level, and the project board is not involved in managing product delivery.
n.2: The executive is not involved in executing work packages.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the development stage. After a call with the Harbridge's buyer, Charlotte Vane emails Felix Haddad directly and asks Mint and Tallow to make the brand logo larger on all six sleeves. Felix tells his team to make the change and mentions it to Nadia Osei in his next checkpoint report. Is this an appropriate way to carry out the 'managing product delivery' process, and why?
o: Yes, because the senior user represents the users and can ask for changes to products that affect them.
Yes, because the change can be made within the work package tolerances agreed with the agency.
No, because the team manager should take instructions from the project manager and raise the request as an issue.
No, because changes to the sleeve design should be approved by the Harbridge's buyer before work starts.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In managing product delivery the team manager works to the work package agreed with the project manager, notifies the project manager of new issues and takes any action the project manager requires, rather than instructions directly from board members (see manual 17.4.2). Charlotte's request is a request for change to an agreed product and should go through Nadia and the issue procedure.

n.0: The senior user can raise a request for change, but through the project's issue procedure, not by instructing a team manager.
n.1: Tolerances limit deviation in delivering agreed products; they do not let a team manager accept new requirements from a board member.
n.3: The buyer is a customer stakeholder; changes to the project's products are controlled through the project's own change control.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in week 2 of its 16-week development stage. To get ahead, Nadia Osei prepares the detailed trials stage plan now, including a date for every trial run, and asks the board to approve it with her next highlight report. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare next stage plan' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because preparing the plan early gives the line supplier more time to arrange its engineers.
Yes, because the trials stage is the most critical stage and so needs the longest planning time.
No, because the next stage plan should be prepared by the team managers who will run the trials.
No, because it should be prepared near the end of the current stage, when its detail is more reliable.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: The next stage plan is prepared near the end of the current stage, close to when the work happens, so that it reflects what has been learned and stays within the planning horizon (see manual 7.2.2 and ch 18). It is then approved by the board in 'authorize a stage or exception plan' at the stage boundary.

n.0: The supplier's needs can be met through the project plan; detailed stage planning this early will be unreliable.
n.1: How critical a stage is does not change the planning horizon; the trials detail depends on what happens in development.
n.2: The project manager prepares stage plans; team managers prepare team plans.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'managing a stage boundary' process at the end of the development stage. During the three-week shutdown, the maintenance staff and Gerrit Vos's engineers worked long night shifts. Nadia Osei reviews how the teams performed and how their health and well-being held up, and records the findings for the lessons log and the end stage report. Which practice is being applied?
o: Organizing
Progress
Quality
Business case
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In managing a stage boundary, the organizing practice is applied by reviewing the project team's performance, health and well-being for lessons and for the end stage report (see manual table 18.3).

n.1: Progress is applied by creating and issuing the end stage report; reviewing team performance and well-being applies organizing.
n.2: Quality is applied by checking the quality register for the stage's quality activities.
n.3: Business case is applied by updating the business case and benefits management approach; the review here is of the teams' performance and well-being.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'managing a stage boundary' process at the end of the trials stage. Tariq Javed confirms that Harbridge's will list the range in 300 stores at launch rather than 400. This lowers forecast year-one sales but keeps the forecast within the benefits tolerance. Nadia Osei updates the business case and the benefits management approach and reports the change in the end stage report, so that the board can decide whether to authorize the final stage. Is this an appropriate way to carry out the 'managing a stage boundary' process, and why?
o: Yes, because the senior user specifies the benefits and so can approve the lower forecast.
Yes, because changes to forecast benefits are handled by updating the business case at the stage boundary.
No, because a fall in forecast benefits should be handled by preparing an exception plan.
No, because benefits are confirmed after closure, so forecasts should not change during the project.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: At a stage boundary the business case is updated to reflect changes in the project and its environment, the benefits management approach is updated, and the end stage report gives the board what it needs to decide on the next stage (see ch 18). A change in forecast benefits within tolerance is handled here, not through an exception plan.

n.0: The senior user specifies the benefits and shows the business that they are on track, but the decision to continue on the updated business case is the board's.
n.2: Exception plans respond to a forecast breach of tolerance; this change is within the benefits tolerance.
n.3: Benefits are confirmed mainly after closure, but forecasts are maintained throughout and updated at every stage boundary.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'closing a project' process after the first eight weeks of sales. Nadia Osei arranges for the range to pass to the normal sales and operations teams, checks that the line has a maintenance contract and trained operators, and obtains confirmation from the senior users that the range has been accepted. She also checks that post-project benefits reviews have been planned. Is this an appropriate application of the 'confirm project acceptance' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the products pass to the operational environment and acceptance is confirmed, with support in place.
Yes, because confirming acceptance includes carrying out the first benefits review before the project closes.
No, because acceptance should be confirmed by the business layer once the first benefits review is complete.
No, because the maintenance contract for the line is an operational matter that is not part of closing a project.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: Confirming project acceptance passes the products to the operational and maintenance environment and confirms that they have been accepted; closing a project also makes sure the business can support the products afterwards (see manual 19.4.3 and 19.2). Checking that post-project benefits reviews are planned is part of this activity.

n.1: Benefits reviews after closure are planned during the project, but carrying them out is not a project activity.
n.2: Acceptance is confirmed during closing, before the project ends, on behalf of the users; benefits reviews come after closure, so waiting for one would keep the project open.
n.3: Making sure the business can support the products after closure is an objective of closing a project.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Fernhollow Kitchen is in the 'closing a project' process. Nadia Osei checks that every product in the plans, from the six recipes and the packaging to the line and the co-manufacturing agreement, is recorded as approved and handed over, and then closes the register that lists the products and their status. Which practice is being applied?
o: Quality
Plans
Issues
Progress
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In closing a project the plans practice is applied by checking and closing the product register, which lists the products of the plans and their status (see manual table 19.3).

n.0: Quality is applied by checking and closing the quality register of quality activities; the product register records product status.
n.2: Issues would be applied by reviewing open issues and recommending follow-on actions; this is about the products' status.
n.3: Progress is applied through the end project report and lessons report; closing the product register applies plans.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Fernhollow Kitchen has completed its launch stage. Rob Hennessy asks Nadia Osei to keep the project open, with its board and reports, for three more years until the forecast £6 million of annual branded sales has been confirmed. Is this an appropriate way to carry out the 'closing a project' process, and why?
o: Yes, because the project is not complete until its benefits have been realized and confirmed.
Yes, because the executive is accountable for the business case, including its benefits.
No, because later benefits are confirmed by post-project reviews that the business carries out.
No, because the senior user, not the executive, decides when the project closes.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: A project is finite, and a clear end is better than a slow drift into use. In closing, the benefits management approach is updated to plan post-project benefits reviews, which the business carries out after closure; running them is not a project activity (see manual 19.3, 19.4 and 5.3.1).

n.0: Most benefits are realized after the project; the project ends when its products are accepted, and benefits are confirmed afterwards.
n.1: The executive is accountable for the business case, but that does not mean the project should stay open while benefits accrue.
n.3: Closure is authorized by the project board in directing a project, on the project manager's request; it is not a decision for the senior user alone.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the planning and approvals stage. Lisa Ventnor notifies Kezia Oduya that the course measurement work package is complete. Before updating the product register and the stage plan, Kezia checks that the accredited course measurer has signed the certificate, as the course's product description names the measurer as its approver. Is this an appropriate application of the 'receive completed work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because each product should have the approval required by the quality responsibilities in its product description.
Yes, because Greg Halloran, as senior supplier, has confirmed that Paceline's work met the terms of its contract.
No, because completed work packages should be approved by the project board before the stage plan is updated.
No, because acceptance of products is confirmed in the 'closing a project' process rather than during a stage.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'receive completed work package' the project manager makes sure each product has gained its requisite approval, as defined by the quality and sustainability responsibilities in its product description, then updates the product register and stage plan (see manual 16.4.3).

n.1: No such confirmation is described, and a contract sign-off does not replace the approval named in the product description.
n.2: The project board does not approve individual work packages; the approvers named in each product description do.
n.3: Closing a project confirms acceptance of the project product as a whole; individual products are approved as their work packages complete.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the build-up stage. Kezia Oduya is preparing her fortnightly highlight report in the 'report highlights' activity. Lisa Ventnor is Paceline's team manager, an events officer provides project support and Bernadette Lowe provides business assurance. According to the recommended RACI, whom should Kezia consult?
o: Lisa Ventnor, the events officer providing support and Bernadette Lowe
Andrew Mallory and the other members of the project board
Andrew Mallory, Bernadette Lowe and Inspector Ravi Sandhu
Cllr Yvonne Price and the cabinet, as the council's business layer
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'report highlights' the project manager is responsible, and the team manager, project support and project assurance are consulted (see manual 16.4.8 and table 16.2).

n.1: The board receives the highlight report; it is not consulted in preparing it.
n.2: The executive receives the report and Inspector Sandhu has no role in the project management team; the team manager and support are missing.
n.3: The business layer is not consulted on highlight reports; the board decides what is reported onwards to it.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon build-up stage is forecast to finish within its tolerances, but volunteer sign-ups are 300 behind plan. Kezia Oduya agrees an amended work package with Zara Quinn that adds three recruitment events at the city's universities, paid for from within the stage budget, and reports the action in her next highlight report. Is this an effective way to control the stage, and why?
o: Yes, because volunteer recruitment is run by the volunteering programme, outside the project's control.
Yes, because the project manager can take corrective action within stage tolerance through a work package.
No, because any shortfall against plan should be escalated to the board in an exception report.
No, because corrective actions should be approved by the board before the work package is changed.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: When evaluating stage status reveals a deviation, the project manager identifies and selects solutions within stage tolerance and triggers them through 'authorize a work package' (new or amended work packages), keeping the board informed through highlight reports (see manual 16.4.4 and 16.4.6).

n.0: Zara's programme is doing the work under a work package, so it is within the project's control; that is why the amended work package works.
n.2: Exception reports are for forecast breaches of stage or project tolerance; this stage is forecast to stay within tolerance.
n.3: Corrective action within stage tolerance is the project manager's decision; the board is told, not asked.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the build-up stage. Lisa Ventnor receives the draft work package for setting up the course, which requires every barrier and sign to be in place by 6am. Volunteers cannot reach the route before 5am because of the road closure times, so Lisa shows Kezia Oduya the work cannot be done in time, and they agree a later finish time and extra Paceline crew before Lisa accepts. Is this an appropriate application of the 'accept a work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the team manager may change a work package's constraints when they conflict with the team plan.
Yes, because the team manager agrees with the project manager what is required and whether it can be achieved.
No, because the team manager should accept the work package as issued and raise problems in checkpoint reports.
No, because the constraints in the work package were set by the project board, which would need to agree a change.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'accept a work package' the team manager agrees with the project manager what is to be delivered, the constraints and procedures, and whether the work is achievable, before agreeing to deliver it (see manual 17.4.1).

n.0: The team manager cannot change a work package alone; the change is agreed with the project manager.
n.2: Accepting work known to be unachievable would only defer the problem; the activity exists to agree an achievable work package first.
n.3: Work package constraints are agreed between the project manager and team manager; the board sets stage tolerances, not work package details.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the build-up stage. Lisa Ventnor's team has finished installing the timing mats and the results system, and Lisa is carrying out the 'notify work package completion' activity. According to the recommended RACI, which role should be informed?
o: Senior supplier
Senior user
Business layer
Project support
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In the recommended RACI for 'notify work package completion', project support is informed; the business layer, senior user and senior supplier are not involved (see manual 17.4.4 and table 17.2).

n.0: The senior supplier is not informed in this activity, even though the team is a supplier team.
n.1: The senior user is not involved in notifying work package completion.
n.2: The business layer is not involved in managing product delivery.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the build-up stage. At a safety advisory group meeting, Lisa Ventnor learns that fewer paramedics than expected will be available on race day. Without involving Kezia Oduya, she agrees with Inspector Ravi Sandhu to merge two medical posts and changes her team's plan to match. Is this an effective way to manage product delivery, and why?
o: Yes, because the safety advisory group approves the safety plan, so agreeing changes with it directly is efficient.
Yes, because the team manager manages the development of products within the work package.
No, because the team manager should tell the project manager of new risks and act as the project manager directs.
No, because Lisa should have raised an exception report with the project board about the shortage.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'execute a work package' the team manager notifies the project manager of any new issues, risks or lessons and takes the action the project manager requires (see manual 17.4.2). Changing medical cover affects the safety plan and the stage, so Kezia must assess it.

n.0: The safety advisory group approves the plan, but changes to the project's products go through the project manager's control.
n.1: The team manager manages development within the agreed work package; merging medical posts goes beyond it.
n.3: Team managers do not raise exception reports to the board; work package problems go to the project manager.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon build-up stage is nearing its end. Kezia Oduya prepares the plan for the final stage, covering event week and the six weeks after it. The plan includes the debrief, the sponsor and carbon reports, the economic impact study, and the activities to hand the event over to the events team and close the project. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare next stage plan' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the business case is updated from the stage plan before the board authorizes the final stage.
Yes, because the next stage plan is prepared near the end of this stage, and closure is planned in the final stage.
No, because closing the project should be planned as a separate stage after the economic impact study.
No, because the final stage plan should be prepared after the board has authorized the final stage.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: The plan for the next stage is produced near the end of the current stage, and closure activities are planned as part of the stage plan for the final stage; closing a project is not a stage of its own (see manual chapter 18 and 7.2.2.2).

n.0: The business case is updated using the revised project plan, but this does not explain why this stage plan is appropriate.
n.2: Closing a project is a process within the final stage, not a separate stage.
n.3: The board needs the plan to decide whether to authorize the stage, so it is prepared beforehand.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon planning and approvals stage is ending, and Kezia Oduya is preparing the end stage report in the 'evaluate the stage' activity. According to the recommended RACI, how should Lisa Ventnor, Paceline's team manager, be involved?
o: Responsible for preparing the report
Accountable for the report
Consulted on the report
Informed when it is issued
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'evaluate the stage' the project manager is responsible, and the team manager, project support and project assurance are consulted (see manual table 18.2).

n.0: The project manager is responsible for preparing the end stage report.
n.1: A team manager is not accountable for the end stage report.
n.3: The team manager is consulted while the report is prepared, not just informed afterwards.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon planning and approvals stage is ending. Entries are open and the sponsorship contract is signed, but the volunteer plan, one of the stage's products, is only half finished. Kezia Oduya moves it into the build-up stage plan and asks the board to authorize the next stage, stating that the current stage's work is complete. Is this an effective way to manage the stage boundary, and why?
o: Yes, because the next stage plan should include any work that is carried forward from the current stage.
Yes, because the volunteer plan is produced by Zara Quinn's programme, which sits outside the project.
No, because an unfinished product means an exception plan must be approved before the next stage starts.
No, because the board should be told which of the stage's products are complete and approved, and which are not.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: Managing a stage boundary assures the board that the products in the current stage plan are completed and approved, and gives it what it needs to judge continued viability (see manual 18.2). Hiding an unfinished product denies the board an accurate view before it commits to the next stage.

n.0: Carried-forward work can go in the next stage plan, but the board must be told about it rather than told the stage is complete.
n.1: The volunteer plan is one of the stage's products, so it is part of the project whoever produces it.
n.2: An exception plan follows a forecast breach of tolerance and a board request; an unfinished product is reported, not automatically treated as an exception.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'closing a project' process at the end of the final stage. Kezia Oduya confirms that the project can close, updates the project plan with actual figures, closes the project log, makes sure the project records are archived, and drafts closure messages for residents, churches, traders, volunteers and partner charities. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare planned closure' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because closing is prepared by updating the plan, closing the log, archiving records and drafting messages.
Yes, because the project manager authorizes closure of the project once its records have been archived.
No, because closure messages to stakeholders are drafted by the board after it has authorized closure.
No, because the project log should stay open until the post-project benefits reviews have been completed.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'prepare planned closure' the project manager confirms the project can close, updates the project plan with actuals, closes the project log, makes sure project information is secured and archived, and prepares closure communications (see manual 19.4.1).

n.1: The project board authorizes closure in directing a project; the project manager prepares and requests it.
n.2: Preparing closure communications is part of the project manager's preparation; the board then notifies the business layer that the project has closed.
n.3: Post-project benefits reviews happen after closure and are run by the business; the project log is closed in closing a project.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'closing a project' process. Andrew Mallory is the executive, Kezia Oduya the project manager and Greg Halloran the senior supplier. Kezia is preparing the end project report and the lessons report in the 'evaluate the project' activity. Which describes the recommended RACI for this activity?
o: Kezia responsible, the cabinet accountable, Greg informed
Andrew responsible, Kezia accountable, Greg consulted
Kezia responsible, Andrew accountable, Greg consulted
Kezia responsible and accountable, Andrew informed
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: For 'evaluate the project' the executive is accountable, the project manager responsible, the senior supplier and project assurance consulted, and the business layer not involved (see manual 19.4.4 and table 19.2).

n.0: The business layer is not involved in evaluating the project; the executive is accountable and the senior supplier is consulted.
n.1: The roles are reversed: the project manager prepares the reports and the executive is accountable.
n.3: The executive, not the project manager, is accountable, and the senior supplier is consulted.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: The Carrowford Half Marathon project is in the 'closing a project' process. The economic impact study is complete, and the council has decided to repeat the event next year as normal business. Andrew Mallory proposes keeping the project open, with Kezia Oduya and the project log, until next year's race, so that benefits from the repeat event can be measured within the project. Is this an effective way to close the project, and why?
o: Yes, because the project should stay open until all of its expected benefits have been confirmed.
Yes, because the senior user is responsible for benefits realization, so the board must stay in place to see it through.
No, because benefits cannot be measured for an event that is repeated each year as normal business.
No, because the project should close and plan post-project benefits reviews that the business carries out.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: Closing a project provides a fixed end point; benefits still to come are covered by updating the benefits management approach to plan post-project reviews, which the business carries out after closure (see manual 19.1, 19.2 and 19.4.3). Carrying out those reviews is not a project activity.

n.0: Most benefits are realized after a project closes; keeping it open adds cost and delays handover to the events team.
n.1: The senior user's responsibility for the continued realization of benefits carries on after closure, without the project board staying in place.
n.2: Benefits from repeated events can still be measured, through post-project reviews planned in the benefits management approach.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Mairi Campbell and Arjun Menon draft the wave 1 work package together over a video call. It lists the 35 applications and their product descriptions, time, cost and scope tolerances, weekly checkpoint reports, the constraint that no switch-over may take place on month-end processing days, and how each application will be handed to operations. Arjun confirms his team can deliver it before work starts. Is this an appropriate application of the 'authorize a work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because authorizing the work package allows Arjun Menon to report progress directly to the project board.
Yes, because the work package is co-created with the team manager, who confirms it can be delivered before work starts.
No, because the work package should also carry a benefits tolerance for the running cost savings.
No, because work for an external supplier should be agreed with the senior supplier rather than the team manager.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'authorize a work package' the project manager defines the work package, builds a relationship with the team manager, co-creates and reviews it with them, confirms that they accept it and then authorizes the start (see manual 16.4.1). The contents, including scope, cost and time tolerances, constraints and checkpoint frequency, fit a work package description.

n.0: The team manager reports to the project manager through checkpoint reports; the board receives highlight reports from the project manager.
n.2: A work package description carries scope, cost and time tolerances; benefits tolerance is not set at work package level.
n.3: The senior supplier commits Stratoshift's resources at board level, but work packages are agreed between the project manager and the team manager.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Arjun Menon reports that two applications in wave 2 are not ready to move. Staying within stage tolerance, Mairi Campbell swaps them with two applications from wave 3 and updates the work packages and the stage plan. Which role is accountable for the 'take corrective action' activity?
o: The executive, Fraser McIntyre.
The project manager, Mairi Campbell.
The team manager, Arjun Menon.
Project support, from the change team.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In the recommended RACI for 'take corrective action', the executive is accountable, the project manager is responsible for selecting and triggering the action within tolerance, and project support is informed (see manual 16.4.6 and table 16.2).

n.1: Mairi Campbell is responsible for taking the corrective action, but accountability sits with the executive.
n.2: The team manager carries out the changed work through the work packages; he is not accountable for the activity.
n.3: Project support is informed of corrective action, not accountable for it.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. The stage plan allows each migration wave a time tolerance of two weeks. Arjun Menon's checkpoint report forecasts that wave 1 will finish four days late because two engineers are ill, and Mairi Campbell expects to recover most of the time in the next fortnight. She immediately sends an exception report to the project board. Is this an effective way to carry out controlling a stage, and why?
o: Yes, because Fraser McIntyre asked to be told at once of any slip in a migration wave.
Yes, because later waves depend on earlier ones, so any delay to a wave should be escalated to the board.
No, because exception reports are raised by the team manager and passed to the board by the project manager.
No, because the slip is within tolerance, so she should act on it herself and report it in her highlight report.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: The project manager escalates through an exception report when stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded; a forecast deviation within tolerance is handled by corrective action in controlling a stage and reported in the highlight report (see manual 16.4.6 and 11.2.6).

n.0: Fraser McIntyre asked to be told if a wave was forecast to slip by more than two weeks, which is the tolerance; four days is within it.
n.1: The dependency between waves is real, but it is reflected in the two-week tolerance; a slip within tolerance is not an exception.
n.2: The project manager raises exception reports; a team manager raises a forecast breach of work package tolerance with the project manager as an issue.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Arjun Menon receives the draft wave 2 work package. With his team in Pune, he finds that two planned switch-over weekends fall during a major Indian festival when most of the engineers are on leave. He agrees new dates with Mairi Campbell that avoid the society's month-end days, then accepts the work package and prepares a team plan. Is this an appropriate application of the 'accept a work package' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because the team manager agrees with the project manager what is to be delivered and that it is achievable.
Yes, because accepting the work package allows the team manager to set new tolerances for the work package.
No, because the team manager should accept the work package as issued and raise any problems later as issues.
No, because a team plan for a work package has to be approved by the project board before work starts.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'accept a work package' the team manager agrees with the project manager what is to be delivered, the constraints, reporting and procedures, and whether the work is achievable, then agrees to deliver it, producing a team plan if needed (see manual 17.4.1).

n.1: Work package tolerances are set by the project manager; the team manager agrees to deliver within them.
n.2: Accepting a work package includes checking that it is achievable and agreeing changes before accepting; known problems should be resolved first.
n.3: Team plans are optional and produced by the team manager; the project board does not approve them.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Arjun Menon's team is migrating the wave 2 applications, updating the quality register as each test is passed and notifying Mairi Campbell of new risks. Which role is accountable for the 'execute a work package' activity?
o: The senior supplier, Lena Fischer, who commits Stratoshift's people.
The team manager, Arjun Menon, who leads the engineers doing the work.
The executive, Fraser McIntyre, who is accountable for the whole project.
The project manager, Mairi Campbell, who authorized the work package.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In the recommended RACI for 'execute a work package', the project manager is accountable and project assurance is consulted; the business layer and executive are not involved (see manual 17.4.2 and table 17.2).

n.0: The senior supplier is accountable for the quality of supplier products at board level, but the board is not involved in managing product delivery.
n.1: The team manager carries out the work package; accountability for the activity sits with the project manager.
n.2: The executive is not involved in executing a work package.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. Lena Fischer, who sits on the project board as senior supplier, phones Arjun Menon and tells him to move three engineers to another Stratoshift client for two weeks, delaying part of the wave 2 work package. Arjun does so and mentions it in his next checkpoint report. Is this an effective way to carry out managing product delivery, and why?
o: Yes, because the senior supplier commits Stratoshift's people and can decide where its engineers work.
Yes, because the delay was reported to the project manager in the team manager's next checkpoint report.
No, because the team manager takes instructions on the work package from the project manager, not from a board member.
No, because instructions to a team manager should come from the executive as the single point of accountability.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In managing product delivery the team manager works to the work package agreed with the project manager, notifies the project manager of issues and takes any action required by the project manager, not instructions directly from the board (see manual 17.4.2). Lena should raise the resourcing problem with Mairi.

n.0: The senior supplier commits supplier resources at board level, but changing an authorized work package should go through the project manager.
n.1: Reporting the change afterwards does not make it acceptable; the project manager should decide before the work package is changed.
n.3: Neither the executive nor other board members instruct team managers; direction flows from the board to the project manager.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Project Skyline is in the wave migration stage. After Mairi Campbell's exception report about wave 3 slipping into the December change freeze, the board asks for an exception plan. Mairi records the request in the project log and prepares a plan from the current position to the end of the stage, then updates the project plan and business case to reflect it. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare exception plan' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because Mairi can approve the exception plan herself while the project stays within project tolerance.
Yes, because the plan replaces the stage plan from the current position, and the effect on the project is assessed.
No, because an exception plan is prepared in controlling a stage as part of escalating issues and risks.
No, because the exception plan should replace Arjun Menon's team plan rather than the stage plan.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: When the board asks for an exception plan, the project manager records the request, prepares a plan from the current position to the end of the stage to replace the stage plan, and reviews and updates the project plan and business case (see manual chapter 18, 'prepare exception plan').

n.0: The project board approves a stage-level exception plan; the project manager cannot approve her own plan.
n.2: The exception report is raised in controlling a stage; the exception plan itself is prepared in managing a stage boundary.
n.3: Exception plans replace stage or project plans; they are not produced for team plans.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Project Skyline is at the end of the wave migration stage. Mairi Campbell reviews how the Pune engineers and Hugh Bannerman's operations staff have worked together, including fatigue after repeated switch-over weekends, and records lessons on team health and well-being for the end stage report. Which practice is being applied by the managing a stage boundary process, and why?
o: Progress, because the stage's actual costs and dates are compared with those in the stage plan.
Organizing, because team performance, health and well-being are reviewed to inform lessons and the report.
Quality, because the quality register is checked to confirm the stage's quality activities were completed.
Issues, because the fatigue of the teams should be recorded and assessed as a formal issue.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In managing a stage boundary the organizing practice is applied by reviewing the project team's performance, health and well-being, feeding lessons and the end stage report (see manual chapter 18, table 18.3).

n.0: Comparing costs and dates with the plan is not what Mairi is doing; she is reviewing how the teams worked together and their well-being.
n.2: Checking the quality register is how the quality practice is applied at a stage boundary; this review is about the people.
n.3: Nothing is said about raising an issue; the review gathers lessons on team health for the report.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Project Skyline is at the end of the foundations stage. Mairi Campbell sends the board the wave migration stage plan and the updated business case, but no end stage report. She says the fortnightly highlight reports have already told the board how the foundations stage went. Is this an effective way to carry out managing a stage boundary, and why?
o: Yes, because highlight reports are time-driven controls that already cover the status of the stage for the board.
Yes, because an end stage report is needed when an exception plan is being presented to the board.
No, because the end stage report should be written by project assurance for the board to review.
No, because the board needs the end stage report to review how the stage performed before deciding.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'evaluate the stage' the project manager prepares the end stage report, which gives the board the information it needs to review the stage just ending and decide what to do next; it is an event-driven control at the stage boundary (see manual chapter 18 and 11.2.2).

n.0: Highlight reports give periodic status during the stage; the stage-end decision is supported by the end stage report.
n.1: It is the other way round: an end stage report is always prepared at a stage end, and with an exception plan it is needed only if the board asks for one.
n.2: The project manager is responsible for the end stage report; project assurance is consulted.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Project Skyline is in the decommissioning stage and approaching closure. Mairi Campbell confirms that all products have been delivered, including certificates confirming that member data on the old hardware was destroyed. She updates the project plan with actual figures, closes the project log, archives the project records in line with the digital and data management approach and prepares closure messages for staff and suppliers. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare planned closure' activity, and why?
o: Yes, because it confirms the project can close, updates the plan with actuals and secures the project's records.
Yes, because closing the project log also completes the post-project benefits reviews for the business.
No, because closure activities should be planned as a separate stage that follows decommissioning.
No, because project records should be destroyed once the products have been handed over to operations.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In 'prepare planned closure' the project manager confirms the project is ready to close, updates the project plan with actuals, closes the project log, makes sure project information is secured and archived, and prepares closure communications (see manual 19.4.1).

n.1: Post-project benefits reviews are planned during closure and carried out by the business after the project ends.
n.2: Closing a project is part of the final stage; closure is never planned as a stage of its own.
n.3: Project information is secured and archived so that it can be used later, for example in audits and benefits reviews.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Project Skyline is in the 'closing a project' process. Mairi Campbell works through the product register, confirming that each product, including every migrated application and each disposal certificate, is complete or has a follow-on action, and then closes the register. Which practice is being applied by the closing a project process, and why?
o: Quality, because the product register records whether each product passed its quality checks.
Issues, because any product that is not complete has to be raised as an off-specification.
Plans, because the product register is checked and closed to confirm the products of the plan.
Progress, because the product register is used to compare actual progress with the stage plan.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: In closing a project the plans practice is applied by checking and closing the product register, which lists all the products of the plan and their status (see manual chapter 19, table 19.3).

n.0: Quality checks and their results are recorded in the quality register; the product register lists the products and their status.
n.1: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its quality specification; an incomplete product with a follow-on action is not necessarily one.
n.3: The product register is not being used to track progress against the stage plan; it is being checked and closed.

Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.q: Project Skyline is in the decommissioning stage. The £1.4 million yearly saving will not appear until year three, well after both data centres have closed. Mairi Campbell proposes keeping the project open, with herself as project manager, until the saving can be measured, so that the board can confirm the benefit before closing. Is this an effective way to carry out closing a project, and why?
o: Yes, because the executive stays accountable for the business case until all of the benefits have been realized.
Yes, because confirming benefits is one of the steps of the business case technique in PRINCE2 7.
No, because later benefits should be measured in post-project reviews planned in the benefits management approach.
No, because benefits stop being measured once the products have been handed over to operations.
Practitioner: Controlling, Delivering &.w: A project should have a clear end rather than drift on; benefits that arise after closure are assessed in post-project benefits reviews, which closing a project plans by updating the benefits management approach and which the business carries out (see manual 19.2, 19.3 and 5.3.1).

n.0: Whoever is accountable for the business case, the project should close once its products are accepted; later benefits are confirmed in post-project reviews, and the senior user remains responsible for their realization after closure.
n.1: Confirming benefits is a step of the technique, but it mostly happens after closure, so it does not justify keeping the project open.
n.3: Benefits continue to be measured after handover, through post-project reviews carried out by the business.
